Título: An autonomous mobile robot with functions of action learning, memorizing, recall and identifying the environment using Gaussian mixture model
Tarea: Identificar el entorno y aprender acciones en diferentes entornos.
Algoritmo (texto): Q-learning, un método de aprendizaje por refuerzo, y redes neuronales caóticas (CNNs) y modelos de mezcla gaussiana (GMM).
Observaciones: Percepciones del entorno en cinco direcciones a una cuadrícula de distancia.
Acciones: Acciones discretas (adelante, izquierda, derecha).
Recompensa: No se especifica explícitamente, pero se infiere que se basa en la identificación correcta del entorno y la realización de acciones óptimas.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona la realización de 30 pruebas con 5 acciones cada una.
Líneas base: SOM retroalimentada
Resultado: El método propuesto logró una tasa de discriminación del 71.40% en comparación con el 65.20% del método convencional.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que el método podría confundir entornos similares, lo que afecta la tasa de discriminación.

Título: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
Tarea: highly challenging 3D locomotion tasks, learning running gaits for bipedal and quadrupedal simulated robots, and learning a policy for getting the biped to stand up from starting out lying on the ground
Algoritmo (texto): generalized advantage estimation (GAE), a family of policy gradient estimators that significantly reduce variance while maintaining a tolerable level of bias, with a trust region optimization procedure for both the policy and the value function, represented by neural networks
Observaciones: raw kinematics to joint torques
Acciones: torque-level control, continuous
Recompensa: not stated, but the expected total reward is maximized
Entrenamiento: 1-2 weeks of real time for 3D bipeds, not specified for other tasks
Líneas base: classical and RL
Resultado: learned complex gaits using high-dimensional, general purpose neural network function approximators for both the policy and the value function, each with over 104 parameters
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Learning deep control policies for autonomous aerial vehicles with MPC-guided policy search
Tarea: learn obstacle avoidance policies for a simulated quadrotor.
Algoritmo (texto): MPC-guided policy search, using DDP-like algorithms for trajectory optimization.
Algoritmo (diccionario): Guided Policy Search; MPC / NMPC; Policy search (PGPE, PoWER, gSDE)
Observaciones: raw observations from the vehicle’s onboard sensors, such as IMU readings and data from laser range finders
Acciones: continuous, as implied by the use of neural networks
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: simulated quadrotor with simulated laser range sensors
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: guided policy search with offline trajectory optimization; MPC
Resultado: Our approach can learn policies that are robust to a variety of perturbations and generalize successfully to large obstacle courses, without catastrophic failure during training.
Limitaciones: The method relies on an approximate model of the system dynamics, which may not be perfectly accurate.

Título: A Joint Learning Framework of Visual Sensory Representation, Eye Movements and Depth Representation for Developmental Robotic Agents
Tarea: autonomously perceive depths by simultaneously developing its visual sensory representation, eye movement control, and depth representation knowledge through integrating multiple visual depth cues during self-induced lateral body movement.
Algoritmo (texto): sparse coding and reinforcement learning, tightly coupled with a unified cost function
Observaciones: two images from the dominant eye and two eyes for stereo disparity
Acciones: multiple eye motor control signals, discrete (pan/vergence angles)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: 30 iterations, 100 different images, not stated hardware
Métricas: mean absolute error (MAE) for eye movements; MAE of depth perception
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: the framework could jointly learn to improve the sensory encoding and represent the visual stimuli while learning to generate multiple eye motor control with depth perception, with MAE of eye movements and depth perception decreasing over time
Limitaciones: the framework is tested in simulation and not in the real robot, and the dominant eye may be competitively selected during the learning period

Título: Deep reinforcement learning with successor features for navigation across similar environments
Tarea: navigation in simple maze-like environments
Algoritmo (texto): successor feature-based deep reinforcement learning (SF-RL)
Observaciones: visual and depth inputs from a forward-facing camera or on-board Kinect sensor
Acciones: discrete actions (stand still, turn left, turn right, go straight)
Recompensa: −0.04 for each step, −0.96 for colliding with obstacles, 1 for reaching the goal
Simulador: simulated Pioneer-3dx robot in 3D maze-like environments
Entrenamiento: 30,000 steps for supervised learning, 200,000 steps for SF-RL and DQN, hardware not stated
Métricas: average reward; success ratio; number of steps
Líneas base: supervised learning; DQN; DQN-FixFeature; DQN-Finetune; SF-RL; SF-RL-Transfer
Sim2real: transfer learning from simulated to real Robotino
Resultado: SF-RL-Transfer converges to performance comparable to the optimal policy much faster than training from scratch, and the agent is still able to perform well on the old task after the transfer.
Limitaciones: The method requires a large number of steps for training, and the transfer learning from simulated to real environment is not always successful.

Título: Deep visual foresight for planning robot motion
Tarea: pushing objects to desired locations
Algoritmo (texto): model-predictive control (MPC) based on probabilistic inference through a learned predictive image model
Observaciones: RGB camera images, current and previous end-effector poses, and a sequence of future commands
Acciones: continuous actions, discrete commands
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: 50,000 pushing attempts, 10 7-DoF arms, 10 Hz sensor readings, 5 Hz commanded pose updates
Métricas: mean distance between final and goal pixel positions
Líneas base: random actions; move end-effector to goal; move end-effector along vector (with replanning); visual MPC (ours)
Resultado: Our method outperforms simple baselines based on geometric heuristics and known hand-to-camera calibration, with a mean pixel distance of 2.52±1.06 compared to 3.19±1.68 for the best baseline.
Limitaciones: The method is limited to relatively simple short-horizon tasks and is sensitive to self-occlusions and incorrect model predictions.

Título: Meta Learning Shared Hierarchies
Tarea: The agent learns to solve a distribution of related tasks, such as maze navigation and obstacle courses, with the goal of quickly learning new tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): Meta Learning Shared Hierarchies (MLSH), which uses any off-the-shelf reinforcement learning method.
Observaciones: The agent observes state variables (s) and takes actions (a) based on these observations.
Acciones: Discrete actions, as the algorithm uses a stochastic policy.
Recompensa: The reward is defined as the total return R = r0 + r1 + ... + rT-1 over T timesteps, with the goal of maximizing the expected return during an agent's entire lifetime over the sampled tasks.
Simulador: 2D continuous movement, gridworld navigation, and 3D physics tasks involving the directional movement of robots.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the algorithm iteratively performs update steps which can be broken into a warmup period and a joint update period.
Métricas: Expected return during an agent's entire lifetime over the sampled tasks
Líneas base: Previous work in hierarchical reinforcement learning; Metalearning approaches
Resultado: The method is capable of learning meaningful sub-policies solely through interaction with a distribution of tasks, outperforming previously proposed algorithms. 3D humanoid robots can robustly walk and crawl with the same policy, and 4-legged robots can discover directional movement primitives to solve a distribution of mazes as well as sparse-reward obstacle courses.
Limitaciones: The method assumes a constant set of sub-policies during the warmup period, which may limit its flexibility.

Título: Reinforcement learning with deep energy-based policies
Tarea: learn stochastic policies for continuous states and actions, particularly for exploration in multimodal reward landscapes and compositionality in reinforcement learning tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): soft Q-learning, based on actor-critic methods and energy-based models
Robot: swimming snake (simulated), not stated for other tasks
Observaciones: state and action space, specifically the state is the 2D position and action is 2D velocity
Acciones: continuous 2D velocity actions, discrete for the swimming snake
Recompensa: defined as a mixture of Gaussians for the multi-goal environment, speed along the x-axis for the swimming snake, not stated for other tasks
Simulador: simulated environments, specifically a 2D multi-goal environment and a simulated swimming snake
Entrenamiento: not stated, but the method is compared to DDPG which uses a training budget of 10 million time steps
Métricas: performance in multi-goal environment; performance in simulated swimming snake
Líneas base: DDPG
Resultado: The method outperformed DDPG in the multi-goal environment, achieving better exploration performance and learning diverse trajectories that lead to all goals, while DDPG randomly commits to a single goal.
Limitaciones: The method is focused on high-dimensional continuous spaces and highly multimodal objectives, but it is not clear if it can handle very complex tasks or if it scales well to large state and action spaces.

Título: Socially aware motion planning with deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: Navegar de forma autónoma en un entorno con muchos peatones, respetando normas sociales.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (CADRL) con una red neuronal simétrica para múltiples agentes.
Observaciones: Posición, velocidad, tamaño y objetivo del agente (posición, velocidad preferida, orientación)
Acciones: Velocidad, acciones discretas
Recompensa: Se define a través de una función de recompensa que recompensa el llegar al objetivo y penaliza las colisiones, con un enfoque en minimizar el tiempo de llegada.
Simulador: Simulaciones con casos de prueba simétricos y no simétricos
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se entrenaron tres copias de cuatro agentes.
Métricas: Tiempo extra para alcanzar el objetivo; Distancia mínima de separación; Preferencia de norma (porcentaje izquierda/derecha)
Líneas base: ORCA; CADRL; SA-CADRL sin norma; SA-CADRL con norma izquierda; SA-CADRL con norma derecha
Sim2real: Transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a hardware real.
Resultado: El SA-CADRL con norma derecha (SA-CADRL(rh)) produjo un tiempo extra para alcanzar el objetivo de 0.31 a 0.69 segundos, una distancia mínima de separación de 0.155 a 0.180 metros y una preferencia de norma del 12% a 88% a favor de la norma derecha, mientras que ORCA tuvo un tiempo extra para alcanzar el objetivo de 0.86 a 1.80 segundos, una distancia mínima de separación de 0.106 a 0.125 metros y una preferencia de norma del 46% a 54%.
Limitaciones: El SA-CADRL no siempre responde de manera consistente con las normas sociales humanas, ya que muestra preferencias mixtas entre reglas derechas e izquierdas.

Título: Uncertainty-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Collision Avoidance
Tarea: Navegar en un entorno desconocido evitando colisiones.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning basado en un modelo con estimación de incertidumbre.
Observaciones: Imágenes de cámaras (16x16 y 32x18 en escala de grises)
Acciones: Velocidad y dirección de giro (acciones discretas)
Recompensa: Costo que incluye un término para la tarea y otro para las colisiones, donde el costo de las colisiones depende de su velocidad.
Simulador: Simulaciones con obstáculos y un entorno real con un obstáculo único
Entrenamiento: 20 iteraciones con 20 rollouts por iteración en simulaciones, 5 iteraciones con 5 rollouts por iteración en el RC car
Líneas base: Modelo basado en un modelo sin considerar la incertidumbre; Controlador de seguridad conservador
Sim2real: Transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a la realidad
Resultado: El robot experimenta colisiones más lentas y menos frecuentes en la simulación y en el RC car, lo que permite mejorar la eficiencia de aprendizaje y la seguridad.
Limitaciones: El método requiere un número significativo de iteraciones y rollouts para aprender a navegar eficientemente, lo que puede ser un desafío en entornos complejos.

Título: The landmark detection method using surf and q-learning for an autonomous mobile robot
Virtual-to-real deep reinforcement learning: Continuous control of mobile robots for mapless navigation
Tarea: Navegar un robot móvil noholonómico al objetivo sin colisionar con obstáculos, utilizando solo información de rango escasa y la posición relativa del objetivo.
Algoritmo (texto): Asíncrono Deep Reinforcement Learning (deep-RL)
Observaciones: 10-dimensional range findings, 2-dimensional previous velocity, 2-dimensional relative target position
Acciones: Continuous steering commands
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the planner is trained to avoid obstacles and reach the target position.
Simulador: Virtual environment based on sparse 10-dimensional range findings, 2-dimensional previous velocity, and 2-dimensional relative target position.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions the training process.
Líneas base: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
Resultado: The proposed mapless motion planner was trained in a virtual environment and successfully navigated a nonholonomic differential drive robot to the target position without colliding with any obstacles.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a highly abstracted observation input, which may limit its performance in real-world scenarios with more complex environments.

Título: Data-efficient hierarchical reinforcement learning
Tarea: The agent learns to perform complex behaviors such as pushing objects and utilizing them to reach target locations in simulated robots.
Algoritmo (texto): HIRO (HIerarchical Reinforcement learning with Off-policy correction), based on TD3 (a variant of DDPG for continuous control).
Observaciones: Position and orientation of the agent and its limbs (state observations).
Acciones: Continuous actions, discrete goals for the lower-level policy.
Recompensa: The agent is rewarded for approaching the target location and for performing actions that yield state observations close to the desired goal.
Simulador: Simulated environments for Ant Gather, Ant Maze, Ant Push, and Ant Fall tasks.
Entrenamiento: Trained using off-policy experience, with a few million environment steps (equivalent to a few days of real-time interaction).
Líneas base: FeUdal Networks (FuN); stochastic neural networks for HRL (SNN4HRL); Variational Information Maximizing Exploration (VIME); Option-Critic Architecture
Resultado: HIRO can learn complex behaviors for simulated robots, such as pushing objects and utilizing them to reach target locations, in only a few million samples, equivalent to a few days of real-time interaction. It outperforms previous state-of-the-art techniques.
Limitaciones: The results are still far from perfect, and there is much work left for future research to improve the stability and performance of HRL methods on these tasks.

Título: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Action Control
Tarea: Learn basic skills and compound skills simultaneously for robotic control in a continuous action space.
Algoritmo (texto): Hierarchical Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (h-DDPG) based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)
Observaciones: Sensor data and first-person view camera images
Acciones: Continuous actions, discrete for basic skills, continuous for compound skills
Recompensa: Defined as the expected future return, with a discounted factor, and based on the performance of the robot in the navigation scenarios
Simulador: Gazebo 2 in a ROS Indigo environment
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Discrete action space deep reinforcement learning algorithm
Resultado: The proposed algorithm can learn both high performance basic skills and compound skills, and its performance in solving compound tasks outperforms the discrete action deep reinforcement learning algorithm.
Limitaciones: The method requires explicitly defined rewards for both levels of hierarchy, and the basic tasks learned at the lowest-level of hierarchy are non-task specific.

Título: Improving exploration in evolution strategies for deep reinforcement learning via a population of novelty-seeking agents
Tarea: learn to walk in a simulated humanoid environment and play Atari games
Algoritmo (texto): Evolution Strategies (ES) hybridized with novelty search (NS) and quality diversity (QD) algorithms
Observaciones: agent's final {x,y} location, RAM states
Acciones: continuous actions for locomotion, discrete actions for Atari games
Recompensa: distance traveled in the positive x direction for humanoid locomotion, reward from Atari games
Simulador: OpenAI Gym's Humanoid-v1 environment, Atari 2600 environment
Entrenamiento: 600 generations, not stated for Atari
Métricas: median reward per generation; performance on Atari games
Líneas base: Evolution Strategies (ES); Noisy DQN; A3C+
Resultado: NSRA-ES outperforms ES and other methods on both the humanoid locomotion and Atari games, achieving higher median rewards in 8/12 games and 9/12 games respectively.
Limitaciones: The BC distance is not normalized by trajectory length, which can lead to biases in novelty. The BC design may need further investigation for different tasks.

Título: Meta-reinforcement learning of structured exploration strategies
Tarea: learn exploration strategies for complex tasks in reinforcement learning, particularly for robots performing manipulation and locomotion tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): model agnostic exploration with structured noise (MAESN), a gradient-based meta-learning algorithm
Observaciones: state space, action space, and latent exploration space
Acciones: discrete or continuous, with structured stochasticity
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: MAML (Finn et al., 2017a); RNN-based algorithms (Duan et al., 2016b; Wang et al., 2016)
Resultado: MAESN substantially outperforms prior meta-learning methods in learning exploration strategies and adapting quickly to new tasks.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Overcoming Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Demonstrations
Tarea: stacking blocks at a given location from a random initial state
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) and a demonstration buffer
Observaciones: state variables (positions of blocks, target positions)
Acciones: continuous control actions (robot arm movements)
Recompensa: not stated, but implies sparse rewards
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: initialization with learning from demonstrations; fine-tuning with RL
Resultado: our method significantly outperforms initialization with learning from demonstrations and fine-tuning with RL
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Motion Planning among Dynamic, Decision-Making Agents with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Navegar entre peatones evitando colisiones
Algoritmo (texto): A3C (Actor-Critic) con LSTM, basado en aprendizaje por refuerzo
Observaciones: Posición, velocidad y radio del agente; posición, velocidad y orientación preferida del otro agente
Acciones: Velocidad y ángulo de dirección, discretas
Recompensa: 1 si llega al objetivo, -0.25 si hay una distancia mínima < 0, -0.1 + 0.05 si hay colisión
Entrenamiento: 1.2 millones de episodios en 12 horas en una GPU NVIDIA GTX1060
Métricas: Porcentaje de colisiones; Porcentaje de agente que no llega al objetivo; Tiempo extra a la meta promedio
Líneas base: SA-CADRL
Resultado: El nuevo algoritmo GA3C-CADRL-10 se desempeña comparativamente bien con SA-CADRL en escenarios con hasta 4 agentes, pero mejora ligeramente en entornos con más de 4 agentes.
Limitaciones: El algoritmo requiere un tiempo de entrenamiento más largo y una tasa de aprendizaje más baja para la estabilidad, y aún puede haber colisiones después de la convergencia debido a la selección aleatoria de acciones durante el entrenamiento.

Título: PRM-RL: Long-range robotic navigation tasks by combining reinforcement learning and sampling-based planning
Tarea: end-to-end differential drive indoor navigation in office environments and aerial cargo delivery in urban environments with load displacement constraints.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Continuous Action Fitted Value Iteration (CAFVI)
Robot: differential drive robot, quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)
Observaciones: LIDAR observations for the differential drive robot, joint position-velocity vector for the quadrotor and load
Acciones: continuous actions for both robots
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: simulator with noisy sensors and dynamics for indoor navigation, simulated urban environment for aerial cargo delivery
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: traditional sampling-based planners, RL agents on their own
Resultado: PRM-RL successfully completes up to 215 m long trajectories under noisy sensor conditions in indoor navigation and completes flights over 1000 m without violating task constraints in an environment 63 million times larger than used in training for aerial cargo delivery.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Self-Supervised Deep Reinforcement Learning with Generalized Computation Graphs for Robot Navigation
Tarea: learn collision avoidance policies for mobile robots
Algoritmo (texto): generalized computation graph that subsumes value-based model-free methods and model-based methods
Observaciones: raw monocular camera images
Acciones: continuous actions
Recompensa: reward for collision-free navigation
Entrenamiento: 4 hours of fully autonomous reinforcement learning
Líneas base: single-step and N-step double Q-learning
Resultado: our approach can learn a successful navigation policy on an RC car in a real-world, indoor environment from scratch using raw monocular images in 4 hours of fully autonomous, self-supervised training
Limitaciones: the approach is limited by the sample complexity and the need for continuous learning, as well as the high-dimensional state space when learning from raw images

Título: Sim-to-Real: Learning Agile Locomotion For Quadruped Robots
Tarea: learn quadruped locomotion gaits (trotting and galloping) from scratch using reinforcement learning.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: roll, pitch, angular velocities of the base, and motor angles
Acciones: desired pose of each leg in the leg space (swing and extension components)
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: PyBullet with a physics simulator that includes a faithful actuator model and latency handling
Entrenamiento: 4.35 and 3.25 hours for trotting and galloping respectively
Líneas base: none
Sim2real: improving the physics simulator and learning robust policies
Resultado: After learning in simulation, a quadruped robot can successfully perform both trotting and galloping in the real world.
Limitaciones: The reality gap is challenging to overcome, and the transfer of policies from simulation to the real world is not always successful.

Título: Soft Actor-Critic Algorithms and Applications
Tarea: learn walking gaits and robotic manipulation tasks
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), based on maximum entropy RL framework
Observaciones: motor angles, roll and pitch angles, angular velocities, RGB images
Acciones: swing angle and extension of each leg, joint angle positions for the hand
Recompensa: rewards large forward velocity, penalizes large angular accelerations, large pitch angles, and extending front legs under the robot
Simulador: OpenAI gym benchmark suite, rllab implementation of the Humanoid task
Entrenamiento: 500 steps per episode, 160k environment steps, 2 hours of real-world training time
Líneas base: DDPG; PPO; TD3; SQL
Resultado: SAC outperforms baseline methods on harder tasks with a large margin, learning to walk from 160k environment steps, and learning dexterous hand manipulation tasks from raw RGB images in 20 hours
Limitaciones: challenges for real-world reinforcement learning due to underactuation and perception difficulties

Título: Towards optimally decentralized multi-robot collision avoidance via deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: Learn a collision-avoidance policy for multiple nonholonomic mobile robots to navigate to their goal positions without collisions in rich and complex environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Policy gradient based reinforcement learning
Observaciones: raw 2D laser measurements, relative goal position, and current velocity
Acciones: continuous velocity commands
Recompensa: A reward function that penalizes collisions and encourages reaching the goal and smooth movement
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: centralized methods; ORCA and its extensions; previous decentralized methods
Resultado: The learned policy is able to find time efficient, collision-free paths for a large-scale nonholonomic robot system and can be well generalized to unseen scenarios, outperforming previous decentralized methods.
Limitaciones: The method assumes perfect sensing in the training environment, which may not hold in real-world scenarios.

Título: Vision-and-Language Navigation: Interpreting Visually-Grounded Navigation Instructions in Real Environments
Tarea: Seguir instrucciones naturales en un entorno 3D real para navegar a un lugar específico.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) con un espacio de acciones basado en grafos de puntos panorámicos.
Observaciones: Imágenes RGB panorámicas y poses 3D del agente (posición, orientación, elevación de la cámara).
Acciones: Cambiar la vista panorámica (posición 3D, orientación, elevación de la cámara), acciones determinísticas.
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: Matterport3D Simulator, basado en el conjunto de datos Matterport3D.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: Precisión en la navegación a un objetivo específico
Líneas base: Básicos de RL; Modelos de secuencia a secuencia
Resultado: Los agentes basados en secuencias a secuencia lograron un rendimiento significativo en la tarea de navegación según instrucciones naturales, estableciendo varios baselines.
Limitaciones: El conjunto de datos está sesgado hacia espacios de vida limpios y ordenados, con pocos objetos personales y poca diversidad de personas y animales.

Título: Continuous control for robot based on deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: Continuous control for a robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with DDPG (Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient) as the main algorithm.
Observaciones: not stated
Acciones: Continuous actions.
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: not stated
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: End-to-End Robotic Reinforcement Learning without Reward Engineering
Tarea: arrange objects, place books, and drape cloth
Algoritmo (texto): maximum entropy RL with Soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm, combined with active queries and classiﬁer-based rewards
Observaciones: images viewed by the robot’s camera
Acciones: discrete actions for end-effector motion
Recompensa: log probability of success given the state, derived from a binary classiﬁer trained on goal and non-goal observations
Entrenamiento: 1-4 hours of interaction with the real world
Líneas base: standard reinforcement learning; inverse reinforcement learning; classiﬁer-based reinforcement learning
Resultado: our method effectively learns to arrange objects, place books, and drape cloth, directly from images and without any manually speciﬁed reward functions, and with only 1-4 hours of interaction with the real world
Limitaciones: the method requires a small number of positive outcome examples and binary queries from the user, and the success probability of the classiﬁer can be exploited by the RL algorithm

Título: Exploring to learn visual saliency: The RL-IAC approach
Tarea: learn a model of visual saliency directly on a robot to enhance object localization and recognition.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning-Intelligent Adaptive Curiosity (RL-IAC), based on Intelligent Adaptive Curiosity (IAC).
Observaciones: RGB-D input, depth segmentation, feature maps, object segmentation, superpixels, saliency map, bounding boxes.
Acciones: displacements in the environment, based on the navigation graph.
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: saliency maps accuracy; bounding box proposals quality
Líneas base: classical saliency techniques; CNN-based saliency methods; traditional object detection methods
Resultado: The saliency model learned directly on the robot outperforms several state-of-the-art saliency techniques, and RL-IAC can drastically decrease the required time for learning a reliable saliency model.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a depth-based object detector and assumes the availability of a SLAM algorithm for region definition.

Título: Learning Navigation Behaviors End-to-End with AutoRL
Tarea: Learn end-to-end point-to-point and path-following navigation behaviors that avoid moving obstacles.
Algoritmo (texto): AutoRL, an evolutionary automation layer around reinforcement learning (RL) that searches for a deep RL reward and neural network architecture with large-scale hyper-parameter optimization.
Robot: a poi (a simulated differential drive robot)
Observaciones: noisy lidar observations
Acciones: robot linear and angular velocities, continuous
Recompensa: The reward is defined as a parameterized atomic reward that provides more timely feedback to aid learning, and it is used to maximize the probability of reaching the true objective and the cumulative reward.
Simulador: generated from a real building floor plan
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: baseline policies
Resultado: AutoRL policies are 23% and 26% more successful than baseline policies across new environments.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that reward shaping is well understood for some areas (e.g., video games) but remains a black art for most tasks, including navigation. Similarly, selection of neural network architecture often consists of trial and error, and remains another source of training difficulties.

Título: Learning agile and dynamic motor skills for legged robots
Tarea: learn agile and dynamic motor skills for legged robots
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with actor-critic method, using a multi-layer perceptron as the policy network
Observaciones: history of the robot's states
Acciones: joint position targets, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: hybrid simulator combining rigid-body simulation and actuator nets
Entrenamiento: 11 hours on a personal computer with one CPU and one GPU
Líneas base: classical and RL
Resultado: ANYmal is capable of precisely and energy-efficiently following high-level body velocity commands, running faster than ever before, and recovering from falling even in complex configurations
Limitaciones: the method is limited by the reality gap between simulation and real systems, and the accuracy of the actuator models

Título: Learning to Walk Via Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Learn walking gaits for a quadruped robot directly in the real world without relying on any model or simulation.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with automated temperature adjustment
Observaciones: Joint angles, IMU readings, and desired motor positions
Acciones: Continuous, determined by neural network policy
Recompensa: Bounded reward based on the robot's position measured by a motion capture system
Entrenamiento: About 400 rollouts, equating to about two hours of real-world time
Líneas base: Prior works based on maximum entropy RL
Resultado: The algorithm can learn a stable gait in about two hours of real-world time and achieve state-of-the-art performance on simulated benchmark tasks with a single set of hyperparameters.
Limitaciones: The method is sensitive to the scale of the reward function, and the temperature parameter needs to be tuned per environment.

Título: PRIMAL: Pathfinding via Reinforcement and Imitation Multi-Agent Learning
Tarea: Pathfinding for multiple robots in a partially-observable environment.
Algoritmo (texto): Asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C) algorithm, with imitation learning (IL) from an expert planner.
Observaciones: Limited field of view (FOV) centered around the agent, including obstacle positions, positions of other agents, and goal positions.
Acciones: Discrete actions (move in one of four cardinal directions or stay still).
Recompensa: Agents are penalized for not reaching their goals, slightly more for staying still than moving; agent collisions result in a -2 reward; +20 reward for finishing an episode when all agents are on their goals.
Simulador: Hybrid simulation of a factory mockup involving both real-world and simulated robots.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: state-of-the-art MAPF planners
Resultado: The learned policies outperformed state-of-the-art MAPF planners in terms of success rates in a hybrid simulation involving both real-world and simulated robots.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a partially-observable environment and may struggle in fully-observable or cluttered factory environments.

Título: RL-RRT: Kinodynamic Motion Planning via Learning Reachability Estimators from RL Policies
Tarea: learn an obstacle-avoiding policy and a reachability estimator for kinodynamic motion planning.
Algoritmo (texto): AutoRL (a variant of DDPG) for learning the local planner, and a supervised reachability estimator for predicting time to reach between states.
Robot: Asteroid robot; Differential Drive robot; Car-like robot
Observaciones: noisy robot lidar, relative goal position, robot velocity
Acciones: continuous actions (forward thrust and turn rate)
Recompensa: a parameterized reward function that includes goal reaching, collision avoidance, and clearance from obstacles
Simulador: simulated depth measurements (e.g., lidar) around the robot
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: percentage of goal states identified as reachable; path finish time
Líneas base: SST [14]
Sim2real: transfer learning from simulation to a physical differential drive robot
Resultado: RL-RRT is up to 2.3 times more likely to identify a path within a fixed time budget and the identified path is up to 4.5 times shorter compared to SST [14].
Limitaciones: RL policies often lack long-term planning capabilities and can get trapped in environments with complex obstacles.

Título: Reinforcement learning for UAV attitude control
Tarea: el control de actitud de un Iris quadcopter
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Gradient Policy (DDGP), Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: velocidad angular de cada eje, velocidad angular de cada rotor
Acciones: control signals para cada motor, acciones continuas
Recompensa: no se especifica directamente, pero se menciona que se utiliza un reward para maximizar la recompensa a lo largo del tiempo
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un número específico de pasos, episodios o horas, pero se menciona que se utilizan episodios
Líneas base: PID controller
Resultado: controllers trained using PPO outperform PID control and are capable of exceptional performance
Limitaciones: se menciona que hay un gap entre la simulación y la realidad, pero no se especifican más detalles

Título: DeepGait: Planning and Control of Quadrupedal Gaits Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Planning and executing sequences of footholds for quadrupedal locomotion in rigid non-flat terrain using proprioceptive and exteroceptive sensing.
Algoritmo (texto): Policy-gradient methods, specifically Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms.
Observaciones: Proprioceptive and exteroceptive measurements, including the attitude w.r.t the goal, CoM velocity, feet positions, feet contact states, and local height-map.
Acciones: Joint position references, discrete decision variables for which surface and when to make contact with, and continuous state-input trajectories for the motion of the base.
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but implied to be related to locomotion performance and avoiding obstacles or gaps.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the method is trained across a set of challenging locomotion scenarios.
Métricas: Generalization across terrain types; Tracking reference footholds while balancing the robot
Líneas base: A state-of-the-art model-based approach [4]
Resultado: The planner can generalize well across terrain types, and the controller succeeds in tracking reference footholds while always balancing the robot.
Limitaciones: The method still poses challenges such as how to eliminate undesirable yet retain beneficial emergent behavior, and reducing overall sample complexity.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Automatic Exploration for Navigation in Unknown Environment
Tarea: El agente aprende a explorar un entorno desconocido construyendo un mapa del entorno completo sin conocimiento previo.
Algoritmo (texto): Algoritmo de Aprendizaje por Refuerzo Profundo (DRL) basado en una red neuronal profunda para aprender una estrategia de exploración a partir de un mapa parcial.
Robot: no se menciona un robot específico
Observaciones: Mapa parcial del entorno (grilla visual)
Acciones: Selección de la siguiente ubicación de objetivo, discreta
Recompensa: No se especifica en el resumen, pero se menciona que se utiliza una función de utilidad basada en la entropía de Shannon para evaluar la incertidumbre del mapa.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se realizan experimentos en un robot físico.
Líneas base: Métodos tradicionales; Métodos basados en aprendizaje por refuerzo
Sim2real: No se menciona una técnica específica
Resultado: El algoritmo propuesto tiene una mejor eficiencia de aprendizaje y adaptabilidad en entornos desconocidos, y el comportamiento aprendido se puede transferir bien de la simulación al robot físico.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que el enfoque end-to-end ignora la información proporcionada por los métodos de navegación maduros en robótica y aumenta la dificultad de entrenamiento. También se señala que hay un desafío significativo entre la similitud y la realidad.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Population-Coded Spiking Neural Network for Continuous Control
Tarea: Continuous control of mobile robots with high-dimensional observation and action spaces.
Algoritmo (texto): Population-coded spiking actor network (PopSAN) trained with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms, including DDPG, TD3, SAC, and PPO.
Observaciones: Continuous observations, encoded into the activity of individual neuron populations.
Acciones: Continuous actions, generated by decoding the output population activities into real-valued actions, with discrete or continuous actions depending on the implementation.
Recompensa: Average rewards over 10 episodes for each evaluation, where each episode lasted for a maximum of 1000 execution steps.
Entrenamiento: 1 million steps, evaluated every 10k steps, 10 models for each algorithm corresponding to 10 random seeds
Métricas: Mean rewards; Half the value of standard deviation
Líneas base: Deep actor networks; DNN to SNN conversion method (DNN-SNN); SAN with rate-coded inputs (RateSAN)
Sim2real: Layer-wise rescaling technique to map the trained PopSAN with full-precision weights onto the low-precision Loihi chip, and forcing each layer in the SNN on Loihi to start its operation one timestep after its previous layer started its operation.
Resultado: PopSAN achieved the same level of performance as the deep actor networks across all the tasks for all the DRL algorithms, and was 140 times more energy-efficient on continuous control tasks than the deep actor network running on TX2.
Limitaciones: The PopSAN method relies on the appropriate learnable encoding of the network inputs and outputs with the right inductive priors, and the performance could be limited by the representation capacity of the individual neurons.

Título: Deep Reinforcement learning for real autonomous mobile robot navigation in indoor environments
Tarea: autonomous self-learning robot navigation in an unknown environment without a map or planner.
Algoritmo (texto): Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (GA3C) with deep reinforcement learning.
Observaciones: 2D laser scanner data and RGB-D camera data (2D laser scan fusion)
Acciones: discrete actions (angular and linear velocities)
Recompensa: Reward function includes final goal state, collision state, and intermediate states based on distance to goal and orientation to goal; maximum number of iterations per episode with negative reward if goal not reached.
Entrenamiento: 32 training instances in parallel for 20,000 episodes (25 minutes for 1D convolutions, 7 hours for 2D convolutions) on an Intel core i7 and Nvidia GeForce 1070ti
Líneas base: none
Resultado: The method achieved robust and fast learning results, with circling states often reached but the agents able to recover.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a custom simulation environment and may face challenges in real-world deployment due to the need for accurate sensor fusion and robustness.

Título: Efficient and Trustworthy Social Navigation via Explicit and Implicit Robot-Human Communication
Tarea: social navigation, where the robot needs to coordinate with a human to avoid collisions and navigate efficiently.
Algoritmo (texto): planner based on inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to generate communicative actions that maximize the robot’s transparency and efficiency, using a hybrid model that considers both continuous movements and discrete behavior modes.
Observaciones: human and robot trajectories, velocity, acceleration, distance to goal, avoiding obstacles, and avoiding the front side of the robot.
Acciones: actions are discrete (communicative actions) and continuous (robot motion), with explicit communication through a wearable haptic device.
Recompensa: reward functions are defined for both human priority and robot priority scenarios, based on avoiding obstacles, maintaining a desired velocity, and avoiding collisions.
Simulador: simulated environment with orthogonal paths and obstacles.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: human trust; effort reduction; understandability of plans
Líneas base: social force model
Resultado: The planner generated plans that were easier to understand, reduced users’ effort, and increased users trust of the robot, compared to simply performing collision avoidance.
Limitaciones: The model assumes cooperative users and does not account for adversarial behavior, and the amount of data required for training the IRL model can be large and expensive to obtain.

Título: Flightmare: A Flexible Quadrotor Simulator
Tarea: learning a sensorimotor policy for quadrotor control and collision-free path planning in a complex 3D environment.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: RGB cameras with ground-truth depth and semantic segmentation, range finders, and collision detection
Acciones: discrete rotor thrusts or continuous body rates, depending on the task
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: Flightmare, a flexible quadrotor simulator built with Unity and a physics model
Entrenamiento: 25 million time steps for each task, using a laptop with a 12-core Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8850H CPU at up to 2.60GHz
Líneas base: RotorS; Hector; AirSim; FlightGoggles
Resultado: Flightmare achieved 230 Hz for rendering and up to 200,000 Hz for dynamics simulation, allowing the training of neural network controllers for quadrotor stabilization and path planning in complex environments.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Frozone: Freezing-Free, Pedestrian-Friendly Navigation in Human Crowds
Tarea: navigation in dense crowds, avoiding collisions and maintaining pedestrian-friendliness.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) combined with a real-time algorithm (Frozone) for collision avoidance.
Observaciones: 2D position and unit vector representing the front/forward direction of the pedestrian, relative goal location of the robot, depth image from a depth camera.
Acciones: Continuous velocities, bounded to avoid sudden angular motion.
Recompensa: Reward function shaped to minimize time to reach the goal, reduce oscillatory motions, head towards the goal, and avoid collisions.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: success rates; pedestrian-friendliness; rate of freezing
Líneas base: prior methods addressing FRP; DRL-based collision avoidance methods; socially-aware navigation methods
Resultado: Our method results in a 50% increase in success rates, 100% increase in pedestrian-friendliness, and >80% decrease in the rate of freezing in challenging scenarios.
Limitaciones: The method relies on limited sensing capabilities and may face issues with the loss of perception data due to the robot’s motion.

Título: High-Speed Autonomous Drifting with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: driving through sharp corners quickly and stably at high speed (>80 km/h) with large sideslip angles (>20°).
Algoritmo (texto): soft actor-critic (SAC), a model-free deep reinforcement learning algorithm
Observaciones: steering angle δ, throttle τ, forward and side velocities (vx, vy), total velocity v, side slip angle β, heading angle ψ
Acciones: continuous steering angle and throttle, discrete
Recompensa: defined by partial rewards for cross track error (ey), course angle error (eψ), and slip angle error (eβ), with a speed factor to encourage high speed
Entrenamiento: trained on six maps with different levels of difficulty, using Adam optimizer, learning rate 0.0003, batch size 512, for 145.90 episodes (time not stated)
Métricas: cross track error (CTE); heading angle error (HAE); maximum and average velocity (MAX-VEL, AVG-VEL); lap time (L.T.); smoothness of driving (SMOS); maximum slip angle (SLIP)
Líneas base: DQN; DDPG; SAC-WOS
Resultado: The SAC controller achieved the shortest lap time (145.90 seconds) and the highest average velocity (103.71 km/h) among the four methods, with a heading angle error of 5.707° and a slip angle of 29.23°. It also showed good generalization to different vehicle types and mass/tire friction conditions.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the action smoothing strategy can improve the final performance, but it is not clear if this is a limitation of the method or an improvement.

Título: Highlighted map for mobile robot localization and its generation based on reinforcement learning
Tarea: improving the accuracy of Monte Carlo localization (MCL) in monotonous environments by generating a highlighted map that emphasizes landmarks.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) based optimization, specifically using a variant of the RL method from [35]
Observaciones: sensor measurements and the map
Acciones: discrete (particle states)
Recompensa: not stated, but related to the accuracy of the pose estimate
Entrenamiento: not explicitly stated, but involves multiple iterations and tests
Métricas: objective function J; estimation error 1t; computation time 0t
Líneas base: conventional map (likelihood field); KLD-sampling-based MCL (KLD-MCL); scan-matching-based MCL (SM-MCL)
Resultado: The highlighted map provided better performance in terms of the objective function J, lower estimation error 1t, and similar computation time compared to the conventional map and the improved MCL-based algorithms in the simulations.
Limitaciones: The method is designed for low-cost robots and may not perform as well in more complex or high-performance environments.

Título: Learning Agile Robotic Locomotion Skills by Imitating Animals
Tarea: Learning agile locomotion skills by imitating real-world animals for a 18-DoF quadruped robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with motion imitation and latent space adaptation, using a feedforward network for the policy.
Observaciones: 3D location of keypoints, IMU readings, and robot poses.
Acciones: Continuous actions, represented by a distribution over actions.
Recompensa: Defined as the agent's expected return, which is the sum of discounted rewards over time.
Entrenamiento: About 200 million samples in simulation, with 50 real-world trials for adaptation, using proximal policy optimization.
Líneas base: Non-adaptive policies trained in simulation without randomization; Robust policies trained with randomization but not adapted to new environments
Resultado: Adaptive policies outperformed non-adaptive policies on most skills, with a significant improvement in maintaining balance in the real world.
Limitaciones: The policies struggle with some complex motions, such as the Running Man, where the robot shuffles backwards instead of lifting its feet during each step.

Título: Learning quadrupedal locomotion over challenging terrain
Tarea: Learn quadrupedal locomotion over challenging terrain.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL), specifically a temporal convolutional network (TCN) for the policy, with privileged learning and an automated curriculum.
Observaciones: Proprioceptive signals from joint encoders and an inertial measurement unit (IMU).
Acciones: Continuous, based on actuation commands.
Recompensa: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be related to locomotion speed and efficiency.
Simulador: Simulation, with terrains that are rigid and procedurally generated.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be extensive given the robustness achieved.
Métricas: Success rate; Mean linear speed; Mean heading error; Cost of transport (COT)
Líneas base: Baseline [1, 26]
Sim2real: Not explicitly stated, but implied from the deployment on physical robots.
Resultado: The controller achieved higher locomotion speed and lower cost of transport (COT) compared to the baseline in various natural environments, with a zero failure rate in the DARPA Subterranean Challenge and robust performance on unstable debris in indoor environments.
Limitaciones: The training only used rigid terrains and a small set of procedurally generated terrain profiles, which may limit the generalizability to more complex terrains.

Título: Learning to Walk in the Real World with Minimal Human Effort
Tarea: learning to walk on flat ground, a soft mattress, and a doormat with crevices
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with a multi-task learning framework and safety constraint
Observaciones: position and yaw angle of the torso, smoothness of actions
Acciones: continuous, defined by a three-dimensional task vector
Recompensa: defined by a task vector that includes the desired direction of walking, position and yaw angle, and smoothness of actions
Entrenamiento: a few hours
Líneas base: prior work by Haarnoja et al.
Resultado: learned to walk on three terrains in just a few hours, with minimal human effort, and acquired distinct and effective gaits for each terrain
Limitaciones: challenges in transferring the trained policies to the real world, due to the sim-to-real gap

Título: Learning to be Safe: Deep RL with a Safety Critic
Tarea: learn to navigate, locomote, and manipulate objects safely in various environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Safety Q-functions for Reinforcement Learning (SQRL), built on top of off-policy algorithms like SAC.
Observaciones: state and action pairs, with a safety incident indicator I(s)
Acciones: continuous, constrained by a safety critic
Recompensa: defined as minimizing the frequency of catastrophic failures during training, with a safety threshold ϵsafe
Simulador: drunk spider, Minitaur, and cube rotation environments
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: final task performance; cumulative failure rate
Líneas base: SAC; WCPG; ESAC; CPO; RS
Resultado: SQRL achieves better final performance and fewer safety incidents, with faster and more stable learning compared to other methods, especially in the Minitaur and cube rotation tasks.
Limitaciones: The safety threshold ϵsafe needs to be tuned, and the method may be overly cautious in some cases, leading to lower performance.

Título: Long-Range Indoor Navigation with PRM-RL
Tarea: long-range indoor navigation with noisy sensors and controls through cluttered environments.
Algoritmo (texto): AutoRL as the RL method, with PRM as the sampling-based planner.
Observaciones: configuration space (C), collision-free subset of conformation space (Cfree), sensor data, robot dynamics
Acciones: continuous actions for obstacle avoidance
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: simulated environments for kinematic differential drive and kinodynamic car-like robots
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: six baselines in eight different buildings
Sim2real: SLAM-based PRM-RL enables real robot deployments
Resultado: PRM-RL with AutoRL is more successful than several baselines, is robust to noise, and can guide robots over hundreds of meters in the face of noise and obstacles in both simulation and on robots, including over 5.8 km of physical robot navigation.
Limitaciones: the method is sensitive to the quality of the local planner and the computational complexity of roadmap construction.

Título: Mobile robot path planning in dynamic environments through globally guided reinforcement learning
Tarea: Path planning for mobile robots in dynamic environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Globally Guided Reinforcement Learning (G2RL), which combines a global guidance and a local RL-based planner.
Observaciones: Local observation within a field of view (FOV) including free cells, static obstacles, and dynamic obstacles.
Acciones: Discrete actions (Up, Down, Left, Right, Idle).
Recompensa: A novel reward structure that provides dense rewards, encouraging the robot to explore all potential solutions while not strictly following the global guidance. The reward function is defined with specific conditions for reaching free cells, conflicting with obstacles, and reaching cells on the global guidance path.
Simulador: Three different map types: regular, random, and free maps.
Entrenamiento: Trained with one NVIDIA GTX 1080ti GPU, using TensorFlow 1.4, for 200,000 training steps.
Métricas: Moving Cost; Detour Percentage; Computing Time
Líneas base: Global Re-planning; Local Re-planning; Naive reward function
Resultado: G2RL outperforms local and global re-planning methods, with the smallest number of moving steps and smallest standard deviations. It also performs similarly to centralized approaches in terms of moving cost and detour percentage, with a slightly higher computing time.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the naive reward function introduces more detour steps and waiting time steps, and may even cause deadlocks, while their reward function encourages convergence of the navigation tasks while exploring all potential solutions.

Título: One Policy to Control Them All: Shared Modular Policies for Agent-Agnostic Control
Tarea: learn control policies for various agent morphologies, including bipeds, quadrupeds, and monopods
Algoritmo (texto): Shared Modular Policies (SMP) using TD3 as the underlying RL method
Observaciones: local limb states, including global positions, velocities, rotations, and range of movement
Acciones: continuous torque values for all the actuators, discrete
Recompensa: sum of instant rewards across an episode of 1,000 time-steps
Entrenamiento: 1 million training steps, 4 random seeds reported
Líneas base: standard multi-task RL approach; monolithic policy trained on single-agent environments
Resultado: SMP with both-way message passing achieved high rewards even in a zero-shot manner, outperforming the multi-task RL baseline and decentralized message passing schemes
Limitaciones: The method is agnostic to the choice of root node, but the performance can vary slightly depending on the root node

Título: Reinforcement co-learning of deep and spiking neural networks for energy-efficient mapless navigation with neuromorphic hardware
Tarea: mapless navigation
Algoritmo (texto): Spiking Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (SDDPG)
Observaciones: relative distance and direction from the robot to the goal, linear and angular velocities of the robot, distance observations from the laser range scanner
Acciones: left and right wheel speeds (discrete)
Recompensa: R = Rgoal if Gdis < Gth, Robstacle if Odis < Oth, A * (Gdis(t) - Gdis(t-1)) otherwise
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: energy efficiency; rate of successfully navigating to the goal
Líneas base: DDPG
Resultado: The SDDPG on Loihi consumed 75 times less energy per inference as compared to DDPG on Jetson TX2, while also achieving a higher rate of successfully navigating to the goal, ranging from 1% to 4.2%.
Limitaciones: The method is sensitive to the forward-propagation timestep size.

Título: Robot Navigation in Crowds by Graph Convolutional Networks with Attention Learned from Human Gaze
Tarea: Navegación en multitud para un robot móvil.
Algoritmo (texto): Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) con atención aprendida de la mirada humana, Reinforcement Learning (RL)
Observaciones: Posición y estado de los humanos en la multitud.
Acciones: Acciones continuas, ya que se refiere a la navegación del robot.
Recompensa: No se especifica explícitamente, pero se infiere que se basa en la eficiencia y la eficacia de la navegación.
Simulador: Simulaciones con conjuntos de datos de trayectorias de peatones reales.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona pruebas en entornos reales.
Métricas: Tasa de éxito; Tiempo de navegación
Líneas base: SARL; D-GCNRL; U-GCNRL
Sim2real: No se menciona una transferencia de simulación a la realidad.
Resultado: El modelo G-GCNRL mejora la tasa de éxito en un 18.4% y reduce el tiempo de navegación en un 16.4% en comparación con SARL.
Limitaciones: Los modelos existentes consideran solo interacciones parciales entre el robot y cada humano en la multitud, lo que no captura completamente la naturaleza global y dinámica de las interacciones de la multitud. Además, la información sobre la multitud se obtiene combinando la información de estas interacciones parciales, lo que no captura completamente la información estructural importante sobre la configuración geométrica de la multitud y la relación del robot con ella.

Título: The Path Planning of Mobile Robot by Neural Networks and Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: el agente aprende el plan de ruta para un robot móvil.
Algoritmo (texto): DDPG, un algoritmo de aprendizaje por refuerzo basado en redes neuronales y aprendizaje jerárquico.
Robot: robot móvil diferencial con dos ruedas.
Observaciones: posición y orientación del robot, velocidad de las ruedas.
Acciones: velocidad de las ruedas, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: recompensa inmediata basada en el rendimiento del agente, recompensas de descuento.
Simulador: entorno de simulación basado en pyglet.
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico.
Líneas base: Q-Learning; DDQN; PDQN; A3C; DQN
Sim2real: no se menciona una transferencia de simulación a real.
Resultado: DDPG redujo el tiempo de planificación del camino y el número de pasos del camino en comparación con DDQN, mejorando la suavidad del camino planificado en un 79%.
Limitaciones: el método depende de la simulación y no se ha probado en un entorno real.

Título: UAV coverage path planning under varying power constraints using deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: design a trajectory that enables a mobile agent to travel over every point of an area of interest, with random start positions and multiple options for landing positions in an environment containing no-fly zones.
Algoritmo (texto): double deep Q-network (DDQN), based on Q-learning and deep Q-learning
Observaciones: camera and GPS receiver
Acciones: discrete actions (north, east, south, west, land)
Recompensa: coverage reward for each target cell that is covered by the UA V’s field of view for the first time, safety penalty in case the safety controller rejects the agent’s proposed action, constant movement penalty, and penalty in case the UA V runs out of movement budget without having safely landed in a landing zone
Simulador: two-dimensional grid map with three channels (start and landing zones, target zones, and no-fly zones)
Entrenamiento: 50,000 experience replay memory buffer size, 10,000 maximum number of training episodes, 1,190,389 trainable parameters, 0.95 discount factor, 0.005 target network update factor, 128 minibatch size
Líneas base: none
Resultado: The agents successfully landed after completing a trajectory for each movement budget, with a landing ratio of 99.37%, 99.78%, and 98.26% for maps A, B, and C respectively, and a coverage ratio that balanced safe landing and maximum coverage on three different environments.
Limitaciones: The safety controller’s capabilities on a real-world UA V would likely be extended to force navigation to the closest landing zone in the rare cases when the RL agent misses the right moment to return.

Título: Voronoi-Based Multi-Robot Autonomous Exploration in Unknown Environments via Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Autonomous exploration in unknown environments using a multi-robot system.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with a variant using human demonstration data for collision avoidance.
Observaciones: Laser range data, relative position of the target, and velocity command.
Acciones: Continuous linear and angular velocity commands.
Recompensa: The reward function includes distance, safety clearance, angular velocity, and linear velocity components.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: FEP and receding horizon NBVP; Two-stage heuristic information gain-based NBVP; A priori knowledge-based dynamic object search strategy; Incremental road-map based path planning strategy; Traditional approach of frontier-based exploration and DRL
Resultado: The proposed method achieved a 30% reduction in exploration time compared to the traditional approach, and the robots were able to navigate through the waypoints with a 95% success rate.
Limitaciones: The method relies heavily on the training data and the performance may degrade in dynamic environments.

Título: BADGR: An Autonomous Self-Supervised Learning-Based Navigation System
Tarea: reaching a goal GPS location while avoiding collisions and bumpy terrain
Algoritmo (texto): end-to-end reinforcement learning with a predictive model, using a self-supervised, off-policy algorithm
Observaciones: RGB images and GPS
Acciones: discrete actions (linear and angular velocity commands)
Recompensa: defined as avoiding collisions and bumpy terrain, with a reward function that includes penalties for collisions and bumpy terrain, and a goal reaching term
Entrenamiento: 34 hours of data in urban terrain and 8 hours in off-road terrain
Líneas base: LIDAR; naive policy
Resultado: BADGR successfully reached the goal 100% of the time in the urban environment, with an average bumpiness of 8.7±4.4, outperforming both the LIDAR and naive policies.
Limitaciones: The amount of data gathered may seem significant, but the total dataset consisted of 720,000 off-policy datapoints, which is smaller than currently used datasets in computer vision and significantly smaller than the number of samples often used by deep reinforcement learning algorithms.

Título: Collision avoidance in pedestrian-rich environments with deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: collision avoidance in pedestrian-rich environments
Algoritmo (texto): collision avoidance with deep reinforcement learning (CADRL) using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
Observaciones: observable states of nearby agents (positions, velocities, radii) and unobservable states (goal positions, preferred speeds, orientations)
Acciones: speed and heading angle (continuous)
Recompensa: sparse reward function that awards the agent for reaching its goal and penalizes for getting too close to other agents
Entrenamiento: about 24 hours (2 · 10^6 episodes) on a computer with an i7-6700K CPU and 32 parallel environment threads
Líneas base: classical collision avoidance algorithm; another deep RL-based algorithm; our previously published learning-based approach
Resultado: the proposed algorithm outperforms prior works as the number of agents in the environments is increased, achieving fewer collisions and shorter time to goal
Limitaciones: the number of training episodes is large due to the stark contrast in initial policies between this and the earlier approach, and the low learning rate required for stable training

Título: Decentralized Multi-Agent Pursuit Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Capturar un objetivo móvil más rápido con múltiples agentes no holonómicos.
Algoritmo (texto): Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)
Observaciones: Posición relativa del objetivo y otros agentes, usando sensores como LiDARs o cámaras de profundidad.
Acciones: Velocidad angular, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: Combina recompensas individuales y de grupo, basadas en la distancia al objetivo y la formación de los agentes.
Simulador: Simulación con un entorno circular sin obstáculos.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un número específico de pasos o episodios, pero se menciona la aplicación de curriculum learning.
Métricas: Tasa de captura; Tiempo promedio de captura
Líneas base: Algoritmos clásicos; Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)
Sim2real: Transferencia de política desde simulación a drones reales.
Resultado: El algoritmo TD3 logró una tasa de captura del 90% con tres drones, superando a los métodos clásicos.
Limitaciones: El algoritmo requiere un entrenamiento inicial con un radio de captura grande y luego se reduce gradualmente, lo que puede ser un desafío.

Título: Decentralized Structural-RNN for Robot Crowd Navigation with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Safe and efficient navigation through human crowds for mobile robots.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (RL) with a novel end-to-end decentralized structural-RNN (DS-RNN) network.
Observaciones: Robot's position, velocity, goal position, maximum speed, heading angle, and radius; humans' positions.
Acciones: Continuous actions (position and velocity).
Recompensa: The reward is defined as the total accumulated return from each state, which is the expected return for following the policy from the state. The goal is to maximize the expected return.
Simulador: Simulator for training the DS-RNN network.
Entrenamiento: Not stated, but the paper mentions that the network is trained using model-free RL without any supervision.
Métricas: Performance in challenging navigation settings compared with previous methods.
Líneas base: Reaction-based methods (ORCA, RVO), Trajectory-based methods, Learning-based methods (Deep V-Learning).
Sim2real: The method is tested on a real-world TurtleBot 2i after being trained in the simulator.
Resultado: The DS-RNN network outperforms previous methods in challenging navigation scenarios and demonstrates better performance in real-world testing compared to the simulator.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method assumes the state transitions of all surrounding humans are known and well-defined, which are in fact highly stochastic and difficult to model.

Título: Decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning with networked agents: recent advances; [带有网络智能体的去中心化多智能体强化学习进展]
Tarea: sequential decision-making in a common environment without central coordination, where agents exchange information with their neighbors over a communication network.
Algoritmo (texto): FQI (Fitted Q-iteration) and its decentralized variant, policy gradient methods, value-based and policy-based methods.
Observaciones: state and local observations from neighbors, joint action space
Acciones: discrete actions, as implied by the use of Q-functions and policy iteration
Recompensa: long-term return that is common to all agents in cooperative settings, or team-average reward in non-cooperative settings
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: single-agent RL; classical MARL algorithms
Resultado: The proposed algorithms achieve finite-sample performance and linear convergence rates in certain settings, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and empirical results.
Limitaciones: Theoretical analysis is limited, especially for non-cooperative settings and deep neural networks as function approximators.

Título: Deep reinforcement learning for drone navigation using sensor data
Tarea: Navigate a drone to the location of an anomaly using sensor data.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, using incremental curriculum learning.
Observaciones: Sensor direction, sensor magnitude, N, E, S, W space, x-distance, y-distance to the target
Acciones: Discrete actions (move N, E, S or W by one cell)
Recompensa: Positive reward for reaching the goal, negative reward for colliding with an obstacle, small penalty for each movement
Entrenamiento: 50 million training episodes using incremental curriculum learning
Líneas base: Baseline PPO without memory; PPO 8; PPO 16
Resultado: The PPO algorithm with LSTM memory learned to navigate the drone to the goal in a 16x16 grid with 1 obstacle after 5 million iterations, and the mean final reward was used to determine when to stop training each lesson.
Limitaciones: The agent struggles with more complex obstacles and does not travel directly to the goal when the Grid-World environment has very few obstacles.

Título: Learning Vision-Guided Quadrupedal Locomotion End-to-End with Cross-Modal Transformers
Tarea: learn to navigate through different terrains and obstacles, collecting spheres for reward bonuses
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a Transformer-based model, using PPO for training
Observaciones: proprioceptive states and visual observations from a depth camera
Acciones: continuous actions for locomotion control
Recompensa: forward reward, sphere reward, alive reward, and energy usage penalty
Simulador: 6 simulated environments with varying terrain, obstacles, and spheres
Entrenamiento: 15M samples with 5 different random seeds
Métricas: mean episode return; distance moved; number of collisions
Líneas base: State-Only baseline; Depth-Only baseline; State-Depth-Concat baseline; Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) baseline
Resultado: Our method outperforms the baselines by a large margin in both simulated and real-world environments, moving 92% farther and colliding less in the Indoor & Obs environment, and approximately 90% farther without colliding into any obstacles in the Forest environment.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the generalization ability of the State-Depth-Concat baseline decreases as training progresses, whereas for their method it either plateaus or increases over time, indicating that their method is more effective at capturing essential information in the visual and proprioceptive information during training, and is less prone to overfit to training environments.

Título: Learning a State Representation and Navigation in Cluttered and Dynamic Environments
Tarea: The robot's goal is to successfully navigate towards the goal, while avoiding potential hazards along the way.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL), specifically a model-free RL algorithm
Observaciones: Depth frames from a front-facing camera, the camera’s trajectory, and relative coordinates of a nearby goal
Acciones: Velocity command (discrete or continuous not stated)
Recompensa: Not stated
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Not stated
Resultado: The system can navigate in a cluttered scene and avoid people moving across its path in a very reactive manner.
Limitaciones: The method assumes the robot is made of a single rectangular cuboid and does not simulate the whole robot and its velocity tracking controller.

Título: Learning efficient navigation in vortical flow fields
Tarea: Learning efficient point-to-point navigation in the presence of unsteady two-dimensional flow fields.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Remember and Forget Experience replay
Observaciones: Local flow information, such as velocity or vorticity
Acciones: Continuous actions (swimming maneuvers)
Recompensa: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be related to reaching the target location efficiently.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper discusses the training process and results in simulation.
Líneas base: Global path planner
Resultado: The RL approach achieved near 100% success in reaching the target locations while approaching the time-efficiency of paths found by a global optimal control planner, outperforming a bio-mimetic vorticity sensing approach by nearly two-fold in success rate.
Limitaciones: The success of the velocity approach may not extend to real-world scenarios with more complex, 3D fluid flows and non-linear dynamics.

Título: Learning to Fly-A Gym Environment with PyBullet Physics for Reinforcement Learning of Multi-agent Quadcopter Control
Tarea: control of one or more nanoquadcopters
Algoritmo (texto): A2C, DDPG, PPO, SAC, TD3 (Stable Baselines3), MADDPG, QMIX (RLlib)
Algoritmo (diccionario): A2C; PPO; DDPG; TD3; SAC; MADDPG; QMIX
Observaciones: kinematics, RGB, depth, segmentation
Acciones: commanded RPMs, desired velocities
Recompensa: negation of the squared Euclidean distance from the set point for single agent take-off and hover, negative squared Euclidean distance for leader and negative squared Euclidean distance for follower in multi-agent leader-follower task
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: PPO, A2C, SAC for single agent take-off and hover, MADDPG, QMIX for multi-agent leader-follower
Resultado: SAC performs best, all algorithms succeed albeit with very different learning curves for single agent take-off and hover, stable training leading to successfully trained policies for multi-agent leader-follower task
Limitaciones: learning curves and performance of algorithms are not tuned, only default implementations are used

Título: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: A quadruped robot must learn to walk across challenging terrain, including uneven surfaces, slopes, stairs, and obstacles, while following base-heading and linear-velocity commands.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with modifications for massively parallel use
Observaciones: Base-heading and linear-velocity commands, terrain type (flat, sloped, randomly rough, discrete obstacles, stairs)
Acciones: Continuous actions for locomotion
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but implied to be related to successfully navigating the terrain while following commands
Entrenamiento: Training policies for flat terrain in under 4 minutes, and in 20 minutes for uneven terrain
Métricas: Not explicitly stated, but likely includes success rate, time to complete tasks, and robustness to terrain
Líneas base: previous work on training legged robots using reinforcement learning
Resultado: The approach allows training policies for flat terrain in under 4 minutes, and in 20 minutes for uneven terrain, representing a speedup of multiple orders of magnitude compared to previous work.
Limitaciones: The approach requires significant computational resources and may not be feasible for all researchers, and the success of the approach is highly dependent on the specific implementation details and hyperparameters.

Título: Lvio-Fusion: A Self-adaptive Multi-sensor Fusion SLAM Framework Using Actor-critic Method
Tarea: fusionar datos de sensores (estéreo, LiDAR, IMU, GPS) para estimar la posición y mapeo en tiempo real de un robot móvil.
Algoritmo (texto): actor-critic method (TD3 algorithm)
Observaciones: información de los sensores en el estado actual del robot (features, IMU, GPS, etc.)
Acciones: pesos de los factores de los sensores (discretos)
Recompensa: recíproco del error de pose relativa (RPE) entre la pose estimada y la real
Simulador: no se menciona un simulador específico, se evalúa en datos reales
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico
Líneas base: VINS-Fusion; LIO-SAM
Sim2real: no se menciona una técnica específica
Resultado: Lvio-Fusion logró una precisión media de 1.07 metros y un RMSE de 1.13 metros en el KITTI dataset, mejorando significativamente la precisión en comparación con VINS-Fusion y LIO-SAM.
Limitaciones: el algoritmo necesita ser entrenado y evaluado con conjuntos de datos más grandes para generalización.

Título: Memory-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Obstacle Avoidance in UAV with Limited Environment Knowledge
Tarea: enable a UAV quadrotor to autonomously avoid collisions with obstacles in unstructured and unknown indoor environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Recurrent Q-network with Temporal Attention, based on Deep Q-Network (DQN)
Observaciones: noisy depth maps from a simulated Kinect sensor
Acciones: discrete actions: 'go straight', 'turn left', 'turn right'
Recompensa: reward is defined as Ri = min(1, di−rdrone/σ−rdrone), where di is the distance to the nearest obstacle, rdrone is the radius of the drone, and σ is the threshold distance; if the agent collides, the episode ends with a penalty of -10; the agent also receives an additional +0.5 reward if it chooses the 'go straight' action
Simulador: simulated environments with varying complexity, including hallways and rooms with obstacles of varying structures and sizes
Entrenamiento: trained in 12 different simulated indoor environments, network hyper-parameters are as shown in Table I
Métricas: average number of steps taken until collision with an obstacle
Líneas base: DQN previously proposed [23]; random policy; straight policy
Sim2real: degraded sensor images with Gaussian blurring, random jitter and superpixel replace at the time of training
Resultado: The proposed DRL model outperforms DQN on different environments, the UA V smoothly follows a path while avoiding static obstacles and skillfully chooses actions to avoid collisions with dynamic obstacles as well. The average energy consumption over several runs is 0.0571 Wh/m for the proposed approach and 0.0743 Wh/m for D3QN, showing that the proposed method achieves a lower value of energy consumption per unit distance traveled when compared to the D3QN method.
Limitaciones: The method requires substantial amount of data concerning the images of hallway environments and is not efficient. Moreover, the method proposed in [23] is not intuitive. It does not attempt to mimic how humans learn to avoid obstacles.

Título: Model-Based Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Flight with Suspended Payloads
Tarea: Transporting suspended payloads using a quadcopter.
Algoritmo (texto): Meta-reinforcement learning with a model-based approach, using PETS algorithm and variational inference.
Observaciones: The agent observes the state of the hybrid robot-payload system, including the position of the payload and the quadcopter's actions.
