Acciones: The agent outputs actions for the quadcopter, which are discrete (commands to the motors).
Recompensa: The reward is defined as the quadcopter following a desired payload trajectory, dropping off the payload at designated locations, and picking up new payloads with a magnetic gripper.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Non-adaptive methods
Sim2real: The method is tested on a real-world quadcopter after being trained in simulation.
Resultado: The method enables a quadcopter to plan and execute trajectories that follow desired payload trajectories, drop off these payloads at designated locations, and even pick up new payloads with a magnetic gripper. The performance improvement over non-adaptive methods is demonstrated on a real-world quadcopter.
Limitaciones: The method requires domain knowledge to identify all possible factors of variation, and that we can measure each factor at training time. Additionally, the performance may degrade if the payload dynamics change significantly from the training data.

Título: Real-time active vision for a humanoid soccer robot using deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: controlar los movimientos de la cabeza de un robot humanoide de fútbol para obtener la mejor visión de los puntos de referencia útiles y mantener la pelota en el campo de visión mientras se localiza a sí mismo en un entorno dinámico.
Algoritmo (texto): DDQN y PER, basado en Deep Q-learning
Observaciones: imágenes en escala de grises capturadas por una cámara montada en la cabeza del robot
Acciones: movimientos discretos del robot hacia una dirección específica para un pequeño ángulo fijo
Recompensa: la función de recompensa se encarga de alentar al robot a mover su cabeza hacia la posición óptima y penalizarlo por moverse lejos de ella; se mide el éxito en términos de la tasa de éxito, la duración del éxito y la duración de la pérdida de la pelota
Entrenamiento: 30,000 pasos de tiempo, implementado en una PC con un procesador Intel Core i7-7700HQ y una tarjeta gráfica Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060
Métricas: tasa de éxito; duracion de éxito; duracion de pérdida de la pelota
Líneas base: métodos basados en entropía
Resultado: El método propuesto logró una tasa de éxito del 80% en la obtención de la mejor posición de visión, superando a los métodos basados en entropía en el contexto de RoboCup, especialmente cuando aumenta el error de localización.
Limitaciones: El método requiere un procesamiento significativo y un procedimiento de entrenamiento costoso, y puede ser difícil realizar un entrenamiento real en un entorno físico.

Título: Recovery RL: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Learned Recovery Zones
Tarea: extracting a red block without toppling other blocks or colliding with a distractor arm, navigating a maze, avoiding obstacles in a 2D navigation task, and performing contact-rich manipulation tasks in simulation and on a physical robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Recovery RL, which uses a task policy and a recovery policy, with DDPG for model-free recovery and MPC for model-based recovery.
Observaciones: high-dimensional image observations
Acciones: discrete actions for navigation and manipulation tasks
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: 6 simulation domains, including navigation, manipulation, and visual navigation tasks
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: ratio of the cumulative number of task successes and the cumulative number of constraint violations
Líneas base: Unconstrained; Lagrangian Relaxation (LR); Safety Q-Functions for RL (SQRL); Risk Sensitive Policy Optimization (RSPO); Reward Penalty (RP); Critic Penalty Reward Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO)
Resultado: Recovery RL outperforms the next best prior method across all domains, trading off constraint violations and task successes 2-20 times more efficiently in simulation domains and 3 times more efficiently in physical experiments.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the model-based recovery mechanism may be better able to compensate for approximation errors in the safety critic, but this is not universally true for all tasks.

Título: Robot Navigation in Constrained Pedestrian Environments using Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Navegar de forma segura alrededor de peatones en entornos indoor con restricciones espaciales.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) con un planificador de movimiento basado en muestreo y un polímero reactivamente aprendido con RL.
Robot: Simulación de un robot no holonómico con ruedas.
Observaciones: Objetivo final, mediciones lidar, waypoints.
Acciones: Velocidad lineal y angular, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: Se compone de múltiples términos que fomentan alcanzar el objetivo final, minimizar el tiempo, evitar colisiones y seguir el camino global.
Simulador: Gibson Interactive Simulator, que utiliza el motor de física Pybullet y modelos de peatones basados en el modelo ORCA.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, se menciona la utilización de múltiples entornos de simulación.
Líneas base: SAC; planificador de movimiento basado en muestreo
Sim2real: No se menciona una transferencia de simulación a real.
Resultado: Los agentes entrenados en entornos simplificados de paredes generalizan mejor a entornos 3D reconstruidos de entornos reales.
Limitaciones: Los autores reconocen que el desafío original de la navegación no puede ser aprendido progresivamente, sino que es el resultado de combinar patrones complejos de layout-movimiento de agentes dinámicos (peatones).

Título: Robotic Occlusion Reasoning for Efficient Object Existence Prediction
Tarea: when being asked about an object, a robot needs to move as few steps as possible around a table with randomly placed objects to predict whether the queried object exists.
Algoritmo (texto): recurrent neural network model trained with reinforcement learning and supervised learning methods using a curriculum training strategy
Observaciones: egocentric RGB images, word instruction
Acciones: three movement actions (circle left, circle right, and stop), discrete
Recompensa: accuracy reward for correct prediction, latency reward for movement steps, total reward is a summation of these two rewards
Entrenamiento: about four days using one GPU (NVIDIA Titan RTX), 900k, 900k, 400k, and 400k episodes respectively for four levels of training data
Métricas: accuracy of correct predictions; average number of movement steps
Líneas base: passive model; random model; exhaustive exploration model
Resultado: the proposed model can outperform the passive and random baselines by a large margin, and achieve a similar prediction accuracy to the exhaustive exploration model while requiring only about 10% of the baseline’s number of movement steps on average.
Limitaciones: the model generalizes to novel object combinations with a moderate loss of accuracy, and the variety of object combinations in the training data benefits increasing generalization.

Título: Robotic information gathering with reinforcement learning assisted by domain knowledge: An application to gas source localization
Tarea: localizar fuentes de gas en un entorno desconocido
Algoritmo (texto): Aprendizaje por Refuerzo (RL) con modelado de conocimiento del dominio
Observaciones: concentración de gas, velocidad del viento
Acciones: moverse en una cuadrícula de celdas (↑,↓,←,→)
Recompensa: basada en la distancia de Tierra Mover entre la distribución de fuentes estimada y la verdadera
Simulador: método de elementos finitos (FEM) para simular la dispersión de gas
Entrenamiento: no se menciona
Líneas base: model-free RL; chemotaxis; anemotaxis; infotaxis
Resultado: el algoritmo propuesto con conocimiento del dominio mejora la localización de fuentes de gas en comparación con el RL model-free y otros métodos
Limitaciones: el algoritmo requiere un modelo de dispersión de gas que puede ser complejo de implementar y el rendimiento puede depender de la precisión del modelo

Título: Ving: Learning Open-World Navigation with Visual Goals
Tarea: navegar hacia un objetivo visualmente indicado en entornos outdoor y no estructurados.
Algoritmo (texto): aprendizaje por refuerzo (RL) con aprendizaje supervisado y aprendizaje por diferencias temporales, combinado con búsqueda de grafos no métricos.
Observaciones: observaciones egocéntricas tomadas por una cámara montada en el robot
Acciones: acciones continuas de velocidad lineal y angular
Recompensa: no se especifica directamente, pero se infiere que se basa en la capacidad del robot para llegar al objetivo visualizado
Entrenamiento: usando datos de experiencia previa recogidos fuera de línea, sin necesidad de recopilación de datos en línea
Métricas: rendimiento general en la navegación hacia objetivos visuales
Líneas base: metodos basados en planificación; metodos de aprendizaje por refuerzo y planificación
Resultado: ViNG supera a varios métodos basados en aprendizaje por refuerzo y planificación en la navegación hacia objetivos visuales en entornos no estructurados, aprendiendo solo de datos de experiencia previa recogidos fuera de línea.
Limitaciones: señala que el método puede fallar si no se le permite recopilar nueva experiencia en un simulador o en el mundo real.

Título: APPL: Adaptive Planner Parameter Learning
Tarea: The agent learns to navigate through complex environments by adjusting the parameters of a classical navigation system based on human demonstrations, interventions, and feedback.
Algoritmo (texto): Adaptive Planner Parameter Learning (appl), which includes appld, appli, apple, and applr. applr uses unsupervised reinforcement learning.
Observaciones: 3D point cloud data from a Velodyne LiDAR transformed into 2D laser scan, robot's position and velocity, obstacle map inflation radius.
Acciones: Continuous, as it adjusts parameters of a planner.
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but implied to be related to navigation performance and traversal time.
Simulador: Not explicitly stated, but the method involves simulation training.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but involves collecting interventions and demonstrations.
Líneas base: Default parameters; Parameters learned without context; Demonstrator; Type A interventions; Type A and B interventions; Full demonstration
Resultado: appli can improve navigation performance by learning from only a few interventions, and the overall system can generalize well to unseen environments, with traversal times significantly reduced compared to default parameters and even outperforming full demonstrations in some cases.
Limitaciones: The method relies on human interventions and demonstrations, which may not always be available or accurate, and the performance may degrade in highly complex or novel environments.

Título: A Walk in the Park: Learning to Walk in 20 Minutes With Model-Free Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: robotic locomotion, specifically quadrupedal walking
Algoritmo (texto): Q-function actor-critic methods, specifically DroQ with Dropout and Layer Normalization
Observaciones: joint angles and velocities
Acciones: low-level PD control targets, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: 20,000 samples, 0.3 hours
Líneas base: Wu et al. [23]; Smith et al. [24]; Kumar et al. [16]; Rudin et al. [22]; Lee et al. [25]
Resultado: The A1 quadrupedal robot learned to walk in 20 minutes across five environments, including natural outdoor terrains, using a simple model-free method.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the key is not any one specific critical choice, but the general principle of augmenting actor-critic RL with regularization or normalization.

Título: Adaptive Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV-based Active Sensing
Tarea: Planar un piloto automático (UA V) para mapear áreas de terreno con mayor temperatura, utilizando un sensor a bordo.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) combinado con Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) y una red neuronal convolucional (CNN).
Algoritmo (diccionario): AlphaZero / MCTS + red; CNN como codificador
Observaciones: Mapa de la terreno, posiciones de medición 3D, costos de vuelo entre posiciones de medición.
Acciones: Posiciones de medición 3D, discretas.
Recompensa: La recompensa se define como la diferencia entre la traza de la matriz de covariancia antes y después de aplicar el filtro de Kalman, ajustada por el costo de la acción.
Simulador: Simulaciones de monitoreo de terreno con variaciones en mapas de prioridad, variables de objetivo y posiciones iniciales del UA V.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se utilizan épocas de simulación y entrenamiento de la CNN.
Líneas base: MCTS; algoritmos de optimización global
Sim2real: No se menciona una transferencia de simulación a real.
Resultado: Nuestro método se muestra en par con métodos existentes mientras reduce el tiempo de ejecución en 8-10 veces.
Limitaciones: El método se basa en simulaciones y puede ser computacionalmente costoso para tareas reales.

Título: Advanced Skills by Learning Locomotion and Local Navigation End-to-End
Tarea: El agente debe alcanzar una posición objetivo dentro de un tiempo definido.
Algoritmo (texto): Optimización de Polímero Proximal (PPO) con Isaac Gym en simulación.
Observaciones: Posiciones y velocidades de los resortes, velocidad lineal y angular de la base, comandos, acciones anteriores, y mediciones del terreno alrededor del robot.
Acciones: Posiciones de los resortes objetivo para los motores, transformadas en torques de los resortes por un controlador PD.
Recompensa: La recompensa se divide en dos partes: una recompensa de tarea solo activa al final del episodio, y varias penalizaciones proporcionadas durante el episodio. La recompensa de tarea se calcula como 1 / (1 + ||xb - x∗b||^2) si el tiempo es mayor que T - Tr, y 0 en caso contrario, donde xb y x∗b son las posiciones actuales y objetivo de la base, t es el tiempo desde el inicio del episodio, T es la longitud máxima del episodio y Tr es un parámetro que define la duración de la recompensa. También se introducen penalizaciones para aceleraciones de resortes, torques de resortes, colisiones, y cambios de acción bruscos. Además, se introduce una nueva recompensa que penaliza las aceleraciones de los pies, reduciendo los impactos con el suelo, causando ruido y posibles daños en los motores y estructura.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica el presupuesto de entrenamiento, pero se menciona que el algoritmo PPO se utiliza para entrenar la red neuronal en simulación y luego se transfiere al robot real sin necesidad de adicional entrenamiento.
Líneas base: Seguimiento de velocidad; Control basado en posición continua
Sim2real: No se especifica la técnica utilizada para transferir del simulador al robot real.
Resultado: El agente aprendió un nuevo gaita de locomoción que resulta en un menor consumo de energía y una tasa de éxito más alta. El agente pudo cruzar terrenos desafiantes que no eran posibles anteriormente.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que la recompensa principal es escasa, lo que hace que sea beneficioso agregar una recompensa que fomente la exploración al principio del entrenamiento. También se menciona que la penalización de estancamiento puede afectar la solución óptima.

Título: Adversarial Motion Priors Make Good Substitutes for Complex Reward Functions
Tarea: learning agile and controllable locomotion for legged robots
Algoritmo (texto): Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) with a policy gradient method (PPO)
Observaciones: joint angles, joint velocities, orientation, and previous actions
Acciones: joint angles and torques, discrete
Recompensa: a composite reward combining a task reward and a style reward, where the style reward is learned from motion capture data
Entrenamiento: 4 billion environment steps, approximately 4.2 years of simulation data, 16 hours on a single Tesla V100 GPU
Líneas base: complex reward formulations [5], [6], [19]
Sim2real: domain randomization to simulate real-world conditions
Resultado: policies trained with motion priors achieved a lower Cost of Transport and exhibited more natural gait transitions, leading to more energy-efficient locomotion
Limitaciones: the method requires a significant amount of computational resources and time for training, and the transfer to the real robot is not perfect due to the complexity of the real-world environment

Título: CPG-RL: Learning Central Pattern Generators for Quadruped Locomotion
Tarea: learn to modulate the intrinsic oscillator setpoints (amplitude and frequency) and coordinate rhythmic behavior among different oscillators for quadruped locomotion.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with amplitude-controlled phase oscillators, specifically Policies Modulating Trajectory Generators (CPG-RL).
Observaciones: Proprioceptive sensing and contact booleans
Acciones: Discrete (torques or desired task space positions)
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the goal is to achieve robust locomotion and adapt to disturbances.
Entrenamiento: Training budget and hardware not stated
Métricas: Robustness to disturbances; Performance on uneven terrain; Ability to modulate body height and foot swing heights
Líneas base: Model-based control; Learning-based control
Sim2real: Sim-to-real transfer to the Unitree A1 quadruped
Resultado: The CPG-RL controller achieved robust locomotion on the Unitree A1 quadruped, including walking at 0.8 m/s with a 13.75 kg load representing 115% of the nominal quadruped mass, and modulating body height and foot swing heights on the fly.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that parameter tuning remains difficult and that the sim-to-real transfer presents added difficulties from non-modeled dynamics and possible overfitting of simulator physics engine parameters.

Título: Cat-Like Jumping and Landing of Legged Robots in Low Gravity Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Controlar la orientación de un robot quadrúpedo en entornos de baja gravedad, incluyendo reorientación, aterrizaje y salto.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: Posiciones y velocidades de los joint, ángulo de inclinación del base y velocidad angular de inclinación del base.
Acciones: Posiciones de los joint deseadas, acciones discretas
Recompensa: La recompensa se define en términos de la orientación del base, las torques deseados, la aceleración del base y la velocidad del base.
Entrenamiento: 150 millones de pasos, 150000 episodios, 6 horas de entrenamiento en una computadora moderna
Líneas base: No se mencionan
Sim2real: Transferencia de simulación a real utilizando randomización del dominio
Resultado: El robot SpaceBok logró reorientarse, aterrizar y saltar con precisión en un entorno de baja gravedad, demostrando un rendimiento de 0.22 m/s en la velocidad del base.
Limitaciones: Los autores reconocen que la simulación no puede capturar todas las dinámicas complejas del sistema, lo que puede causar desafíos en la transferencia de simulación a la realidad.

Título: Combining Learning-Based Locomotion Policy With Model-Based Manipulation for Legged Mobile Manipulators
Tarea: Learn locomotion policies for legged robots that can counteract disturbances and adapt to multiple manipulator configurations.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a wrench sequence generator, combined with Model Predictive Control (MPC) for the arm controller.
Observaciones: External wrench (force and torque) observations, wrench sequence prediction.
Acciones: Continuous actions for base control, discrete actions for arm control.
Recompensa: Not stated
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Performance on rough terrain with manipulation tasks
Líneas base: Model-based control (MPC)
Resultado: The legged mobile manipulator demonstrated stable locomotion on rough terrain while performing manipulation tasks, with improved performance using wrench predictions from MPC.
Limitaciones: The method requires re-training for different manipulator configurations, and the performance on rough terrain with manipulation tasks is the main metric.

Título: Concurrent Training of a Control Policy and a State Estimator for Dynamic and Robust Legged Locomotion
Tarea: learn a control policy and state estimator for dynamic and robust legged locomotion on various terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for training the actor and critic, supervised learning for training the estimator network.
Observaciones: base orientation, angular velocity, joint positions and velocities, desired joint position targets for two previous time steps, joint position error history, joint velocity history, Cartesian positions of the feet relative to the center of mass, and given velocity command.
Acciones: desired joint positions for each actuator, discrete
Recompensa: defined by a combination of linear and angular velocity rewards, airtime reward, foot slip reward, foot clearance reward, orientation reward, joint torque reward, joint position reward, joint speed reward, joint acceleration reward, action smoothness rewards, and base motion reward.
Entrenamiento: 800 different environments, 100 Hz, not stated
Líneas base: MPC-based controller; previous work on Mini Cheetah
Sim2real: dynamics randomization, curriculum learning, and training in simulation followed by transfer to the real robot.
Resultado: The Mini Cheetah achieved highly dynamic locomotion at 3.74 m/s in various indoor and outdoor environments and robust and reliable locomotion behaviors on a slippery plate, bumpy asphalt road, and hills.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the end-to-end neural network structure may not be interpretable and that the performance of the policy network can be sensitive to the quality of the state estimates from the estimator network.

Título: Deep Hierarchical Planning from Pixels
Tarea: Navegar en un laberinto 3D desde la primera persona, activar pines en secuencias correctas, y juegos de Atari.
Algoritmo (texto): Director, que combina un algoritmo de aprendizaje jerárquico con Dreamer para el aprendizaje de la política de trabajo.
Observaciones: Imágenes de primera persona y datos propioscópicos
Acciones: Acciones de torques articulares, acciones discretas para juegos de Atari
Recompensa: Recompensa de similitud coseno entre vectores de estado y objetivo, recompensa de 10 puntos al activar todos los pines en la secuencia correcta, recompensa de 1 punto por cada paso en el objetivo en mazes.
Simulador: Simulaciones de mazes, entornos de Pin Pads, juegos de Atari, Control Suite, Crafter y DMLab
Entrenamiento: Más de 6 millones de pasos de entrenamiento, 4 instancias de entorno, 16 pasos de política por gradiente, 24 horas de entrenamiento en un GPU V100
Métricas: Retorno de episodio; Tasa de éxito; Puntuación humana normalizada
Líneas base: DreamerV2; Plan2Explore; HIRO; NORL
Resultado: Director supera a DreamerV2 y Plan2Explore en mazes de diferentes tamaños y en la secuencia de activación de pines, logrando un rendimiento humano normalizado superior en los juegos de Atari.
Limitaciones: El aprendizaje jerárquico puede ser menos eficiente en tareas que requieren memoria a largo plazo.

Título: Deep Whole-Body Control: Learning a Unified Policy for Manipulation and Locomotion
Tarea: The task the agent learns is to control a legged robot with an attached arm for manipulation and locomotion, specifically tasks like wiping a whiteboard, picking up a cup, pressing door-open buttons, placing, throwing a cup into a garbage bin, and picking in clustered environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Advantage Mixing and Regularized Online Adaptation (RMA) for Sim2Real transfer.
Robot: Unitree Go1 quadruped, Interbotix WidowX 250s arm
Observaciones: Base state, arm state, leg state, last action, end-effector position and orientation command, base velocity command, and environment extrinsics.
Acciones: Target arm joint position and target leg joint position, both discrete.
Recompensa: The reward is the sum of manipulation reward and locomotion reward, with the manipulation reward encouraging minimizing energy consumption at each leg joint.
Simulador: Simulation environment with varying parameters for training the policy.
Entrenamiento: Training budget not stated, but the paper mentions 1000 episodes for testing.
Métricas: Survival percentage; Base Accel; Vel Error; EE Error; Tot. Energy
Líneas base: Separate policies for legs and the arm; One uncoordinated policy; Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA); Expert policy; Domain Randomization
Sim2real: Regularized Online Adaptation (RMA) is used to transfer the policy from simulation to the real robot.
Resultado: The unified policy outperforms separate and uncoordinated policies, achieving 87% survival rate and 0.82 m3 arm workspace, compared to 64% survival rate and 0.58 m3 arm workspace for separate policies.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method relies on the assumption that the environment extrinsics can be accurately predicted by the adaptation module, which may not always be the case.

Título: Finding Fallen Objects Via Asynchronous Audio-Visual Integration
Tarea: Finding fallen objects via asynchronous audio-visual integration in a 3D virtual environment.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL), imitation learning, modular planning
Observaciones: first-person-view RGB image, depth map, egocentric binaural audio, agent's current pose
Acciones: move forward, rotate left, rotate right, look up, look down, found (discrete)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical and RL
Resultado: Experimental results suggest that it remains very challenging for embodied agents to complete the task successfully.
Limitaciones: The task could plausibly be solved primarily by learning semantic correlations between sounds and the scene context, and the locations of the sounding sources were defined in 2D uniform grids with fixed height, rather than the 3D locations that characterize sound source localization in real-world environments.

Título: Goal-Driven Autonomous Exploration through Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Autonomous navigation and exploration in unknown environments towards a global goal.
Algoritmo (texto): Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) for local navigation, with an Information-based Distance Limited Exploration (IDLE) method for global navigation.
Observaciones: Laser readings and robot odometry sensors.
Acciones: Continuous actions for linear and angular velocity.
Recompensa: Goal reward if the distance to the goal is less than a threshold, collision reward if a collision is detected, and an immediate reward based on current linear and angular velocities.
Simulador: Simulated environment for training the TD3 policy.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: The proposed method outperformed similar exploration methods in complex static and dynamic environments without relying on a map or prior information.
Limitaciones: The method relies on laser sensors and may not work well in environments with limited visibility or where the robot has already visited a location.

Título: Learning Agile Skills via Adversarial Imitation of Rough Partial Demonstrations
Tarea: Learning agile skills such as backflip and stand-up for a quadruped robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Wasserstein Adversarial Behavior Imitation (WASABI), a variant of Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (GAIL)
Observaciones: Limited state observations, such as only local velocities of the robot’s base
Acciones: Continuous, target joint positions
Recompensa: Extracted from rough and partial demonstrations using a Wasserstein GAN formulation, with the discriminator output used as a reward that encourages the learning agent to generate similar behaviors to the demonstration
Entrenamiento: Not stated explicitly, but Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is used in Isaac Gym, and domain randomization is applied for sim-to-real transfer
Líneas base: LSGAN; handcrafted task reward
Resultado: WASABI outperforms LSGAN in terms of DTW distance, achieving comparable performance to expert policies trained with handcrafted rewards, and successfully replicating roughly demonstrated behaviors on the real Solo 8 robot.
Limitaciones: Providing a good evaluation metric for generic rough demonstrations is not straightforward, and the method may not robustly inform about closeness to feasible, desirable motions from the robot’s perspective.

Título: Legged Locomotion in Challenging Terrains using Egocentric Vision
Tarea: legged locomotion in challenging terrains
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with a cheap-to-compute variant of depth image in phase 1, followed by supervised learning in phase 2
Observaciones: scandots (terrain height at specific coordinates) and proprioception
Acciones: joint angles, discrete
Recompensa: penalizes energy consumption and prevents damage to hardware on complex terrain
Simulador: IsaacGym (IG) simulator with the legged gym library
Entrenamiento: 24 timesteps, 2-3 days on a single GPU
Métricas: average displacement; mean time to fall
Líneas base: blind policy; noisy methods
Resultado: The method outperforms the noisy and blind baselines by 60-90% in terms of total mean time to fall and average displacement, with the monolithic and RMA architectures traveling up to 25% farther on stepping stones and up to 6.3 times farther on stairs and discrete obstacles.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a two-phase training scheme and may not perform as well if the scandots contain more information than what depth can infer.

Título: Legged Robots that Keep on Learning: Fine-Tuning Locomotion Policies in the Real World
Tarea: The agent learns to fine-tune locomotion policies in real-world environments, enabling it to adapt to various terrains and recover from failures.
Algoritmo (texto): off-policy REDQ algorithm, a variant of SAC
Observaciones: The agent observes its own onboard sensors
Acciones: Discrete actions for forward and backward pacing, and a reset policy for recovery, with continuous actions for fine-tuning
Recompensa: The reward is defined by the robot's onboard sensors, encouraging successful completion of the task and recovery from failures
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Success rate; Number of episodes to success
Líneas base: Classical methods; RL methods trained in simulation
Resultado: The A1 quadruped robot learned to pace forwards and backwards on an outdoor grass field and side-step on three indoor terrains, improving its performance through real-world fine-tuning.
Limitaciones: The method relies on pre-training in simulation and may not generalize to all unforeseen conditions, and the real-world training process is not detailed in terms of steps or episodes.

Título: Mobile Robot Path Planning Using a QAPF Learning Algorithm for Known and Unknown Environments
Tarea: computation of feasible paths for mobile robots in known and unknown environments
Algoritmo (texto): QAPF learning algorithm, a variant of Q-learning with artificial potential field (APF) weighting
Observaciones: the agent observes the environment and its state, including obstacles and the goal point
Acciones: discrete actions, as the agent chooses the best action based on the learning values Qm×n
Recompensa: the reward is defined as 100 when the agent arrives at the goal state, -1 when the agent collides with obstacles or steps into the limits of the workspace, and 0 otherwise
Entrenamiento: from 5×10^4 to 3×10^6 episodes, with 161×161=25,921 states, on an Intel Core i9 CPU (3.60 GHz) with 16 GB of RAM running Ubuntu Focal Fossa
Métricas: path length; path smoothness; learning time
Líneas base: classical Q-learning (CQL) approach
Resultado: The QAPF learning algorithm achieved an improvement of 18.83% in path length for the online mode, 169.75% in path smoothness for the offline mode, and 74.84% in training time over the classical approach.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the QAPF learning algorithm may not find the global shortest path, but will find a nearly optimal or optimal path in the best of cases.

Título: Particle Filter Design Based on Reinforcement Learning and Its Application to Mobile Robot Localization
Tarea: designing the particle filter for mobile robot localization to improve the localization accuracy.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) based method, with particle filter (PF) as the base algorithm.
Robot: wheeled robot equipped with a two-dimensional LIDAR
Observaciones: position and orientation of the robot, odometry data, LIDAR measurements, and environment map
Acciones: output of the particle filter, discrete
Recompensa: defined as the negative of the estimation error between the true state and the estimated state, and the negative of the variance of the particles
Entrenamiento: 10 sets of training data, 100,000 iterations, 100 particles, 5 Hz frequency
Líneas base: initial parameters; only α was optimized; only m was optimized; PF equivalent to [12]
Resultado: the proposed method further reduces estimation errors compared to the conventional method, with a mean J of 84.0 and mean 1T ∑Tt=1Δt of 0.212 in the first experiment, and similar performance in a different environment.
Limitaciones: the method assumes that the same performance is obtained when the state changes in a trajectory similar to the one in which the training data were collected, and it is not clear if the method can be easily extended to time-varying systems.

Título: Policy Search for Model Predictive Control With Application to Agile Drone Flight
Tarea: Controlar un dron cuadróptero para que lo pase a través de una serie de barras móviles rápidamente.
Algoritmo (texto): Search for Model Predictive Control (MPC) using policy search, with Gaussian and neural network policies.
Algoritmo (diccionario): MPC / NMPC; Policy search (PGPE, PoWER, gSDE)
Observaciones: state vector xt, control commands ut, and derivative of the current state ˙xt
Acciones: control commands for the quadrotor, discrete or continuous depending on the policy representation
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: standard MPC; trajectory sampling method
Resultado: The proposed controller achieved real-time control performance of a physical drone, outperforming a standard MPC and a trajectory sampling method.
Limitaciones: The method requires a large number of samples in real-time, which can be computationally and memory expensive to run on embedded systems.

Título: REINFORCEMENT LEARNING WITH SPARSE REWARDS USING GUIDANCE FROM OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION
Tarea: The agent learns trajectory tracking and obstacle avoidance for a mobile robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Learning Online with Guidance Offline (LOGO), which is a variant of Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO).
Observaciones: The agent observes state variables, with the possibility of incomplete or censored state information.
Acciones: Continuous actions, as the task involves trajectory tracking and obstacle avoidance.
Recompensa: The reward is sparse and defined by the task completion, with little fine-grain feedback on intermediate steps.
Simulador: MuJoCo and Gazebo simulators, as well as real-world TurtleBot experiments.
Entrenamiento: Not stated explicitly, but the paper discusses extensive experiments and evaluations.
Métricas: Performance improvement in each learning episode; Near-optimal policies found; Excellence in MuJoCo simulations and real-world TurtleBot experiments
Líneas base: State-of-the-art approaches; PofD algorithm
Sim2real: The method is tested on a physical robot, and the paper discusses transferring from simulation to the real robot.
Resultado: LOGO can attain nearly the same performance as an optimal algorithm trained with dense rewards, and shows excellent performance in trajectory tracking and obstacle avoidance tasks.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the behavior policy might not always offer an advantage, and the performance guarantees are based on certain assumptions.

Título: RLOC: Terrain-Aware Legged Locomotion Using Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control
Tarea: generate desired feet positions for dynamic locomotion over uneven terrain
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) policy, guided policy search (GPS)
Algoritmo (diccionario): Guided Policy Search; Policy search (PGPE, PoWER, gSDE)
Observaciones: robot state and terrain information
Acciones: low-level joint position commands, corrective feed-forward joint torques
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: contact-implicit optimization (CIO), differential dynamic programming (DDP), model-based control solutions, classical model-based controllers
Sim2real: domain randomization, transfer of policies from simulation to real robot
Resultado: RLOC framework demonstrated zero-shot generalization to the physical ANYmal C robot despite being trained in a simulator with ANYmal B, achieving high-level tracking of reference base velocity commands over complex uneven terrain
Limitaciones: training sample inefficiency, reality gap problem, need for precise reward function tuning, potential for undesired control behavior, limited to flat terrain simplifications, computational delays, need for exhaustive tuning of planning and control parameters, development time

Título: Reinforcement Learned Distributed Multi-Robot Navigation With Reciprocal Velocity Obstacle Shaped Rewards
Tarea: navegación de múltiples robots evitando colisiones en un espacio compartido.
Algoritmo (texto): actor-critic based DRL (Deep Reinforcement Learning) con BiGRUs (Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units)
Observaciones: posiciones y velocidades relativas de los robots y obstáculos, representados en términos de VO (Velocity Obstacle) y RVO (Reciprocal Velocity Obstacle) vectors
Acciones: incrementos de la velocidad actual en cada paso de tiempo, acciones continuas
Recompensa: función de recompensa basada en el área de RVO y el tiempo esperado de colisión, que fomenta el comportamiento de evitación de colisiones recíprocas
Entrenamiento: 10 horas en una computadora con CPU i7-9700 y GPU Nvidia GTX 1080
Métricas: tasa de éxito; tiempo de viaje; velocidad promedio
Líneas base: SARL; GA3C-CADRL; NH-ORCA
Sim2real: transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a la realidad
Resultado: Nuestro algoritmo RL-RVO tiene una tasa de éxito del 100% y un tiempo de viaje promedio de 83.75 iteraciones en el escenario circular con 8 robots, superando a NH-ORCA en tasa de éxito y tiempo de viaje.
Limitaciones: El algoritmo es sensible a la densidad de obstáculos y robots, y puede tener problemas con la representación de robots con diferentes números de entradas.

Título: Robot navigation in a crowd by integrating deep reinforcement learning and online planning
Tarea: Navigating a robot among pedestrians in a way that is time-efficient and collision-free.
Algoritmo (texto): SG-DQN, a graph-based deep Q-learning method with a social attention mechanism and dueling DQN architecture.
Algoritmo (diccionario): DQN; Dueling DQN; Atención; Variante de DQN
Observaciones: The agent observes the position, velocity, and radius of the robot and pedestrians, as well as the goal position, preferred velocity, and heading angle of the pedestrians.
Acciones: Discrete actions (stop action and 80 discrete actions for holonomic robots, which can be extended to car-like robots).
Recompensa: The reward function is designed to navigate the robot towards its goal, penalize collisions, and reward maintaining a safe distance from pedestrians. It includes three parts: Rg, Rc, and Rs.
Simulador: Crowd-Nav simulator for simple scenarios and a custom complex scenario simulator.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions training over episodes and a learning rate of 0.0005, discount factor of 0.9, and exploration rate decaying from 0.5 to 0.1 over 10,000 episodes.
Métricas: Average return; Navigation time; Discomfort rate
Líneas base: LM-SARL; G-GCNRL; previous state-of-the-art algorithms
Resultado: The proposed method helps the robot to better understand the crowd and achieve a high success rate of more than 0.99 in the crowd navigation task, outperforming state-of-the-art methods while requiring less than half of the computational cost.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method is trained in a simulated environment and may not perform as well in real-world scenarios due to the complexity of real crowds.

Título: TERP: Reliable Planning in Uneven Outdoor Environments using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: reliable robot navigation in uneven outdoor terrains
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Attention modules
Observaciones: elevation maps of the environment, robot pose, and goal
Acciones: discrete (waypoints)
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: Clearpath Husky robot created using ROS Melodic and Unity game engine
Entrenamiento: trained in a workstation with an Intel Xeon 3.6 GHz processor and an Nvidia Titan GPU
Métricas: Success Rate; Cumulative Elevation Gradient (CEG); Normalized Trajectory length; Goal Heading Deviation
Líneas base: Dynamic Window Approach (DW A); ego-graph; end-to-end Attn-DRL network
Resultado: TERP consistently outperforms other methods in terms of success rate, and CEG even in challenging high-elevation and city-curb environments. The computed stable trajectories possess longer trajectory lengths and higher deviations from the goal depending on the environment.
Limitaciones: The effective sensing point cloud percentage can be low especially near steep ditches due to the low reﬂectance of the LiDAR’s rays. In such cases, additional depth sensors need to be integrated to achieve better perception. In addition, boundaries between different surfaces may not be sensed by the elevation map. Using a fusion of RGB image data and point clouds could help address this problem.

Título: ARiADNE: A Reinforcement learning approach using Attention-based Deep Networks for Exploration
Tarea: autonomously explore and map an unknown environment as fast as possible
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based approach, using two attention-based neural networks
Observaciones: ot = (G′t,ψt), where G′t is the augmented graph based on the current collision-free graph Gt, and ψt is the robot current position
Acciones: select one neighboring node of its current position as the next viewpoint, discrete
Recompensa: composed of three parts: number of observed frontiers, punishment on the distance between the previous and new viewpoints, and a fixed finishing reward if the exploration task was completed
Simulador: Robot Operating System (ROS) simulations, with a real sensor model and a realistic low-level motion controller
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: state-of-the-art conventional methods
Resultado: outperforms both learning and non-learning state-of-the-art baselines in terms of average trajectory length to complete exploration in hundreds of simplified 2D indoor scenarios
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: A Comparison of PPO, TD3 and SAC Reinforcement Algorithms for Quadruped Walking Gait Generation
Tarea: generate a constant velocity walking gait for a quadruped robot
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)
Observaciones: body position, body quaternion, foot contact sensors, actuator position, actuator velocity, actuator load, IMUs on the body and legs
Acciones: actuator target positions (discrete)
Recompensa: encourages a stable forward walking gait at a target velocity and orientation, with penalties for deviations and actions
Entrenamiento: three million steps, repeated five times for each algorithm configuration combination
Métricas: average forward velocity (m/s); average forward velocity variance; average lateral velocity (m/s); average lateral velocity variance; quaternion root mean square deviation (RMSD)
Líneas base: TD3; PPO; SAC
Resultado: SAC achieved the highest average reward in configurations v2, v3, and v4, while PPO performed better with smaller state spaces. TD3 had a significantly steeper learning curve but took longer to converge.
Limitaciones: The study does not address the transfer of learned policies to real robots, which is a limitation given the focus on domain randomization.

Título: A Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework With High Efficiency and Generalization for Fast and Safe Navigation
Tarea: fast and safe navigation for mobile robots
Algoritmo (texto): hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework, with low-level DQN and high-level DQN policies
Observaciones: laser sensor data, robot pose, and global map
Acciones: linear and angular velocities, discrete or continuous, depending on the policy
Recompensa: not stated explicitly, but related to reaching the goal and avoiding obstacles
Entrenamiento: 800 thousand steps, 10 Hz control frequency, 22 hours theoretically, 7 days practically
Métricas: success rate; motion efficiency; average speed
Líneas base: traditional nonlearning map-based methods; DRL-based baselines; classical and RL
Sim2real: fine-tuning for acceleration, adding noises to actions
Resultado: The hierarchical DRL framework achieved a success rate of 100% and motion efficiency of 0.25 m/s, outperforming the traditional move-base method which had a success rate of 93% and lower motion efficiency.
Limitaciones: The method is sensitive to the initial location of the robot and may fail if the robot is too close to obstacles at the start.

Título: Advanced Skills through Multiple Adversarial Motion Priors in Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: The agent learns to perform multiple skills such as four-legged locomotion, ducking, standing up, navigating on two legs, and sitting down.
Algoritmo (texto): Multi-AMP, a variant of Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) that allows for multiple, discretely switchable styles.
Observaciones: Linear and angular base velocity, gravity direction, base's height above ground, joint position and velocity, and position of the wheels relative to the robot’s base-frame.
Acciones: Continuous actions, as the robot performs complex movements like standing up, ducking, and navigating.
Recompensa: The reward is defined as a combination of task rewards and style rewards. Task rewards are related to the performance of the policy with respect to the command, while style rewards motivate the agent to extract the style of the motion priors. For the sit-down skill, the policy is trained using a reversed stand-up motion to avoid high impulses in the real robot’s knees.
Entrenamiento: 4096 environments in parallel, 300 epochs longer for the 3-style policy compared to the single-task policy
Métricas: Stand-up task metrics; Sit-down task metrics; Navigation task metrics
Líneas base: Policies that exclusively learn a single task (baseline)
Sim2real: Actuator model for the leg joints to bridge the sim-to-real gap, timed pushes, and joint-velocity-based trajectory termination.
Resultado: The Multi-AMP approach learns to achieve all goals equally well as more specialized policies that learn fewer tasks, with the sit-down skill learned from a reversed stand-up motion to avoid high impulses in the real robot’s knees.
Limitaciones: More time is required to generate motion priors, which is not always available for specific tasks.

Título: Asynchronous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Real-Time Multi-Robot Cooperative Exploration
Tarea: real-time multi-robot cooperative exploration
Algoritmo (texto): Async-MAPPO (an asynchronous variant of MAPPO)
Observaciones: local information, states, observations, and macro actions
Acciones: discrete actions, with action delays
Recompensa: accumulated discounted reward based on macro actions and atomic actions
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical planning-based methods; synchronous RL methods; fastest planning-based method with 2 Mecanum steering robots
Sim2real: action delay randomization in simulation to model real-world delays
Resultado: ACE reduces 10.07% real-world exploration time compared with the synchronous RL baseline and 33.86% compared with the fastest planning-based method with 2 Mecanum steering robots.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method is not yet fully tested in real-world scenarios and that the communication efficiency could be further improved.

Título: Barkour: Benchmarking Animal-level Agility with Quadruped Robots
Tarea: complete a parkour course with various obstacles including weave poles, jumps, and an A-frame, within a time limit.
Algoritmo (texto): on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) and Transformer-based generalist policy
Observaciones: heightfield, proprioceptive states, actions, and velocity commands
Acciones: discrete motor angles from a nominal standing pose
Recompensa: encourages fast completion of tasks and low energy consumption, with penalties for errors and time overruns
Entrenamiento: 17,636 simulated episodes, equivalent to 57.58 hours of robot time, across four different types of environments
Líneas base: specialist policies; Locomotion-Transformer policy
Resultado: The Locomotion-Transformer policy completed the course at half the speed of a dog, demonstrating the effectiveness of the generalist approach.
Limitaciones: The benchmark and methods are limited by the sim-to-real transfer gap, and the hardware optimization required for agile movements.

Título: Benchmarking Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Autonomous Navigation
Tarea: autonomous robot navigation, i.e., moving a robot from one point to another without colliding with any obstacle
Algoritmo (texto): TD3, SAC, DDPG, Lagrangian-based safe RL, model-based RL (Dyna-style, MPC, MBPO), domain randomization
Algoritmo (diccionario): Dyna-Q; DDPG; TD3; SAC; MBPO; Aleatorización del dominio; PPO/TRPO-Lagrangiano; RL seguro (genérico); MPC / NMPC
Observaciones: sensors from LiDAR scans, relative goal position in the robot frame
Acciones: continuous linear and angular velocity (vt, ωt)
Recompensa: defined as +bf · 1(dt < ds) +bp · (dt−1 − dt) − bc · ct, with bf for success, bp for local progress, and bc for collisions
Entrenamiento: TD3 with distributed training pipelines, 3 independent runs
Métricas: success rate; average survival time; average traversal time
Líneas base: classical navigation systems (MLP, Lagrangian method, MPC, DW A)
Resultado: TD3 combined with different techniques achieved success rates of 65% to 82% in static and dynamic environments, with improvements in safety and generalization to unseen environments
Limitaciones: lack of safety guarantees, explainability, and generalizability in learning-based navigation systems, high requirement for sample efficiency, and difficulty in assessing the state of the art

Título: CAJun: Continuous Adaptive Jumping using a Learned Centroidal Controller
Tarea: el agente aprende a realizar saltos continuos con distancias de salto adaptativas.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) para entrenar la política centroidal, con un controlador de piernas basado en programación cuadrática (QP) para optimizar comandos de motor.
Observaciones: la posición del pie en swing, la frecuencia de paso, y la velocidad de la base
Acciones: comandos de motor para las piernas de swing y stance, acciones discretas
Recompensa: no se especifica directamente, pero se menciona que se utiliza PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) para entrenar la política centroidal.
Entrenamiento: menos de 20 minutos en una GPU Nvidia RTX 2080Ti
Líneas base: TWiRL [19]; Barkour [3]; Margolis et al. [30]; Walk-These-Ways [17]
Resultado: CAJun puede realizar saltos continuos con distancias de salto adaptativas, cruzando un agujero de 70cm, lo que es más del 40% más ancho que los métodos existentes, en menos de 20 minutos de entrenamiento en una GPU.
Limitaciones: CAJun aún no puede aterrizar con precisión en la ubicación deseada y no utiliza la percepción, solo ajusta las distancias de salto según comandos ad hoc.

Título: Controlling the Solo12 quadruped robot with deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: follow a given reference velocity
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with a multi-layer perceptron policy network
Observaciones: joint angles, joint velocities, joint target errors, base orientation, linear velocity, angular velocity
Acciones: displacements of the reference joint angles, discrete
Recompensa: based on the squared Euclidean distance between the 3D vector Vx,y,wz and the 3D velocity command V cmd, with penalties for foot clearance, foot slip, base orientation and velocity, joint pose, and power loss, and a smoothness penalty
Entrenamiento: 10,000 training iterations, 300 million collected samples, 100 steps per episode, 10 kHz low-level loop on the real robot, 100 Hz policy network frequency
Métricas: average power consumption; velocity error; base height
Líneas base: classical control methods; model-predictive control (MPC)
Resultado: The learned controller achieved a velocity tracking error of 0.079 ± 0.054 m/s (7.9%) and a power consumption of 17.7 W with a base height of 0.23 m, and the power consumption decreased by 30% when the power weight cE was increased to 4.0, with a slight increase in velocity error to 0.145 ± 0.091 m/s (14.5%)
Limitaciones: The method requires a large number of training iterations and samples, and the performance of the controller is sensitive to the choice of the power weight cE.

Título: Creating a Dynamic Quadrupedal Robotic Goalkeeper with Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: perform soccer goalkeeping tasks, including intercepting a fast-moving ball using dynamic locomotion maneuvers
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for control policies, and model-free reinforcement learning for the high-level planning policy
Observaciones: end-effector trajectories represented by Bézier curves, robot's sensor readings (motor positions, base rotation, and actions in the past 15 timesteps)
Acciones: 12-dimensional action specifying target motor positions for each joint, discrete skill selection
Recompensa: encourages end-effector tracking, imitation of reference motion, and gait stability; also includes a reward for stopping the ball and minimizing the distance between the end-effector and the ball
Entrenamiento: 300 timesteps per episode, 10 seconds, 30 Hz for control policies, 10 Hz for planning policy, trained with PPO
Métricas: save rate of random shots in the real world
Líneas base: classical control methods; RL methods for low-level locomotion control
Resultado: 87.5% successful interception rate of random shots in the real world, compared to human goalkeepers with an average save rate of around 69%.
Limitaciones: The method relies on sim-to-real transfer, which may not always be perfect; the robot's performance may vary in different real-world scenarios.

Título: DRL-VO: Learning to Navigate Through Crowded Dynamic Scenes Using Velocity Obstacles
Tarea: Navegar a través de espacios con obstáculos estáticos y densas multitudes de peatones.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) con un nuevo término de recompensa basado en obstáculos de velocidad.
Observaciones: Lidar, datos cinemáticos de peatones cercanos, punto sub-objetivo.
Acciones: Ángulo de dirección y velocidad lineal, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: Incluye términos para alcanzar el objetivo, evitar colisiones pasivas, suavidad del camino y dirección activa de la dirección de navegación.
Entrenamiento: 250,000 pasos de entrenamiento en un servidor Nvidia DGX-1, 300,000 pasos en un ordenador de escritorio.
Líneas base: Control basado en modelos; Aprendizaje supervisado; DRL basado en modelos; CNN basado en modelos
Sim2real: Transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a realidad.
Resultado: El control DRL-VO logró una mejor balance entre evasión de colisiones y velocidad (tasa de éxito más alta y velocidad promedio más rápida) que los métodos basados en modelos y de aprendizaje supervisado, y se generalizó mejor a diferentes tamaños de multitudes y entornos no vistos.
Limitaciones: El control DRL-VO requiere un servidor de entrenamiento potente y no se ha optimizado para diferentes plataformas de robot.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Multi-Robot Exploration With Macro Actions
Tarea: explorar un entorno desconocido para generar un mapa global mientras se consideran las intenciones de los compañeros de equipo durante las interrupciones de comunicación.
Algoritmo (texto): Macro Action Decentralized Exploration Network (MADE-Net), que utiliza multi-agente deep reinforcement learning (DRL)
Robot: no se especifican nombres de plataformas de robots
Observaciones: posiciones de los robots, mapas locales, posiciones de los objetivos de exploración
Acciones: acciones discretas (macroacciones)
Recompensa: se maximiza la combinación de área explorada sobre la distancia total recorrida en cada paso de tiempo durante la exploración
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona la utilización de entornos paralelos durante el entrenamiento
Métricas: tiempo de exploración; distancia total recorrida; interacciones locales entre robots; tasa de exploración
Líneas base: métodos clásicos; DRL basados en acciones primitivas
Resultado: MADE-Net superó todos los métodos de referencia en términos de tiempo de exploración, distancia total recorrida, interacciones locales entre robots y tasa de exploración en diferentes grados de interrupciones de comunicación.
Limitaciones: el método no se ha probado en un entorno físico real, y solo se ha aplicado a tareas de manejo de materiales y entrega de almacenes en entornos conocidos.

Título: Demonstrating A Walk in the Park: Learning to Walk in 20 Minutes With Model-Free Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learning to walk in various real-world terrains
Algoritmo (texto): Q-function actor-critic methods, based on DroQ which extends SAC with Dropout and Layer Normalization
Observaciones: state space, action space, including PD targets
Acciones: low-level control, such as PD targets, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: 20,000 samples, 0.33 hours
Líneas base: Wu et al. [23]; Smith et al. [24]; Kumar et al. [16]; Rudin et al. [22]; Lee et al. [25]; Ha et al. [27]; Haarnoja et al. [28]; Yang et al. [29]
Resultado: The A1 quadrupedal robot learned to walk in 20 minutes across a range of environments, including indoor and outdoor terrains.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the key is not any one particular choice but the general principle of augmenting actor-critic RL with regularization or normalization.

Título: DreamWaQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn quadrupedal locomotion with implicit terrain imagination using only proprioception.
Algoritmo (texto): proximal policy optimization (PPO) with an asymmetric actor-critic architecture.
Observaciones: temporal partial observations from proprioceptive sensors (IMU, joint encoders) and a context vector.
Acciones: 12-dimensional vector of desired joint angles, discrete.
Recompensa: reward function includes tracking linear and angular velocity, stability, joint accelerations, power distribution, and body height.
Simulador: simulator for training, not specified which one.
Entrenamiento: not stated, but mentions one training phase for H=5.
Líneas base: behavior cloning (BC); grid-adaptive curriculum
Resultado: The robot was able to walk through challenging terrains such as hills and yards with a total reward of -1.0 for body height and -0.01 for foot clearance, demonstrating robustness and durability.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method relies on a complex pipeline and that the policy might be unable to explore failure states in the early stage of learning.

Título: Emergent Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Future Wireless Networks
Tarea: collaboratively complete a task in a partially observable environment, such as traffic control, resource management, and smart city applications.
Algoritmo (texto): EC-MARL (Emergent Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning), which combines MARL with learning communication protocols.
Observaciones: agents' d-dimensional restricted view of the true state space, including messages sent on a shared channel.
Acciones: discrete actions and messages, with policies that can be functions of their entire trajectory of experience.
Recompensa: individual rewards for each agent, with a joint objective for the group.
Simulador: traffic intersection simulator, House3D framework, and other simulated environments.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: Emergent communication between agents makes the traffic fluid without collisions, and EC-MARL has been shown to be robust against noise.
Limitaciones: scalability, non-stationarity, convergence, measuring the effectiveness of emergent communication, effect of noisy communications, communication cost, understanding semantics of emergent communication, compositionality, generalization and interoperability of the communication protocol, learning a well-structured communication protocol, and emergent communication with contextual reasoning.

Título: Federated Reinforcement Learning for Collective Navigation of Robotic Swarms
Tarea: El agente aprende a navegar y evitar colisiones en un grupo de robots mientras evita obstáculos.
Algoritmo (texto): DDPG, con Federated Learning (FL) para la estrategia FLDDPG
Observaciones: Distancia al objetivo, lecturas de 24 sensores láser, velocidad translacional y rotacional, recompensa por lograr el objetivo, evitar colisiones y evitar obstáculos
Acciones: Velocidad translacional y rotacional, acciones discretas
Recompensa: La recompensa se basa en lograr el objetivo, evitar colisiones y evitar obstáculos, con un factor de recompensa para la navegación y una penalización para las colisiones.
Simulador: Entorno simulado y un área real de 4x3m²
Entrenamiento: 120 episodios, 1024 pasos por episodio, 4 robots, factor de descuento 0.99, factor de actualización suave 0.5, recompensa por lograr el objetivo 100.0, penalización por colisión -100.0, factor de recompensa por progreso 4.0, parámetro de penalización por acercamiento log(2)
Métricas: recompensa promedio por episodio; interferencia catastrófica; número de agentes fallidos
Líneas base: IDDPG; SNDDPG; SEDDPG
Sim2real: Transferencia de entrenamiento simulado a un robot real
Resultado: FLDDPG resultó en mayor robustez y generalización en comparación con las estrategias de base, con un volumen de datos de 132 MB para entrenamiento con FLDDPG.
Limitaciones: El entrenamiento con FLDDPG requiere un volumen de datos limitado, lo que puede hacer que el entrenamiento sea vulnerable debido a la inestabilidad de la comunicación.

Título: Federated Transfer Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
Tarea: collision avoidance for autonomous driving cars
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) with Federated Transfer Reinforcement Learning (FTRL)
Observaciones: LIDAR distance data
Acciones: continuous steering actions
Recompensa: defined as r−c∗cond[min(st+1)<d ]− 2d−md, where r is a positive base reward value, c is a positive penalty value for collision events, d is a positive value for casting exponential penalty on md, and md is the number of the dimensions of the LIDAR distance data
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: average distance with obstacles; collision counts
Líneas base: DDPG
Resultado: FTRL can transfer knowledge online, with 27% increase in the average distance with obstacles and 42% decrease in the collision counts
Limitaciones: The framework is not designed for any specific RL method, and the training process is not detailed.

Título: GLiDE: Generalizable Quadrupedal Locomotion in Diverse Environments with a Centroidal Model
Tarea: quadrupedal locomotion, including flat terrain gaits, stepping stone scenarios, balance beam locomotion, and two-legged balancing
Algoritmo (texto): actor-critic algorithm optimized with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: body state (excluding displacement), stance foot position or swing-leg target position, and normalized phase of each foot
Acciones: body linear and angular accelerations, realized by ground reaction forces (GRFs)
Recompensa: based on the rigid body state without concern for many of the issues that lead to more complex reward for RL solutions based on a full model
Simulador: centroidal dynamics model, simulated on a GPU for parallel simulations
Entrenamiento: 1-2 hours of training, with 1600 simulations in parallel
Líneas base: MPC, DeepGait, Laikago RL, Anymal RL
Resultado: The method successfully learned control policies for multiple gaits, stepping stone scenarios, balance beam locomotion, and two-legged balancing, and was able to transfer to a physical A1 robot
Limitaciones: The method relies on a custom parallel QP solver and may not be as general as full-model RL methods, but it can handle complex terrains more efficiently

Título: Intelligent Control of Multilegged Robot Smooth Motion: A Review
Tarea: The task the agent learns is to achieve smooth motion in multilegged robots, including motion planning, leg compliance control, motion stability, foot force PDF control, and intelligent switching control of gait.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) control, including variants like Adaptive Variable Impedance Control (A VIC) and Model Predictive Control (MPC).
Observaciones: Foot force and landing point
Acciones: Continuous actions for motion control
Recompensa: Not stated
Simulador: Quad-SDK, a software development kit for quadrupedal robots
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Traditional control methods (e.g., Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC), Central Pattern Generator (CPG)), classical control methods (e.g., Model Predictive Control (MPC))
Resultado: The study achieved over 100 Hz update rate for gait cycles using a novel hot-start method with 16 elements/cycle, and developed a more accurate terrain estimator that can precisely model the terrain based on proprioceptive perception.
Limitaciones: The study acknowledges limitations such as the complexity of robot structure design, control precision, and external environmental limitations.

Título: Intelligent Robot Path Planning and Navigation based on Reinforcement Learning and Adaptive Control
Tarea: path planning and navigation of intelligent robots
Algoritmo (texto): Q-learning, with adaptive control as a complementary method
Observaciones: state of the environment, location of the robot, environment characteristics
Acciones: discrete actions like forward, backward, left turn, right turn
Recompensa: positive rewards for reaching a target location, negative rewards for colliding with an obstacle
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical methods and other reinforcement learning methods
Resultado: the method based on reinforcement learning and adaptive control achieves significant improvements in path planning and navigation of intelligent robots
Limitaciones: computational complexity of reinforcement learning methods limits their real-time performance and efficiency, adaptive control methods face challenges in modelling uncertainty and parameter tuning

Título: Intention Aware Robot Crowd Navigation with Attention-Based Interaction Graph
Tarea: safe and intention-aware robot navigation in dense and interactive crowds
Algoritmo (texto): model-free RL with attention mechanisms, using a recurrent graph neural network
Observaciones: robot's position, velocity, goal position, maximum speed, heading angle, and radius of the robot base
Acciones: continuous, with a maximum speed of 1m/s
Recompensa: a combination of a potential-based reward and a prediction reward to penalize the robot for intruding into the predicted social zones of humans
Simulador: 2D environment with 12m x 12m space, simulating a dense crowd with up to 20 humans
Entrenamiento: 2× 10^7 timesteps with a learning rate of 4× 10^-5
Líneas base: ORCA; SF; DS-RNN; GST, no HH attn; Oracle, HH attn
Sim2real: technique used to transfer from simulation to the real robot, or 'not stated'
Resultado: Our method outperforms previous works in terms of navigation performance and social awareness, achieving a success rate of 94% and an intrusion time ratio of 3.06 in the most challenging environment.
Limitaciones: simulated human behaviors are far from realistic and the assumption that humans never react to the robot does not hold

Título: Learning-Based Design and Control for Quadrupedal Robots With Parallel-Elastic Actuators
Tarea: Optimizar el diseño de un mecanismo paralelo-elasático para un robot quadrúpedo y optimizar el controlador de locomoción.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) y Optimización Bayesiana (BO)
Observaciones: Posición de las articulaciones, ángulo de la articulación del rodilla, radio de los ejes mayor y menor, ángulo inicial de la elíptica
Acciones: Acciones continuas, torque en las articulaciones
Recompensa: Eficiencia de torque-cuadrado y rendimiento de seguimiento
Entrenamiento: No se especifica
Métricas: Eficiencia de torque-cuadrado; Rendimiento de seguimiento; Tiempo de operación en terreno llano
Líneas base: Controlador de locomoción basado en RL; Diseño de mecanismos basado en heurísticas
Sim2real: Transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a la realidad
Resultado: El nuevo sistema mejora la eficiencia de torque-cuadrado del robot en un 33% y reduce el torque máximo de las articulaciones en un 30% sin comprometer el rendimiento de seguimiento, lo que resulta en un 11% más de tiempo de operación en terreno llano.
Limitaciones: El método requiere un entrenamiento exhaustivo y la transferencia de aprendizaje de simulación a la realidad puede ser inestable.

Título: Learning Bipedal Walking for Humanoids With Current Feedback
Tarea: Learning bipedal walking for a humanoid robot (HRP-5P) to achieve dynamic stability.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with feedforward Multi-Layered Perceptrons (MLPs) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTMs) networks, with targeted dynamics randomization.
Observaciones: Joint positions, joint velocities, roll and pitch orientation, angular velocity of the root (pelvis), motor-level torque signal, walking mode (standing, stepping in-place, walking forward), reference value depending on the mode, clock signal.
Acciones: Desired positions of the actuated joints in the robot’s legs, discrete (low PD gains for joint tracking).
Recompensa: Promotes a symmetrical bipedal walking gait, root velocity, orientation, and height, safe and realistic motion, with specific terms for feet ground reaction forces, body speeds, root linear velocity, root yaw velocity, root height, upper body posture, and joint velocities.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Qualitative performance compared to an open-source model-based controller for walking on uneven terrain
Líneas base: open-source model-based controller
Sim2real: By simulating a degraded torque-tracking environment during training and observing the applied motor torque or equivalently, measured motor currents on the real robot.
Resultado: The RL policy successfully achieved forward walking, stepping and turning in-place, and quite standing on the real HRP-5P robot, demonstrating robustness to uneven terrain.
Limitaciones: The sim2real gap is significantly a result of imperfect current tracking on the real robot that leads to a mismatch in the desired and applied torque, and the method relies on the HRP-5P robot's specific motor control system.

Título: Learning Modular Robot Control Policies
Tarea: Controlar robots modulares para locomoción en diferentes diseños.
Algoritmo (texto): Model-based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) con Guided Policy Search (GPS) y redes neuronales de grafos (GNNs).
Algoritmo (diccionario): Model-based RL (genérico); Guided Policy Search; Policy search (PGPE, PoWER, gSDE)
Robot: No se especifica un robot específico, se menciona 'robots modulares'.
Observaciones: Posición y tipo de módulo (ej. pierna, rueda guiada, cuerpo).
Acciones: Acciones de control para moverse (discretas o continuas, no se especifica).
Recompensa: No se especifica cómo se define la recompensa, pero se menciona que se usa para entrenar la política.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se prueba en muchos diseños adicionales.
Métricas: Transferencia a nuevos diseños sin aprendizaje adicional
Líneas base: Control manual; Model-free RL; Model-based MPC
Sim2real: No se especifica una técnica específica, pero se menciona transferencia a robots reales.
Resultado: Se logró transferencia a un orden de magnitud más de diseños nuevos que no se vieron durante el entrenamiento.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que la transferencia entre diseños con estructuras repetidas pero no necesariamente la misma topología puede ser limitada.

Título: Learning Torque Control for Quadrupedal Locomotion
Tarea: traverse various terrains and resist external disturbances while following user-specified commands
Algoritmo (texto): proximal policy optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: base linear and angular velocities, orientation, joint positions and velocities, last action, and user commands
Acciones: 12 unscaled joint torques, continuous
Recompensa: encourages following user commands, natural looking gaits, and robustness to disturbances, with specific terms for base linear and angular velocity, orientation, joint torque, joint acceleration, feet air time, collision, and action rate
Entrenamiento: 4096 parallel environments, 200 Hz, 15 hours of training time
Métricas: learning curves; traversing different terrains; resisting external disturbances
Líneas base: position-based RL policy
Resultado: The proposed torque-based RL policy achieved higher rewards and was more robust to disturbances compared to the position-based RL policy, successfully traversing various terrains and recovering from external disturbances.
Limitaciones: Determining nominal torques is difficult for torque control, and the action scale needs to be carefully chosen to balance exploration and exploitation.

Título: Learning and Adapting Agile Locomotion Skills by Transferring Experience
Tarea: Learning agile locomotion skills such as jumping over obstacles and bipedal navigation.
Algoritmo (texto): off-policy actor-critic algorithm DroQ, a variant of SAC with dropout regularization and layer normalization
Observaciones: root orientation, joint angles, base displacement, and previous actions
Acciones: target joint angles for the 12 actuated degrees-of-freedom, continuous
Recompensa: reward function defined with minimal shaping, encouraging forward movement, proper orientation, and joint velocity control
Entrenamiento: 3 runs, 1 million steps, hardware not stated
Líneas base: RL from scratch; Source Policy
Resultado: TWiRL achieved 2x the return compared to RL from scratch, with policies that are agile, robust, and safe for execution on physical hardware.
Limitaciones: The method is not well-suited to learning from scratch with RL, and the source policy data may not always be available or optimal for the target task.

Título: Learning to View: Decision Transformers for Active Object Detection
Tarea: learn a motion policy to control a mobile robot to obtain images that maximize the detection quality of an object.
Algoritmo (texto): Decision Transformer with online fine-tuning, based on supervised learning.
Observaciones: bounding box of selected object, RGB image, depth image
Acciones: discrete actions, selected from the set A = {"-#" - "!" - "" - "" - ""}
Recompensa: detection score of the object in the RGB image, with 𝛿 set to 0 if the prediction is wrong
Entrenamiento: 10 episodes of online data collection, with a total buffer size of N
Líneas base: expert policy; pure offline RL methods
Resultado: Our method outperforms all baselines, including expert policy and pure offline RL methods.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a heuristic expert policy that may not be optimal, and the model may suffer from training instability.

Título: Local Path Planning: Dynamic Window Approach With Q-Learning Considering Congestion Environments for Mobile Robot
Tarea: local path planning in dynamic environments, specifically in factories and warehouses
Algoritmo (texto): Q-learning for adjusting weight coefficients in the Dynamic Window Approach (DQDW A)
Observaciones: robot states, environmental conditions, and actions of weight coefficients
Acciones: discrete (weight coefficients selected from a set of values)
Recompensa: defined as a combination of rewards related to goal achievement, distance from the goal, and distance from obstacles
Entrenamiento: 30,000 updates of the Q-table, not stated training budget or hardware
Métricas: success rate; time; trajectory length (TL); posture displacement (PD)
Líneas base: DW A I, DW A II, DW A III, Conventional DW A with Q-learning (CDQ), DQDW A
Resultado: DQDW A achieved the highest success rate and the smallest trajectory length and posture displacement in both learned and unlearned environments, outperforming other methods in terms of efficiency and safety.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: METRA: Scalable Unsupervised RL with Metric-Aware Abstraction
Tarea: The agent learns to discover diverse behaviors in complex, high-dimensional environments, including locomotion and manipulation tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): Metric-Aware Abstraction (METRA), a variant of reinforcement learning that uses a skill policy and a representation function to learn behaviors in a metric-aware latent space.
Observaciones: Pixel-based images for Quadruped and Humanoid, state-based for Ant and HalfCheetah, and a pixel-based version of Kitchen.
Acciones: Continuous for Quadruped and Humanoid, discrete for Ant, HalfCheetah, and Kitchen.
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the reward is related to the state/task coverage and task performance.
Simulador: Gym, DeepMind Control (DMC) Suite, and a pixel-based version of Kitchen from Gupta et al. (2019); Mendonca et al. (2021).
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the experiments cover a range of steps and episodes across different environments.
Métricas: Policy State Coverage; Policy Task Coverage; Return
Líneas base: DIAYN; DADS; CIC; LSD; ICM; RND; Plan2Explore; APT; LBS; APS; LEXA
Resultado: METRA exhibits the best state/task coverage across all environments and the best or near-best performance in downstream tasks, discovering diverse locomotion skills in pixel-based Quadruped and Humanoid.
Limitaciones: METRA might be overly conservative in highly asymmetric environments and might restrict the diversity of behaviors to some degree.

Título: Mobile Service Robot Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: planear rutas eficientes para un robot de servicio móvil en un entorno dinámico.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Q-Learning (DQL) con un algoritmo de transferencia de aprendizaje βββ-decay.
Observaciones: topología del mapa del entorno
Acciones: acciones discretas (movimientos en el entorno)
Recompensa: recompensas basadas en la eficiencia del camino, evitando ubicaciones visitadas previamente, llegando a destinos y alcanzando un estado desconocido.
Entrenamiento: 2200 episodios para el entorno de casa, más de 10,000 episodios para el entorno de hospital, hardware no especificado
Métricas: tasa de éxito de entrenamiento; tasa de éxito de prueba; tiempo de inicio de salto; tiempo hasta el umbral; tiempo hasta la convergencia
Líneas base: agente de aprendizaje sin transferencia
