Resultado: El agente de aprendizaje por refuerzo basado en DQL aprendió todas las rutas basadas en el mapa topológico inicial de diferentes entornos de servicio con una tasa de éxito de más del 98%.
Limitaciones: El tiempo de convergencia puede ser largo, especialmente en entornos más grandes.

Título: Multi-Target Pursuit by a Decentralized Heterogeneous UAV Swarm using Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: multi-target pursuit-evasion
Algoritmo (texto): Role-based Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG)
Observaciones: agent's position, velocity, and the state of obstacles
Acciones: discrete actions for movement commands
Recompensa: penalties for collisions, rewards for tracking targets, and exploration
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: average agent rewards; distance to targets
Líneas base: original MADDPG algorithm
Resultado: The proposed role-based MADDPG algorithm was able to track multiple targets and explore the environment, with an average minimum distance to targets of 0.4616 m in simulation and 0.4983 m in real-world experiments.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a specific hardware setup and may not be easily transferable to other platforms.

Título: Multiagent Soft Actor-Critic Based Hybrid Motion Planner for Mobile Robots
Tarea: multi-robot collaborative navigation task with preset target points
Algoritmo (texto): multi-agent soft actor-critic (MASAC) with minimal snap trajectory optimization
Observaciones: local observations, state variables
Acciones: discrete actions, continuous actions
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: unknown 3-robot fully interaction planning scenario, 6-robot and 12-robot planning scenarios
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: average total distance; average total time; average total reward; collision numbers; success rate
Líneas base: MATD3; MAAC; ORCA
Resultado: MASAC has better comprehensive waypoints searching performance and is closer to the performance of the ideal ORCA algorithm compared to MAAC and MATD3, with a success rate of 93.592% within limited timesteps.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the perfect perception ability of robots and the homogeneous nature of all robots.

Título: OPT-Mimic: Imitation of Optimized Trajectories for Dynamic Quadruped Behaviors
Tarea: Imitar movimientos dinámicos generados por optimización de trayectorias para un robot cuadrúpedo.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: Joint angles and angular velocities, base orientation as a quaternion, and phase.
Acciones: Residual joint angles, discrete
Recompensa: Not stated
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Classical methods (Trajectory Optimization)
Resultado: The method successfully transferred learned behaviors from simulation to the physical Solo 8 robot, achieving agile behaviors such as trot, front hop, 180 backflip, and biped stepping.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a simplified model for trajectory optimization, which may not capture all dynamics of the full-order model. The transfer from simulation to real robot is not explicitly detailed.

Título: Orbit: A Unified Simulation Framework for Interactive Robot Learning Environments
Tarea: The agent learns manipulation tasks such as opening a cabinet, folding cloth, and reorganizing a room, as well as locomotion tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement learning (RL) policies, not stated if a specific algorithm is used.
Robot: ANYmal (quadruped robot) and various manipulator platforms, not stated if specific models are used.
Observaciones: The agent observes the environment through various sensors including RGBD, semantic, LiDAR, and contact sensors.
Acciones: The agent outputs actions that control the robot's manipulation or locomotion, discrete or continuous depending on the task.
Recompensa: The reward is defined based on the task completion, not stated with more detail.
Simulador: NVIDIA Isaac Sim, a high-fidelity physics engine with support for rigid and deformable body simulation, ray-tracing, and real-time rendering.
Entrenamiento: Training is done in minutes using GPU-based parallelization, not stated with specific numbers of steps, episodes, or hours.
Líneas base: Various simulation frameworks including MetaWorld, RoboSuite, DoorGym, DEDO, RLBench, iGibson, Habitat 2.0, SoftGym, ThreeDWorld, ManiSkill2, ManipulatorThor, and IsaacGymEnvs.
Sim2real: Sim-to-real transfer of a locomotion policy for the quadruped robot, ANYmal, is demonstrated.
Resultado: ORBIT is able to obtain up to ∼10x and ∼3x the throughput for rigid and deformable body manipulation tasks respectively compared to existing frameworks.
Limitaciones: Not stated.

Título: RL + Model-Based Control: Using On-Demand Optimal Control to Learn Versatile Legged Locomotion
Tarea: Generar acciones articulares para imitar movimientos de referencia generados por control óptimo basado en modelos (MBOC) en robots quadrúpedos.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) con imitación de movimientos, basado en Model-based Optimal Control (MBOC).
Observaciones: Estado del robot (velocidad corporal, tipo de zancada, fase de contacto, observación del estado del robot).
Acciones: Acciones articulares, discretas o continuas, dependiendo del controlador de gait.
Recompensa: La recompensa mide la similitud entre el estado del robot y los movimientos de referencia generados por el MBOC.
Simulador: Entorno simulado que captura dinámicas corporales completas.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se utilizan dos robots diferentes.
Líneas base: Model-based Optimal Control (MBOC), RL basado en imitación de movimientos.
Sim2real: No se menciona ninguna técnica de transferencia de simulación a real.
Resultado: El método logra imitar movimientos de referencia generados por MBOC con distintos estilos de zancada y velocidades, y se muestra su capacidad para adaptarse a terrenos desiguales.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que el modelo de VHIPM no representa adecuadamente los movimientos de rotación del cuerpo ni la locomoción en terrenos desiguales, pero se compensa con la flexibilidad de RL.

Título: Reaching the limit in autonomous racing: Optimal control versus reinforcement learning
Tarea: fly a quadrotor through a sequence of gates in a given order in minimum time
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with policy-based approach
Robot: nominal drone model, realistic drone model, real-world racing drone
Observaciones: state of the drone, including its position, velocity, and orientation
Acciones: continuous control commands for the drone
Recompensa: gate progress objective, directly optimizing a task-level objective
Simulador: simulated environments with varying settings, including nominal and realistic drone models
Entrenamiento: trained in simulation, in minutes on a standard workstation
Líneas base: Trajectory Tracking; Contouring Control
Sim2real: trained purely in simulation, transferred to the real world zero-shot
Resultado: The RL policy achieved a peak acceleration greater than 12 g and a peak velocity of 108 km/h, outperforming both OC methods in terms of success rate and lap time, especially in the presence of unmodeled dynamics.
Limitaciones: The RL policy is trained purely in simulation, which may not fully capture real-world dynamics and uncertainties.

Título: Reinforcement Learning of CPG-Regulated Locomotion Controller for a Soft Snake Robot
Tarea: learn a goal-tracking locomotion controller for a soft snake robot using a combination of reinforcement learning and central pattern generators (CPGs).
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Free-response Oscillation Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization Option-Critics with Central Pattern Generator (FOC-PPOC-CPG)
Observaciones: position of the center of mass (COM) of the snake’s head, planar displacement vector, distance traveled, instantaneous planar velocity vector, angle between vector ρg(t) and vector v(t), and the locomotion speed
Acciones: discrete tonic inputs to the CPG system, which are then transformed into pressure inputs to pneumatic actuators of the soft snake robot, actions are discrete
Recompensa: a weighted sum over the robot’s instantaneous speed, deviation angle, and total traveled distance on a fixed straight line at the terminating time T, with a better-fitted configuration supposed to maintain oscillating locomotion and reach faster locomotion speed along the original heading direction at time T, with a smaller deviation between the robot’s heading direction and the goal direction, and with overall a longer traveled distance along the robot’s heading direction
Simulador: a physics-based simulator that models the inflation and deflation of the air chamber and the resulting deformation of the soft bodies with tetrahedral finite elements, runs in real time using GPU
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: locomotion speed; deviation angle; total traveled distance
Líneas base: vanilla Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Sim2real: Free-response Oscillation Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization Option-Critics with Central Pattern Generator (FOC-PPOC-CPG)
Resultado: The proposed method achieved more reliable locomotion performance under various goal-reaching locomotion tasks that are unseen during the training process, compared to vanilla PPO.
Limitaciones: The method may not work as desired for soft snake robots due to the nonlinear, delayed, and stochastic dynamical response from the soft actuators.

Título: Robot Parkour Learning
Tarea: learn parkour skills (climbing, leaping, crawling, squeezing through, and running) on low-cost robots using a vision-based policy and simple reward.
Algoritmo (texto): two-stage reinforcement learning method inspired by direct collocation, with RL pre-training with soft dynamics constraints and distillation for Sim2Real transfer
Observaciones: egocentric depth camera
Acciones: continuous, as the robot needs to hold a short-term memory of past visual perceptions
Recompensa: simple reward, not stated in detail
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Blind; RND; MLP; RMA; No Distill; Oracles w/o Soft Dyn; Oracles (w/ Soft Dyn)
Resultado: Our method can enable the robot to climb obstacles as high as 0.40m (1.53x robot height) with an 80% success rate, to leap over gaps as large as of 0.60m (1.5x robot length) with an 80% success rate, to crawl beneath barriers as low as of 0.2m (0.76x robot height) with an 90% success rate, and to squeeze through thin slits of 0.28m by tilting (less than the robot width). Our method has the best performance across all skills.
Limitaciones: The current system requires the simulation environments to be manually constructed, which reduces how automatically new skills can be learned.

Título: Sim-to-Lab-to-Real: Safe reinforcement learning with shielding and generalization guarantees
Tarea: ego-vision navigation in indoor environments
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm with modifications, dual policy setup, PAC-Bayes Control
Observaciones: RGB camera observations
Acciones: discrete actions, with shielding mechanism
Recompensa: cumulative task reward, with safety violations penalized, defined by the safety state-action value function Qb
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical and RL
Sim2real: shielding mechanism during Sim-to-Lab transfer, PAC-Bayes Control for Lab-to-Real transfer
Resultado: The method achieved strong generalization performance in real indoor spaces with a quadrupedal robot, with the trained policies outperforming both classical and RL baselines.
Limitaciones: The method requires substantial resources for Lab training, and the training budget is not specified.

Título: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Quadrupedal Locomotion via Terrain Transformer
Tarea: quadrupedal locomotion over various terrains
Algoritmo (texto): Terrain Transformer (TERT), a high-capacity Transformer model with privileged learning
Observaciones: proprioception observation (48-dimensional vector including base linear and angular velocities, gravity projection, commands, joint velocities, and last action)
Acciones: 12-dimensional vector specifying target joint positions, which are then converted to joint torques through a PD controller
Recompensa: encourages the robot to follow commanded velocities and penalizes velocities along other axes, large joints torques, accelerations and collisions, and adds terms to penalize large action magnitude and encourage smoothness of joint torques
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Teacher; RMA; PPO; StackedPPO; GRU
Resultado: TERT successfully traverses nine different terrains, including grass, soil, pebble, slope, sand pit, stair down, etc., outperforming baselines in terms of return and energy consumption in simulation and real-world validation
Limitaciones: The method relies on privileged information which can be noisy or difficult to obtain in the real world, and the performance degradation when the input distribution shifts.

Título: Walk These Ways: Tuning Robot Control for Generalization with Multiplicity of Behavior
Tarea: omnidirectional velocity tracking and diverse downstream tasks like crouching, hopping, high-speed running, stair traversal, bracing against shoves, and rhythmic dance.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with augmented auxiliary rewards
Observaciones: joint positions and velocities, gravity vector, and timing reference variables
Acciones: position targets for each of the twelve joints, discrete
Recompensa: task rewards for body velocity tracking, fixed auxiliary rewards for stability and smoothness, and augmented auxiliary rewards for locomotion in the desired style
Entrenamiento: 100,000 steps, 50Hz control frequency, Jetson TX2 NX computer
Métricas: survival time; velocity tracking performance; power consumption; payload manipulation
Líneas base: gait-free baseline
Resultado: Pacing and trotting yield the best survival time in out-of-distribution deployment, outperforming the gait-free baseline. Pronking attains the best velocity tracking performance, with similar survival time to the baseline. Several choices of the contact schedule, footswing height, and frequency outperform the gait-free policy in energy efficiency.
Limitaciones: The benefits of adding MoB can come at a cost to in-distribution task performance, specifically limiting the robot’s flat-ground sprinting performance. The behavior parameterization is restrictive for combinations of high linear and angular velocity.

Título: AI-CPG: Adaptive Imitated Central Pattern Generators for Bipedal Locomotion Learned Through Reinforced Reflex Neural Networks
Tarea: enhance humanoid locomotion by combining CPG and DRL to achieve adaptability, balancing ability, and energy efficiency.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for forming a reflex neural network, with CPG for feedforward control.
Observaciones: joint angles and torques, using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to obtain motion frequencies
Acciones: joint torques, discrete (PD controller output)
Recompensa: defined as Rh - αRe + Ra + Rs + Rd + βRg, where Rh is the height of the humanoid head, Re limits energy consumption, Ra is survival reward, Rs optimizes pelvis orientation, Rd teaches movement in target direction, and Rg reduces error in joint angles.
Entrenamiento: 8,192 agents in parallel for 500,000 steps, using PPO
Líneas base: existing methods
Resultado: The proposed method outperformed existing methods in terms of adaptability, balancing ability, and energy efficiency even for uneven surfaces.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a large number of agents for training and may require high computational resources.

Título: AI-driven warehouse automation: A comprehensive review of systems
Tarea: Optimizar operaciones de almacenes, desde la gestión de inventario hasta el cumplimiento de pedidos, y mejorar la eficiencia, la precisión y la adaptabilidad de los almacenes.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning, Machine Learning, Computer Vision
Robot: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs), Robotic Arms, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs)
Observaciones: Sensors, IoT devices, and enterprise systems
Acciones: Discrete (e.g., picking, packing, palletizing) and continuous (e.g., navigation, manipulation)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: not stated
Limitaciones: Ethical considerations, privacy concerns, safety and security risks, and human-robot collaboration issues.

Título: ASC: Adaptive Skill Coordination for Robotic Mobile Manipulation
Tarea: mobile pick-and-place, involving navigating to a receptacle, searching for and picking an object, and placing it at a desired location.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL), with a skill coordination policy and a corrective policy.
Observaciones: two depth images from the front of the robot, a depth image from the gripper, a bounding box image of the target object, joint angles of the robot arm, and an egomotion sensor estimating the robot’s relative heading and displacement from its start pose.
Acciones: discrete actions for navigation, pick, and place, with continuous velocity commands for navigation.
Recompensa: navigation reward penalizes collision, backward movement, and gives a terminal reward if successful; pick reward focuses on searching for and picking the object, with a binary mask indicating the object’s bounding box.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical task and motion planning (TAMP); modular learning; end-to-end learning
Resultado: ASC achieves a near-perfect success rate of 98% in two real-world environments, compared to 73% for sequentially executing skills.
Limitaciones: ASC assumes limited knowledge of the environment and does not rely on detailed maps or precise object locations, but it may struggle with cluttered environments and hand-off errors.

Título: A Multifidelity Sim-to-Real Pipeline for Verifiable and Compositional Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: pilot a Warthog unmanned ground robot to navigate to a goal location with a success probability of 0.95.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, specifically parametric Markov decision process (pMDP) for high-level model
Observaciones: odometry-based estimates of the robot’s location and pose
Acciones: discrete actions, as subtask policies are trained using RL algorithms
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: Unity video game engine for low-fidelity simulation, high-fidelity software-in-the-loop (SIL) simulation, physical hardware
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: success probability of completing the task
Líneas base: classical methods
Resultado: The proposed framework successfully trained and deployed a compositional RL system that consistently completed the robot’s task with a success probability of 0.95.
Limitaciones: The framework requires a high-fidelity SIL simulation that cannot run faster than real time, which precludes its use for training RL policies.

Título: CTS: Concurrent Teacher-Student Reinforcement Learning for Legged Locomotion
Tarea: legged locomotion over uneven terrains
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with concurrent teacher-student architecture
Observaciones: proprioceptive observation (angular velocity, gravity vector, joint positions and velocities, command, previous actions)
Acciones: continuous (angular deviation of the robot’s joint relative to its nominal position)
Recompensa: velocity tracking error, defined as the difference between the desired velocity and the actual velocity
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: state-of-the-art teacher-student methods, Regularized Online Adaptation (ROA)
Resultado: The proposed CTS architecture reduces the average velocity tracking error by up to 20% compared to state-of-the-art teacher-student and ROA methods, demonstrating significant superiority in addressing blind locomotion tasks.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: CaT: Constraints as Terminations for Legged Locomotion Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: legged locomotion, specifically traversing challenging terrains like stairs, slopes, and high platforms
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Constraints as Terminations (CaT)
Observaciones: height-scan of the surroundings
Acciones: desired joint position offsets, continuous
Recompensa: defined through both reward functions and constraints, including velocity tracking, safety, and style constraints
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Interior-point Policy Optimization; Penalized Proximal Policy Optimization (P3O)
Resultado: The agent learned policies that can traverse challenging terrains with agile locomotion skills, satisfying safety and style constraints.
Limitaciones: The approach is simple to implement but may be overly conservative in constraint handling, potentially impairing exploration and learning.

Título: Counterfactual rewards promote collective transport using individually controlled swarm microrobots
Tarea: collectively rotate an ellipsoid rod and transport an object to a target position
Algoritmo (texto): Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with counterfactual rewards
Observaciones: presence of other microrobots and an ellipsoid rod, represented as a linear chain of circular particles
Acciones: discrete actions: move forward, turn left, turn right, or remain stationary
Recompensa: counterfactual rewards that credit each agent for its own contribution to the collective performance
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: angular velocity of the rod; mean distance between the ellipsoid and the target
Líneas base: team rewards; manually designed individual rewards
Resultado: microrobots learned to rotate and transport an ellipsoid rod to a target position, with the angular velocity increasing over time and the mean distance between the ellipsoid and the target decreasing
Limitaciones: the microrobots are subject to thermal noise and interactions with the rod, which introduce additional noise to their trajectories

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Large-Scale Robot Exploration
Tarea: Explorar un entorno desconocido minimizando la longitud del camino y el tiempo total de la tarea, y mejorando la eficiencia de exploración.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) con mecanismos de atención basados en redes neuronales, con aprendizaje con información de verdad (privileged learning).
Observaciones: Mapa de ocupación (occupancy grid) y gráficos informativos (informative graphs) basados en la nube de puntos 3D.
Acciones: Puntos de camino (waypoints) discretos.
Recompensa: Se define como la longitud del camino total y el tiempo total de la tarea, con penalizaciones por movimientos redundantes.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se utilizó un algoritmo de rarefacción de gráficos.
Métricas: Distancia total del camino; Duración total de la tarea; Tiempo de planificación por paso; Eficiencia de exploración (volumen explorado dividido por la distancia total o el tiempo total)
Líneas base: TARE; DSVP; Humanos con conocimiento previo
Sim2real: Transferencia de modelos entrenados en simulación a un robot real sin adicional entrenamiento.
Resultado: Nuestro planificador basado en DRL reduce la eficiencia de exploración en 12% en términos de distancia y 6% en términos de tiempo, y reduce el tiempo de planificación en 60% en comparación con TARE, un planificador de exploración de gran escala de vanguardia.
Limitaciones: El modelo no se generaliza bien a entornos de gran escala y realistas, como un bosque desordenado, donde la planificación se vuelve menos eficiente.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning Assisted UAV Path Planning Relying on Cumulative Reward Mode and Region Segmentation
Tarea: learn to plan a collision-free path for UAVs to move from their current position to a deployment point, considering obstacles at the UAV's flight altitude.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Q-Network (DQN) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) with a cumulative reward model and region segmentation algorithm, using experience replay.
Observaciones: distance to the destination and obstacle density in the adjacent space of the current node
Acciones: discrete actions (Forward, backward, left, right, left front, right front, left back, right back)
Recompensa: cumulative reward based on distance to the destination and obstacle density, with a negative reward for crashing into obstacles and a positive reward for reaching the destination
Simulador: Simulink VRSink, 2D model of the UAV working environment
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: traditional reward model
Resultado: The cumulative reward model improved the training efficiency of DRL algorithms by 30.8%, and the region segmentation algorithm enabled DQN to avoid 99% of local optimal traps and DDPG to avoid 92% of local optimal traps.
Limitaciones: The method relies on exploration and may face issues with sparse training data, and the region segmentation algorithm may not be suitable for all environments.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning With Dynamic Graphs for Adaptive Informative Path Planning
Tarea: map a set of targets of interest in an initially unknown 3D environment using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UA V) as efficiently as possible.
Algoritmo (texto): deep reinforcement learning with a dynamically constructed graph
Observaciones: 3D position coordinates, yaw of the unidirectional onboard sensor, number of targets observed
Acciones: 4D actions (3D position and yaw angle), discrete
Recompensa: encourages the robot to both explore unknown regions and exploit discovered targets, considering both the reduction in utility uncertainty and the number of observed targets
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: number of discovered targets of interest
Líneas base: state-of-the-art non-learning-based and learning-based planning methods
Resultado: our method enables more efficient target discovery compared to state-of-the-art learning and non-learning baselines
Limitaciones: the method is not tested on a physical robot, and the action space needs to be updated as obstacles are discovered

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Robot Path Planning
Tarea: path planning for a mobile robot
Algoritmo (texto): Parallel Soft Actor-Critic (PSAC) algorithm, Hybrid A* algorithm
Algoritmo (diccionario): SAC; Dijkstra / A*; Variante de SAC
Observaciones: coordinates in the world coordinate system, heading angle, distance from the target point
Acciones: continuous actions, including rear wheel speed and front wheel angle
Recompensa: reward function consists of two items: step reward and final goal reward; step reward is based on the distance difference between the current and previous steps, final goal reward is -20 for collision, +25 for reaching the target, and 0 otherwise
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: comparative data on expand points and searching time
Líneas base: Hybrid A* algorithm
Resultado: The PSAC algorithm and Two-way search Hybrid A* algorithm together can significantly enhance robotic navigation systems, offering a scalable solution for operating in complex environments, with high computational efficiency and few expansion points.
Limitaciones: The trajectory generated based on deep reinforcement learning usually does not conform to the actual kinematic constraints of the robot, and the generated trajectory cannot be tracked, resulting in the final robot planning failed and entered the shock stage.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Obstacle Avoidance for Robot Movement in Warehouse Environments
Tarea: obstacle avoidance for robot movement in warehouse environments
Algoritmo (texto): deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with LSTM network, based on ORCA strategy
Observaciones: robot's own state and the state of other pedestrians in the environment
Acciones: discrete robot velocity control signals (linear and angular velocities)
Recompensa: reward function based on spatial behavior of pedestrians, penalizing states where the angle changes too much and entering into the pedestrian's private distance
Entrenamiento: 3,000 training rounds, 500 tests, on a desktop computer with Intel Core i7-7700 3.60 GHz and NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti
Líneas base: ORCA; CADRL; SF_RL; LM_RL
Resultado: APG_RL algorithm achieved a success rate of 0.99, an average time of 10.81 seconds, and a return of 0.3196, outperforming other algorithms in terms of navigation efficiency and pedestrian comfort in complex environments.
Limitaciones: the method is tested in a simulation environment and may not fully generalize to real-world scenarios, and the success rate and average time may vary with the number of pedestrians.

Título: Design and Control of a Bipedal Robotic Character
Tarea: Robots perform expressive and dynamic motions based on user inputs, blending and switching between different motion elements.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: Joint positions, velocities, and torques
Acciones: Discrete actions for policy switches and command signals
Recompensa: Imitation of artist-specified kinematic reference motions and dynamic balancing
Simulador: Simulation model with actuator models and domain randomization
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Not stated
Resultado: The robot can robustly execute artist-created motions and blend or transition between them in real-time, as demonstrated in unscripted shows.
Limitaciones: The unique character does not have a readily available dataset for imitation learning, and the design prioritizes simplicity over the best possible mechanical design.

Título: DiffuseLoco: Real-Time Legged Locomotion Control with Diffusion from Offline Datasets
Tarea: legged locomotion control, including bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion skills
Algoritmo (texto): Diffusion model (DDPM) with a transformer backbone, using delayed inputs and receding horizon control
Observaciones: proprioceptive feedback and joint-level PD targets
Acciones: joint-level PD targets, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: cheap simulation data, potentially extended to real-world hardware
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: prior reinforcement learning; non-diffusion-based behavior cloning baselines
Sim2real: technique used to transfer from simulation to the real robot, or 'not stated'
Resultado: DiffuseLoco demonstrates better stability and lower velocity tracking errors compared to baselines, while demonstrating multi-modal behaviors with skill transitioning and robustness on terrains with varying ground frictions.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: GeRM: A Generalist Robotic Model with Mixture-of-experts for Quadruped Robot
Tarea: Navigate to objects, avoid obstacles, stop objects, distinguish letters, and go through tunnels.
Algoritmo (texto): Offline reinforcement learning with Conservative Q-learning (CQL) variant, using a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer architecture.
Algoritmo (diccionario): Q-learning; Offline RL (genérico); CQL; Transformers en RL (GTrXL…); Variante de Q-learning
Observaciones: Images, language instructions, and command data
Acciones: Discretized robot commands (12-dimensional vector of velocities, gaits, frequencies, heights, pitch angles, foot widths, foot heights, and termination signal)
Recompensa: Not stated
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Existing methods
Resultado: GeRM outperforms existing methods across all tasks with only 1/2 total parameters activated.
Limitaciones: Not stated

Título: Generalization in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Navigation by Reward Shaping
Tarea: local navigation in unknown and cluttered workspaces
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm, Twin Delayed Deep-Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)
Observaciones: LiDAR data, relative position to the target, linear and angular velocities
Acciones: velocities, discrete
Recompensa: penalizes actions that don't increase information in a local map exploration and don't reduce the distance to the goal location; grants for arriving at the target, moving in clear directions, and performing progressive movements; penalizes collisions
Entrenamiento: 20000 episodes, 500 steps timeout, 15 pairs of positions for starting and goal locations, 16 GB RAM, Intel Core i7-11800H CPU, NVIDIA GTX 3060 graphics card, Ubuntu 20.04
Resultado: Our proposed reward function combined with SAC outperforms all compared methods in terms of success rate, especially in complex scenarios with local minima and obstacles.
Limitaciones: The method is susceptible to local minima, and the authors acknowledge the need for further exploration of the environment during training.

Título: Grow Your Limits: Continuous Improvement with Real-World RL for Robotic Locomotion
Tarea: learn quadrupedal locomotion in the real world
Algoritmo (texto): actor-critic RL method with action regularization
Observaciones: root orientation, joint angles and velocities, root (local) velocity, normalized foot contacts, and last recorded action
Acciones: discrete, with a penalty on the magnitude of actions
Recompensa: maximize the robot’s local linear velocity while maintaining an upright orientation, with penalties on angular velocity and torque smoothness
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: model-based RL; sample-efficient RL
Resultado: APRL allows the robot to learn to walk forward in just minutes starting completely from scratch, and the behavior learned with APRL performs significantly better in terms of its average walking speed in challenging situations, on average by a factor of 2.
Limitaciones: The method requires extensive engineering of the simulation settings for the policy to generalize, and most do not have any mechanism to learn from their failures in the real world.

Título: HumanPlus: Humanoid Shadowing and Imitation from Humans
Tarea: learn motion and autonomous skills from human data, including tasks like wearing a shoe, folding clothes, and playing table tennis.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) for low-level policy, Action Chunking Transformer (modified) for imitation learning
Algoritmo (diccionario): Imitation learning (genérico); ACT (Action Chunking Transformer); Transformers en RL (GTrXL…)
Observaciones: proprioceptive observations from onboard sensors (IMU, joint encoders)
Acciones: 19-dimensional joint position setpoints, discrete for hands
Recompensa: defined in Table 1, includes terms for matching target poses, energy saving, and avoiding foot slipping
Simulador: Unitree H1 robot with simulated environment, WHAM for real-time body pose estimation, HaMeR for real-time hand pose estimation
Entrenamiento: 50Hz, 8 context length, 1250 steps per task in simulation, 25Hz in real world, not stated hardware
Métricas: success rates; average task completion time
Líneas base: Kinesthetic Teaching; ALOHA; Meta Quest
Resultado: Our method outperforms baselines with 100% success rates in most tasks, and 15.34 seconds average completion time in Wear a Shoe and Walk task.
Limitaciones: Limited to one human operator, expensive hardware for baselines, lack of robustness to disturbances and whole-body skills.

Título: Humanoid Parkour Learning
Tarea: perform parkour tasks such as jumping on platforms, leaping over hurdles, and running on various terrains
Algoritmo (texto): PPO with a Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) and an MLP as the backbone of the actor, using an auto-curriculum mechanism
Observaciones: onboard depth vision and robot proprioception
Acciones: continuous, as the policy outputs all target joints of the robot body
Recompensa: consists of task rewards, regularization rewards, and safety rewards; includes penalties for motor errors and foot contact
Simulador: isaacgym simulator with fractal noise terrain
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: blind walking policy; built-in MPC controller in Unitree H1
Sim2real: using multiple domain randomization techniques, simulating noise patterns of the depth image, and applying built-in filters in the Intel RealSense API
Resultado: The parkour policy achieves the best performance in the 4 difficult tasks compared with the blind walking policy and the built-in MPC controller in Unitree H1, with success rates of 90%, 80%, 100%, and 100% for jump up, leap, stairs up, and hurdle respectively, and average moving distances of 14.3m, 14.0m, 14.4m, and 14.4m.
Limitaciones: The method relies on manually constructed terrain and is difficult to generalize to unseen terrains without further training. The parkour policy is robust to arm-action override, but more difficult manipulation skills require further tuning to avoid disrupting the visual system.

Título: Learning Agile Locomotion on Risky Terrains
Tarea: traverse risky terrains with dynamic motions
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (end-to-end)
Observaciones: sparse stepping stones and narrow balance beams
Acciones: dynamic motions, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: model-based controllers
Resultado: ANYmal-D achieved peak forward velocity of ≥ 2.5 m/s on sparse stepping stones and narrow balance beams
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Learning Risk-Aware Quadrupedal Locomotion using Distributional Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn risk-aware locomotion policies for legged robots to adapt to risky environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Distributional Proximal Policy Optimization (DPPO), based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).
Observaciones: proprioceptive measurements, previous actions, local height map samples, and input commands (desired linear and angular base velocities).
Acciones: joint positions, discrete (risk parameter conditioned).
Recompensa: adapted from [20], primarily reward command tracking and penalize collisions and energy expenditure, with additional penalties for joint motion and torque based on a curriculum.
Simulador: legged gym library based on IsaacGym simulator.
Entrenamiento: 20k iterations, 10 policies trained, MLPs used for actor and critic, not tuned hyperparameters.
Métricas: undiscounted return; fraction of episodes in which the robot terminates before episode end; L2 distance between commanded and actual linear velocity
Líneas base: PPO; DSAC; PPO1; PPO2; DPPO-CVaR
Resultado: DPPO significantly outperformed DSAC and PPO1 and PPO2 baselines, with a return of 27.62 after 20k iterations, while PPO2 had severely lower returns due to high early termination rate and linear velocity tracking error.
Limitaciones: The risk-sensitive behavior generalizes well beyond the parameter bounds used during training, but the reward shaping baselines had difficulties incorporating risk sensitivity through the standard RL framework.

Título: Learning Speed Adaptation for Flight in Clutter
Tarea: endow flight vehicles with the ability of speed adaptation in prior unknown and partially observable cluttered environments
Algoritmo (texto): online model-free reinforcement learning (RL) with a two-stage reward scheme
Observaciones: 3D local occupancy map, current velocity, current tracking error, decision at the last time step, and a pre-planned trajectory
Acciones: high-level planning instruction (discrete)
Recompensa: maximize traversal speed and minimize collision loss, with a two-stage reward scheme to address sparsity and stochasticity
Simulador: customized simulator with multiple parallel environments
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: constant speed constraint baselines; an alternative method
Resultado: the policy behaves more perception-aware, achieving higher success rates and better flight efficiency and safety compared to constant speed constraint baselines and an alternative method
Limitaciones: the success of the method is limited by the perception latency and the error of trajectory tracking, and the transfer from simulation to real-world scenarios is not explicitly addressed

Título: Learning Vision-Based Bipedal Locomotion for Challenging Terrain
Tarea: Follow speed and heading commands while maintaining balance over challenging terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): PPO actor-critic RL algorithm in MuJoCo simulation environment
Observaciones: Orientation, angular velocity, position, velocity, user commands, periodic clock
Acciones: PD setpoints for all motors, with additional clock increment and shift residuals
Recompensa: A three-component reward function: base locomotion, foot acceleration, and foot collision, with equal weighting
Entrenamiento: 80 cores on a dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8280 server, 30,000 episodes
Métricas: Success Rate; Episodes with foot collision; Termination due to foot collision
Líneas base: blind policy; MLP model; Transformer-based model
Sim2real: Depth image randomization, domain randomization, and sim-to-real transfer pipeline
Resultado: The policy achieved a success rate of 95% on challenging terrains, with only 5% of episodes ending due to foot collisions.
Limitaciones: The method relies on domain randomization and sim-to-real transfer, which can be challenging for vision-based locomotion.

Título: Learning Visual Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation from Demonstrations
Tarea: Lifting baskets, pressing buttons, opening and closing dishwashers, pushing doors, and twisting valves.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for the low-level controller, Diffusion-based Behavior Cloning (BC) for the high-level planner.
Observaciones: End-effector pose, 3D point clouds, robot state variables (joint positions, velocities, etc.).
Acciones: Continuous joint positions for the end-effector, discrete for manipulation flags.
Recompensa: Position and orientation tracking errors, stability, and smoothness terms.
Simulador: IsaacGym for training, real-world Unitree Aliengo robot for testing.
Entrenamiento: 3 billion timesteps for the low-level controller, 20k timesteps for the high-level planner.
Líneas base: End-to-End Behavior Cloning (BC); Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL); End-to-End Visual Reinforcement Learning (VRL)
Resultado: Our method achieved significantly higher success rates across all tasks compared to HRL, with only 20k timesteps of visual data required for training the high-level planner.
Limitaciones: The method is limited to tasks that can be performed with the legs of a quadruped robot, and the success rates for some tasks are still low.

Título: Learning robust autonomous navigation and locomotion for wheeled-legged robots
Tarea: Autonomous navigation and locomotion in urban environments for wheeled-legged robots.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with privileged learning, Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL)
Observaciones: LiDAR, RGB stereo camera, IMU, joint encoders, onboard terrain elevation mapping, GPS antenna, delivery box, 5G router
Acciones: Joint position and wheel velocity commands, discrete (gait selection)
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the system is trained to minimize Cost of Transport (COT) and ∑ τ2, and to follow the shortest path towards the goal point during training.
Simulador: Simulation environment using Wave Function Collapse (WFC) algorithm
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions training in simulation environments through privileged learning and HRL, with episodes generating new obstacle-free paths.
Métricas: Average speed; Mechanical COT; Path following accuracy
Líneas base: ANYmal robot; Traditional navigation setup
Resultado: The robot achieved an average speed of 1.68 m/s with a mechanical COT of 0.16, demonstrating three times the speed with a 53% lower COT compared to the ANYmal robot.
Limitaciones: The paper acknowledges that the improvement is mainly attributed to the driving mode, which evenly distributes weight across all four legs, keeping leg joints relatively static, and that other major factors contributing to energy loss, such as heat loss and mechanical loss from the actuators’ transmission, also come into play during constant walking motions, thus potentially reducing overall efficiency.

Título: Learning to Fly in Seconds
Tarea: Learning to control a quadrotor by mapping its state directly to RPM outputs.
Algoritmo (texto): Asymmetric actor-critic-based architecture with off-policy RL, curriculum learning, and exploration noise scheduling.
Observaciones: State of the quadrotor, including RPMs.
Acciones: RPMs, discrete
Recompensa: Defined by penalties that gradually increase during training, leading to better sample complexity and more reliable policies.
Entrenamiento: 18 seconds of training on a consumer-grade laptop
Líneas base: Classical control methods
Resultado: The agent can control the Crazyflie nano quadrotor with competitive performance in trajectory tracking after 18 seconds of training.
Limitaciones: The high-order integration between inputs and the desired output poses a challenge for RL algorithms, leading to high-sample complexity and unreliable training behavior.

Título: Learning to walk in confined spaces using 3D representation
Tarea: Learning to walk in confined spaces using 3D representation
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: 6D command, proprioceptive observation, exteroceptive observation, privileged state
Acciones: Discrete actions (phase difference and residual joint position target) for low-level policy; 3D velocity command for high-level policy
Recompensa: Velocity tracking rewards, penalties for joint torque, velocity, acceleration or slip, base distance reward to maintain a safe distance from obstacles
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Previous work on locomotion control
Resultado: The method successfully controlled a quadruped robot in confined, rough terrain, demonstrating robust and versatile locomotion in confined and unstructured environments.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a procedural terrain generator and noisy voxel data, which may not generalize well to all real-world scenarios.

Título: Leveraging Symmetry in RL-based Legged Locomotion Control
Tarea: loco-manipulación y bipedal locomoción en robots quadrúpedos
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) con data-augmentation (PPOaug) y con restricciones de equivariancia/hard invariancia (PPOeqic)
Observaciones: proprioceptivas y observaciones específicas del tarea
Acciones: acciones continuas, discretas en algunos casos
Recompensa: funciones invariantes con respecto a la simetría morfológica, recompensas basadas en mediciones relativas del estado del robot
Entrenamiento: 2,000 entornos de simulación, 10 episodios por entorno, 3 semillas
Métricas: tasa de éxito (SR); índice simétrico (SI); rendimiento en escenarios de distribución de probabilidad diferente (OOD)
Líneas base: PPO sin restricciones
Resultado: El PPOeqic mostró un rendimiento consistente superior a otros PPO, demostrando la eficacia de las restricciones de equivariancia en el entrenamiento. Además, PPOeqic mostró mejor eficiencia en el uso de muestras, notoriamente con menos muestras en la etapa temprana del entrenamiento.
Limitaciones: Los comportamientos subóptimos en el PPO, aunque factibles debido a la modelización imprecisa del contacto, se sobreajustan al entorno de simulación y carecen de robustez, lo que se demuestra ser infeasible en la transferencia de sim-to-real.

Título: Lifelike agility and play in quadrupedal robots using reinforcement learning and generative pre-trained models
Tarea: The agent learns to mimic animal behaviors, traverse complex obstacles, and play a multi-agent Chase Tag Game.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with PPO algorithm, using a distributed multi-agent RL architecture TLeague.
Observaciones: The agent observes motion data from animal datasets, including different terrains.
Acciones: Continuous motor actions to control the robot's movements, discrete for some tasks.
Recompensa: The reward is defined as the normalized tracking reward of the generated movements compared to the animal motion data, and success rate in obstacle traversal and game scenarios.
Simulador: Simulation environment for training, including flat terrain, stairs, hurdles, and blocks.
Entrenamiento: 4 days of training with up to 4 NVIDIA TESLA V100 GPUs.
Métricas: Normalized tracking reward; Success rate; Output torque distribution
Líneas base: β-V AE method; GAIL (Adversarial Imitation Learning)
Sim2real: Technique used to transfer from simulation to the real robot is not explicitly stated, but the method is tested on a real robot.
Resultado: The MAX robot successfully mimicked animal behaviors, traversed complex obstacles with high success rates, and played the Chase Tag Game with lifelike agility and strategy, achieving a normalized tracking reward of 0.85 in simulation and 0.75 in reality.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a large pre-trained model and may not generalize well to completely new tasks or environments. The training process is complex and requires significant computational resources.

Título: Model-Based Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning via Separated Proportional-Integral Lagrangian
Tarea: learn an optimal policy satisfying the chance constraints in a model-based reinforcement learning setting for a mobile robot navigation task.
Algoritmo (texto): separated proportional-integral Lagrangian (SPIL) algorithm, which combines penalty and Lagrangian methods.
Observaciones: state, action, and model uncertainty
Acciones: continuous, parameterized neural network
Recompensa: expected discounted cumulative reward, while keeping a high safe probability
Simulador: car-following simulation, real-world mobile robot navigation task
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: penalty method; Lagrangian method
Resultado: The SPIL method achieves better policy performance compared with existing penalty and Lagrangian methods, and the real-world mobile robot navigation experiment proves the effectiveness of the model-based SPIL algorithm in practical engineering problems.
Limitaciones: The method faces the challenge of integral value getting overly large, leading to policy over-conservatism, and the gradient of safe probability is hard to compute, especially in a model-based paradigm.

Título: Not Only Rewards but Also Constraints: Applications on Legged Robot Locomotion
Tarea: train locomotion controllers for legged robots to navigate challenging terrains
Algoritmo (texto): Interior-point Policy Optimization (IPO) with modifications, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Robot: Raibo, six quadrupedal robots, one bipedal robot
Observaciones: joint positions, body orientation, velocity command, joint position errors, joint velocities, action histories, central phases, terrain friction coefficient, body height, body linear velocity, body contact state, foot contact impulse, foot airtime, foot clearance, terrain profiles
Acciones: joint PD targets (converted to joint torques by a PD controller module)
Recompensa: composed of three terms: command tracking, joint torque, and action smoothness; command tracking and joint torque rewards guide the robot to track the given velocity command with minimal torque usage; action smoothness reward regulates the neural network policy to have a smooth output surface
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: previous works that used reward-only framework
Resultado: high-performance controllers can be obtained with significantly less reward engineering (i.e., only three reward coefficients and a single reward coefficient modification) and by exploiting more generalizable and straightforward constraints
Limitaciones: the method relies on extensive reward engineering to find the relative weights for each of the reward terms based on the resulting robot’s motion, which is not trivial because there are often more than ten reward terms

Título: OmniDrones: An Efficient and Flexible Platform for Reinforcement Learning in Drone Control
Tarea: The agent learns to control drones for various tasks, including single-drone hovering, over-actuated system tracking, and multi-agent coordination.
Algoritmo (texto): various single- and multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms, including end-to-end visual-motor control policies, model-based reinforcement learning, and model predictive control (MPC).
Observaciones: IMUs, RGB-D cameras, segmentation sensors, force sensors, and contact sensors
Acciones: discrete and continuous actions, depending on the control mode
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical optimization-based methods and other reinforcement learning baselines
Resultado: The platform supports efficient and flexible drone simulations and benchmark tasks, achieving over 105 steps per second in data collection, and demonstrates the capabilities of multiple learning algorithms on the proposed tasks.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that there are unavoidable gaps between the simulated dynamics and reality, and that the platform is not tested on a physical robot.

Título: One Policy to Run Them All: an End-to-end Learning Approach to Multi-Embodiment Locomotion
Tarea: controlar la locomoción de diferentes tipos de morfologías de robots
Algoritmo (texto): Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) con una arquitectura neural llamada URMA (Unified Robot Morphology Architecture)
Robot: Unitree A1, MAB Honey Badger, MAB Silver Badger, 16 robots simulados (9 cuadrúpedos, 5 humanoides, 1 bípedo, 1 hexápodo)
Observaciones: observaciones de los grados de libertad de los robots, posiciones y velocidades de los pies, y posibles observaciones generales
Acciones: acciones de control de los grados de libertad de los robots, discretas o continuas, dependiendo de la morfología
Recompensa: no se especifica en el resumen, pero se menciona que se utiliza PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
Entrenamiento: 100 millones de pasos por robot, 5 semillas aleatorias
Líneas base: Multi-Head Baseline; Padding Baseline
Resultado: URMA aprendió una política de locomoción en 16 robots simulados que se puede transferir a robots reales sin ajustes adicionales, logrando un rendimiento final superior a los baselines en la transferencia zero-shot.
Limitaciones: la generalización a morfologías completamente nuevas aún es problemática, se omite la información exteroceptiva en las observaciones, y no se ha podido probar la transferencia a robots humanoides debido a su costo.

Título: Optimizing UAV-UGV coalition operations: A hybrid clustering and multi-agent reinforcement learning approach for path planning in obstructed environment
Tarea: reaching predefined targets by following the most time-efficient routes while avoiding collisions
Algoritmo (texto): Multi-agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) and Multi-agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)
Robot: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs)
Observaciones: position of agents, targets, and obstacles, zone radius, speed, flight range
Acciones: discrete actions for navigation
Recompensa: defined as the sum of the total number of completed tasks in the combined scenario divided by the total number of evaluated episodes, and the number of collisions per 1000 episodes
Entrenamiento: 1,000 episodes, training parameters for MADDPG and MAPPO
Métricas: Completion Rate of Tasks; Collisions Per 1K Episode; Number of Steps per Episode; Accuracy; Completion Time of Task
Líneas base: Simplified IADRL (Baseline) [7]; CRFT w/o Zones; MEANCRFT-MAPPO
Resultado: our proposed method substantially surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques, nearly doubling efficiency in terms of target navigation time and task completion rate
Limitaciones: the method is tested in a simulation environment and the authors acknowledge that the method fails to determine how to get the deployed UAVs back to their respective UGVs which might be very far, which results in the UAVs losing power

Título: PIE: Parkour With Implicit-Explicit Learning Framework for Legged Robots
Tarea: traverse various terrains with agile and smooth locomotion in parkour tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): one-stage end-to-end reinforcement learning framework with dual-level implicit-explicit estimation, based on PPO for the actor and critic network and regression for the estimator.
Observaciones: raw depth images, joint actions
Acciones: joint angle commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: mean difficulty level reached; success rates on different terrains
Líneas base: Hoeller et al. [1]; Zhuang et al. [2]; Cheng et al. [3]
Resultado: Our PIE framework enables the robot to climb obstacles as high as 0.75m (3x robot height), leap over gaps as large as 1m (3x robot length) and climb stairs as high as 0.25m (1x robot height), outperforming state-of-the-art methods by at least 50%.
Limitaciones: lacks 3D understanding of the terrain, relies solely on depth images, training confined to static environments.

Título: PLAN-SEQ-LEARN: LANGUAGE MODEL GUIDED RL FOR SOLVING LONG HORIZON ROBOTICS TASKS
Tarea: solve long-horizon robotics tasks such as assembling nuts on pegs, disassembling objects, and manipulating objects in a kitchen setting.
Algoritmo (texto): Plan-Seq-Learn (PSL), which combines language model planning, motion planning, and reinforcement learning for low-level control.
Observaciones: RGB-D images, local observations around the robot (e.g., wrist camera views)
Acciones: discrete actions for low-level control, using joint or end-effector control
Recompensa: defined by the environment, aiming to maximize the expected sum of rewards over the trajectory
Simulador: Meta-World, Obstructed Suite, Kitchen, and Robosuite environments
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: language-based approaches; classical approaches; end-to-end reinforcement learning approaches
Resultado: PSL achieves state-of-the-art results on over 25 challenging robotics tasks with up to 10 stages, with success rates of over 85% from raw visual input.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a pre-trained language model and vision models, which may not always be available or accurate.

Título: Quantum Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robot Navigation Tasks
Tarea: learn optimal policies for a simulated Turtlebot robotic system in several simulated navigation tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) with parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) as function approximators.
Observaciones: state of the environment, including position and velocity
Acciones: continuous actions, as the tasks involve navigation
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical neural network baselines
Resultado: Quantum circuits in hybrid quantum-classic reinforcement learning setups are capable of learning optimal policies in multiple robotic navigation scenarios with notably fewer trainable parameters compared to a classical baseline, but the classical neural network consistently showed better results concerning training times and stability.
Limitaciones: The classical baseline produces more stable and better performing policies overall, and there are yet open questions regarding the application to considerably more demanding tasks.

Título: Rapid locomotion via reinforcement learning
Tarea: Rapid locomotion, including sprinting and high-speed turning on natural terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement learning (RL) with a teacher-student training approach, using PPO for optimization.
Observaciones: Joint angles and joint velocities, IMU readings
Acciones: Joint position commands, continuous
Recompensa: A reward function for tracking linear and angular velocity commands, with additional terms for stability, smoothness, and safety.
Entrenamiento: 400 million simulated timesteps using 4000 parallel agents, roughly equivalent to 92 real-time days, simulated in under three hours using a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU
Métricas: Tracking error for forward and yaw velocity commands
Líneas base: Classical control methods; Domain randomization
Sim2real: Teacher-student training approach for sim-to-real transfer
Resultado: The learned policy sustained a top speed of 3.9 m/s on flat ground, achieving an average speed of 3.4 m/s on uneven outdoor terrain, and enabling high-speed spinning on flat and icy ground.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a minimal sensing suite and may not generalize well to robots with different sensor configurations.

Título: Reinforcement Learning Meets Visual Odometry
Tarea: estimate the camera pose from a sequence of images
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: keypoints, map statistics, and prior poses
Acciones: binary keyframe action and grid size action (discrete)
Recompensa: based on pose error, runtime, and other metrics
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical VO methods; end-to-end VO methods; hybrid VO methods
Resultado: improvements in accuracy up to 19% and increased robustness, tracking all camera trajectories while the w/o RL baseline gets lost
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Research on Autonomous Robots Navigation based on Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: autonomous robot navigation
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Q Network (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: position in a 10x10 grid world environment, including state, action, reward, and next state
Acciones: discrete actions, with actions being continuous in practice
Recompensa: number of collisions, path smoothness
Entrenamiento: 100 independent experiments, each containing 500 episodes
Líneas base: traditional global path planning algorithm; local path planning algorithm
Resultado: our method outperforms other methods in terms of the number of collisions, demonstrating higher navigation efficiency and safety
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Research on Reinforcement Learning Based Warehouse Robot Navigation Algorithm in Complex Warehouse Layout
Tarea: efficiently find the optimal path in complex warehouse layout and make real-time decision
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy-Dijkstra (PP-D), combining Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Dijkstra's algorithm
Robot: mobile robot for complex warehouse layout navigation
Observaciones: sensors such as LiDAR and cameras, status information of the robot
Acciones: discrete actions, output of PPO algorithm
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: accuracy ratio; recall rate; F1 Score; robustness
Líneas base: DQN (Deep Q-Network); A* algorithm
Resultado: PP-D algorithm has the best performance in the four key indicators of accuracy ratio, recall rate, F1 score and robustness, indicating that it has the best comprehensive performance in the complex warehouse layout navigation task of warehouse robots based on reinforcement learning.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Resilient Legged Local Navigation: Learning to Traverse with Compromised Perception End-to-End
Tarea: Guía al robot a un objetivo local dentro del tiempo dado, reconstruyendo el entorno a partir de la percepción corrompida y reaccionando a las fallas de percepción.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) con un diseño actor-critic asimétrico, utilizando PPO.
Observaciones: Percepción local (altura escaneada), percepción propiocéptica, mapa de trascibilidad, y otros estados relacionados con la navegación.
Acciones: Comandos de velocidad, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: Se compone de términos de rendimiento de la tarea, penalizaciones de eventos y términos de regularización.
Simulador: Entorno simulado con terrenos con obstáculos y trincheras invisibles.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica el presupuesto de entrenamiento ni el hardware.
Líneas base: Planificadores locales clásicos
Resultado: Nuestro algoritmo aumenta la tasa de éxito en 30% cuando se enfrenta a fallas de percepción, comparado con los planificadores locales clásicos.
Limitaciones: El método no escala bien a diferentes situaciones y requiere un entrenamiento exhaustivo.

Título: Rethinking Robustness Assessment: Adversarial Attacks on Learning-based Quadrupedal Locomotion Controllers
Tarea: Identificar vulnerabilidades en controladores de locomoción quadrúpeda mediante ataques adversarios secuenciales.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) con regularización de Lipschitz, basado en PPO.
Observaciones: Observaciones de sensores como IMU, encoders de articulaciones, y datos de altura desde lidar y cámaras de profundidad.
Acciones: Acciones discretas (objetivos de articulación para controladores basados en PD o parámetros convertibles a salidas de articulaciones).
Recompensa: La recompensa se define como una función que penaliza al agente si el robot no falla (1alive) y suma recompensas auxiliares que facilitan la exploración (rauxt).
Simulador: Simulación con randomización de dominio (DR) para transferencia sim2real.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona el uso de pipelines de simulación paralela para acelerar el aprendizaje.
Líneas base: Controladores basados en RL robustos y técnicas de RL adversarial.
Sim2real: Transferencia de simulación a real mediante randomización de dominio.
Resultado: Se identifican vulnerabilidades en controladores de locomoción quadrúpeda que pueden ser explotadas mediante secuencias adversarias de baja magnitud, y se demuestra que estos controladores pueden ser robustificados mediante el finetuning con muestras adversarias.
Limitaciones: Se reconoce la necesidad de balancear el trade-off entre rendimiento y robustez durante el finetuning.

Título: RobotKeyframing: Learning Locomotion with High-Level Objectives via Mixture of Dense and Sparse Rewards
Tarea: train a locomotion policy for legged robots to meet specified keyframes at required times while maintaining natural behavior during intermediate periods.
Algoritmo (texto): Multi-Critic Proximal Policy Optimization (MuC PPO)
Observaciones: position, orientation, and joint postures
Acciones: continuous, as it involves joint angles
Recompensa: sparse keyframe rewards and dense style/regularization rewards; the mixture is challenging to manage with standard RL frameworks
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: single-critic PPO
Resultado: The multi-critic approach significantly reduces the effort of hyperparameter tuning compared to the single-critic alternative, and the policy successfully guides the robot to meet multiple keyframes at the required times, with better accuracy in reaching them.
Limitaciones: First, if the timing values are infeasible for the specified goals, the robot may fail to meet the targets. Second, our approach inherits the mode collapse issue from the AMP framework, which can be mitigated in future research through the integration of style embeddings. Third, the performance of our policy is currently limited by the motions in the dataset, restricting its ability to generalize to out of distribution motions or targets.

Título: Robust quadruped jumping via deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: learn to jump varying distances and heights for a quadrupedal robot in noisy environments
Algoritmo (texto): Soft-Actor Critic (SAC) with motor dynamics and power constraints
Observaciones: IMU (base position/orientation/velocity), motor angles/velocities, foot positions/velocities/contacts
Acciones: 12-dimensional trajectory offsets in Cartesian space, discrete
Recompensa: sparse reward based on the error between the desired and actual landing position and orientation
Entrenamiento: 13 trajectories, 1000 initial steps, 10^6 replay buffer size, 512 hidden units per layer, 2 hidden layers, 64 batch size, 0.005 target smoothing coefficient, 1 target update interval, 1 gradient steps, 0.99 discount, Adam optimizer, 3·10−4 learning rate
Líneas base: prior work on MIT Cheetah 3 and Unitree A1
Resultado: The method successfully deployed sim-to-real without further tuning, achieving robust and dynamic jumping motions under noisy conditions, with a maximum jump distance of 2 body lengths and a maximum foot disturbance of 6 cm (33% of the robot’s nominal standing height).
Limitaciones: The method relies on extensive simulation with randomized environment parameters and additional techniques such as online parameter adaptation and learned state estimation modules to facilitate sim-to-real transfer.

Título: SRL-VIC: A Variable Stiffness-Based Safe Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Robotic Tasks
Tarea: maze exploration in unstructured environments, specifically for installing electricity cables within walls.
Algoritmo (texto): Safe Reinforcement Learning (SRL) framework incorporating Variable Impedance Control (VIC) and Recovery Policy (RRL).
Observaciones: 6-dimensional vector including 6 force/torque values measured from a F/T sensor, position not given to the safety network.
Acciones: relative position change and desired stiffness vector {Kx, Ky}, discrete or continuous not explicitly stated.
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: scenarios where VIC is absent; scenarios where a recovery mechanism is not implemented
Resultado: The proposed framework outperforms baselines, yielding a good trade-off between efficient task accomplishment and safety guarantee, and can be deployed on a physical robot without fine-tuning.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a scripted procedure for demonstrating collision constraints, which is simpler but may not capture the complexity of long-term tasks.

Título: Sim-to-real transfer of active suspension control using deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: controlar la suspensión activa de un vehículo forestal para manejar terrenos irregulares.
Algoritmo (texto): DRL (Deep Reinforcement Learning) con técnicas de randomización del dominio, penalización por acciones erráticas y memoria en la observación.
Observaciones: posición y velocidad planarias, ángulos de inclinación, fuerzas en los cilindros hidráulicos, mapa local de altura, y acciones previas.
Acciones: velocidad del motor, ángulo de articulación del marco frontal, y posiciones de los ejes de suspensión, todos discretos.
Recompensa: no se especifica directamente, pero se menciona una penalización por acciones erráticas y un objetivo de controlar la postura del vehículo.
Simulador: AGX Dynamics con modelos de terreno y vehículos basados en CAD.
Entrenamiento: no se especifican los detalles específicos, pero se menciona la calibración de parámetros y la transferencia de simulación a realidad.
Líneas base: control pasivo y control automático de suspensión activa
Sim2real: se utiliza transferencia de simulación a realidad con ajustes de parámetros y penalizaciones.
Resultado: los controladores entrenados con penalizaciones para acciones erráticas y memoria en la observación se muestran con un rendimiento similar en simulación y realidad, logrando maniobras suaves y precisas.
Limitaciones: se menciona que los controladores entrenados sin penalizaciones para acciones erráticas muestran control rápido o 'bang-bang', lo que se traduce en un rendimiento inferior en la realidad.

Título: SoloParkour: Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Visual Locomotion from Privileged Experience
Tarea: training end-to-end visual policies for agile and safe quadruped locomotion from depth pixels to robot control commands
Algoritmo (texto): constrained reinforcement learning (RL) with a sample-efficient off-policy RL algorithm (DDPG with CaT) from depth images, using privileged information from a first policy trained with access to cheap-to-compute information about the terrain
Algoritmo (diccionario): DDPG; Profesor-alumno / privilegiado; RL con restricciones (CMDP)
Observaciones: history of proprioceptive measurements, orientation and angular velocity of the base, previous action samples, a command vector vcmd, and depth images
Acciones: desired joint position offsets with respect to a default joint configuration, then converted to torques through a proportional-derivative (PD) controller
Recompensa: measures progress towards a direction below a commanded velocity threshold, with a reward function that is similar to [13]
Entrenamiento: less than 20 hours on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, with a curriculum of terrains with increasing difficulty
Métricas: average terrain completion; success rates; constraint violations
Líneas base: DAgger; Behavior Cloning (BC); Privileged Reconstruction; From Scratch; No Priv. Critic; Visual RL w/o CaT
Resultado: SoloParkour successfully climbs a 40cm step, leaps over a 35cm gap, and crawls under obstacles 20cm above the ground with high repeatability, outperforming supervised distillation baselines on all terrains and at almost all levels of difficulty
Limitaciones: the policy is likely hitting the battery current limits, and current parkour learning approaches require manually constructing simulation terrains for each specific skill

Título: Spatiotemporal Attention Enhances Lidar-Based Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments
Tarea: Pursue the global goal through guidance of the computed path and effectively avoid dynamic obstacles on a local scale.
Algoritmo (texto): deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) architecture
Observaciones: 2D lidar sensor data, the lidar-derived TAGDs, and upcoming waypoints
Acciones: linear and angular velocities (v, w)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: 300,000 episodes, inference and control time step of 0.2s
Métricas: success rate; collision rate; timeout rate; navigation time
Líneas base: Liang et al. [16]; Pérez-D. et al. [15]; de Heuvel et al. [17]
Resultado: Our approach outperforms all baselines in terms of success rate, with a success rate of 86.2% compared to 78.4% for Liang et al. [16] and 77.4% for Pérez-D. et al. [15].
Limitaciones: The approach relies on correct ICP alignment, and the performance decreases when ICP is disabled or when there are no static obstacles.

Título: Symmetry Considerations for Learning Task Symmetric Robot Policies
Tarea: balance a pole on a cart, climb a box, push a cube, and reposition a cube in-hand
Algoritmo (texto): PPO with and without symmetry loss, and PPO with symmetry augmentation
Observaciones: state and action spaces, including symmetry transformations
Acciones: continuous actions, discrete actions for some tasks
Recompensa: L-1 penalty for pole balancing, sparse delayed reward for climbing, dense tracking reward for pushing, and undiscounted reward for repositioning
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: vanilla PPO; PPO with symmetry loss; PPO with symmetry augmentation
Resultado: PPO with symmetry augmentation yields the best performance consistently over all the tasks, with the highest return and fastest convergence while having a low symmetry loss.
Limitaciones: The policies trained with symmetry loss do not consistently recover in phase C of the ANYmal-Climb task, and the augmentation approach struggles when initialized weights are high.

Título: Viability leads to the emergence of gait transitions in learning agile quadrupedal locomotion on challenging terrains
Tarea: learn agile quadruped locomotion on challenging terrains, specifically focusing on gait transitions to improve viability and energy efficiency.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with a combination of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and neural network policies.
Observaciones: Lateral Divergent Component of Motion (DCM) offset, maximal lateral force the robot can withstand before falling, and average body angular velocity.
Acciones: Discrete actions to modulate the Central Pattern Generator (CPG) dynamics or directly change actuation signals.
Recompensa: The reward function includes viability, Cost of Transport (CoT), and peak contact forces. For flat terrain, a high weight is given to viability and a low weight to energy consumption.
Simulador: Not explicitly stated, but simulations are used for training.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions training policies for different velocities and gaits.
Métricas: Gap crossing success rate; Energy efficiency (Cost of Transport, CoT); Periodicity (Coefficient of Variation, CV); Lateral Divergent Component of Motion (DCM) offset; Maximal lateral force the robot can withstand before falling; Average body angular velocity
Líneas base: Animal data from quadruped animals; Energy efficiency (Cost of Transport, CoT); Periodicity (Coefficient of Variation, CV); Lateral Divergent Component of Motion (DCM) offset; Maximal lateral force the robot can withstand before falling; Average body angular velocity
Resultado: The walk-trot transition on flat terrain improved both viability and energy efficiency, with the best performance achieved when high, low, and low weights were given to viability, CoT, and peak contact forces, respectively.
Limitaciones: The concept of viability is difficult to quantify, and detailed behaviors may differ between animals and robots due to distinct body elements and mechanics.

Título: Visual CPG-RL: Learning Central Pattern Generators for Visually-Guided Quadruped Locomotion
Tarea: Learning visually-guided quadruped locomotion by integrating exteroceptive sensing and central pattern generators (CPGs) into the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architectures.
Observaciones: Velocity commands, exteroceptive measurements (terrain height map samples), proprioceptive measurements (IMU, motor angles/velocities, foot contact booleans), and current CPG states.
Acciones: Modulation of intrinsic oscillator amplitudes and phases (discrete), output at 100 Hz.
Recompensa: Primarily tracking body linear and angular velocity commands, minimizing undesired base velocities, penalizing total power, and avoiding collisions with the environment.
Entrenamiento: 4096 Go1s in parallel on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU, 20 seconds episode length, 100 Hz policy output, 1 kHz joint PD controller update rate, 512 hidden units in LSTM, 3 hidden layers in MLP, 128 hidden units per layer in MLP, 256 hidden units per layer in LSTM, 12 parameters sampled during training, 100 Hz policy output, 1 kHz joint PD controller update rate, 100 Hz oscillator state update rate.
Métricas: Linear velocity tracking; Angular velocity tracking; Linear velocity penalty; Angular velocity penalty; Power
Líneas base: Joint-space policy baseline
Sim2real: Intel RealSense cameras (D435i and T265) for exteroceptive sensing, sim-to-real transfer with domain randomization.
Resultado: The CPG, explicit interoscillator couplings, and memory-enabled policy representations are all beneficial for energy efficiency, robustness to noise and sensory delays of 90 ms, and tracking performance for successful sim-to-real transfer for navigation tasks. The policy network outputs modulation signals at 100 Hz, and the torques computed from the mapped desired joint positions are updated at 1 kHz.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method is tested on a physical robot, but the code is not publicly available, and the method has not yet been confirmed from biology for animal navigation.

Título: A Learning Framework for Diverse Legged Robot Locomotion Using Barrier-Based Style Rewards
Tarea: The agent learns to follow the commanded velocity with task-specific preferred gaits and motion styles, including quadruped, tripod, and biped locomotion.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with a relaxed logarithmic barrier reward function.
Observaciones: Linear velocity, foot contact, height around the foot
Acciones: Continuous, as the agent outputs joint positions and velocities
Recompensa: The barrier reward is a weighted sum of relaxed barrier functions for each constraint, guiding the robot towards the desired motion style. The standard regularization reward is also used.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Not stated
