Resultado: The agent can achieve biped, tripod, and quadruped locomotion, including traversing uneven terrain, galloping at 4.67 m/s, and overcoming obstacles up to 58 cm (67 cm for HOUND2).
Limitaciones: The method is sensitive to the specific weights and functions chosen for each reward, potentially affecting training outcomes and leading to inconsistent results.

Título: A Local Information Aggregation-Based Multiagent Reinforcement Learning for Robot Swarm Dynamic Task Allocation
Tarea: Optimizar la asignación de tareas para una swárm de robots en entornos dinámicos.
Algoritmo (texto): LIA MADDPG (Local Information Aggregation Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient)
Observaciones: posiciones, velocidades, ángulos de movimiento de tareas y robots, y la información de tareas y robots de vecinos.
Acciones: seleccionar tareas, acciones discretas
Recompensa: recompensas basadas en la realización de tareas y costos de movimiento, se definen en función de la cantidad de robots asignados a cada tarea y la distancia a la tarea.
Entrenamiento: no se especifica
Líneas base: MAAC; MAPPO; seis algoritmos de aprendizaje por refuerzo convencionales; un algoritmo heurístico
Resultado: LIA MADDPG demostró ser superior en términos de velocidad de convergencia, estabilidad y escalabilidad, especialmente en tareas que involucran un mayor número de robots.
Limitaciones: El estudio se centra en entornos dinámicos pero no en cambios continuos de ubicación de tareas, y enfrenta el desafío de la explosión dimensional en grandes tareas de asignación de tareas.

Título: An End-To-End Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Modular Task Allocation Framework for Autonomous Mobile Systems
Tarea: coordinar múltiples AMRs para realizar misiones multitarea, específicamente, generar un plan cooperativo para K robots para visitar un conjunto de waypoints, con cada robot comenzando y terminando en la misma ubicación, formando trayectorias cerradas para los robots.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) basado en aprendizaje de red profunda, con arquitecturas de red como Perceptrón Multicapa (MLP) y Mixture of Experts (MoE).
Observaciones: waypoints en el espacio de trabajo, incluyendo la localización y orientación del robot.
Acciones: acciones discretas para asignar subconjuntos de waypoints a cada robot, con acciones continuas para planificar la secuencia de ejecución de cada robot visitando los waypoints asignados a él.
Recompensa: La recompensa se define en términos de la eficiencia y la optimización del camino recorrido por los robots, minimizando el tiempo de ejecución y maximizando la cobertura de los waypoints.
Simulador: simulador basado en el Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) y pruebas en entornos reales.
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un número específico de pasos, episodios o horas de entrenamiento, ni el hardware utilizado.
Métricas: tiempo de ejecución, optimidad del camino, cobertura de los waypoints.
Líneas base: algoritmos heurísticos, métodos basados en aprendizaje de máquina, y soluciones de optimización matemática.
Sim2real: transferencia de entrenamiento desde simulación a la realidad mediante la implementación en un hardware multi-robot basado en ROS 2.
Resultado: El enfoque propuesto reduce el hueco de optimización y la velocidad de cálculo en más del 40% y 90% respectivamente, en comparación con varias soluciones de mTSP de vanguardia, lo que demuestra el rendimiento superior alcanzado. Se validó el enfoque en un hardware multi-robot y se completó la misión de inspección de almacén de manera autónoma.
Limitaciones: Se reconoce que el enfoque propuesto tiene un alto grado de adaptabilidad en términos del número de tareas para la asignación, pero no se mencionan limitaciones adicionales.

Título: Attention-based map encoding for learning generalized legged locomotion
Tarea: Learning generalized legged locomotion on diverse terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with an attention-based map encoding, using a convolutional neural network (CNN) and multi-head attention (MHA) module.
Observaciones: Terrain features sampled from elevation mapping, proprioceptive observations.
Acciones: Discrete foot placements.
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but inferred to be related to successful traversal and robustness against uncertainties.
Simulador: Simulated environments with various terrains, including grid stones, pallets, beams, and gaps.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be extensive given the detailed training stages and terrains.
Métricas: Success rate; Velocity tracking errors; Stuck and failure rates
Líneas base: DTC; Baseline RL
Sim2real: Transfer from simulation to real robots through fine-tuning.
Resultado: The proposed method achieved 100% success rate in traversing a challenging obstacle parkour with disturbances and uncertainties, outperforming DTC and baseline RL in terms of velocity tracking errors and success rates on various terrains.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the quality of proprioceptive observations and may struggle with highly uncertain environments.

Título: Constrained Reinforcement Learning Using Distributional Representation for Trustworthy Quadrotor UAV Tracking Control
Tarea: accurate and reliable tracking control for quadrotors in complex dynamic environments
Algoritmo (texto): Constrained Distributional REinforced-Disturbance-estimator (ConsDRED) for disturbance estimation, combined with Stochastic Model Predictive Control (SMPC)
Observaciones: position, linear velocity, orientation, angular velocity, thrust, torque, aerodynamic effect
Acciones: discrete, simplified affine disturbance feedback
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: simulation platform, VID-Fusion for wind estimation
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: CRPO [14]; other methods in Table I
Resultado: ConsDRED-SMPC framework substantially improves accumulative tracking errors by at least 70% compared with the recent art.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: DNN Task Assignment in UAV Networks: A Generative AI Enhanced Multiagent Reinforcement Learning Approach
Tarea: Distribuir tareas de DNN en un sistema de UAVs para minimizar el tiempo de información en edad (AoI) y equilibrar el uso de recursos.
Algoritmo (texto): MADDPG con Generative Diffusion Models (GDM), llamado GDM-MADDPG.
Observaciones: Posiciones y coordenadas de los objetivos a inspeccionar, tamaños de datos en la zona de la tarea, estado de recursos restantes de los UAVs.
Acciones: Asignación de tareas de DNN, acciones discretas.
Recompensa: La recompensa se define en términos de minimización del AoI, equilibrio de carga y eficiencia de la asignación de tareas, con un objetivo de utilidad que combina la contribución individual de cada UAV, la tasa de completación del trabajo y el equilibrio de la carga de los UAVs.
Simulador: No se especifica un simulador específico, pero se menciona un sistema de UAVs con una formación fija.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se utilizan UAVs con modelos de DNN entrenados.
Métricas: AoI; Tasa de completación de tareas; Equilibrio de carga
Líneas base: Métodos de asignación de tareas existentes; Métodos de planificación de ruta existentes
Sim2real: No se menciona ninguna técnica de transferencia de sim a real.
Resultado: El algoritmo GDM-MADDPG se muestra como superior a los métodos de referencia en términos de planificación de ruta, AoI, tasa de completación de tareas y utilidad del sistema.
Limitaciones: Se reconoce la complejidad del problema como NP-hard y la necesidad de un enfoque que considere tanto variables discretas como continuas.

Título: Discrete-Time Hybrid Automata Learning: Legged Locomotion Meets Skateboarding
Tarea: Enabling a quadrupedal robot to skateboard, which involves handling mode transitions and contact events in a hybrid underactuated system.
Algoritmo (texto): Discrete-time Hybrid Automata Learning (DHAL), with a multi-critic architecture and a Beta distribution policy embedded in a reinforcement learning pipeline.
Observaciones: Joint positions, joint velocities, base roll, base pitch, base yaw, base angular velocity, gravity, contact information, and torque.
Acciones: Discrete actions for each leg's hip and thigh joints, with continuous values for the rest of the joints.
Recompensa: Sparse contact-based rewards for gliding and pushing phases, with additional sim2real critic rewards for smooth gliding and balancing on the skateboard.
Simulador: Simulation environment with a skateboard model and a position PD controller for the truck mechanism.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Smooth gliding and balancing on the skateboard
Líneas base: Model-based control; Model-free reinforcement learning (RL)
Resultado: The Unitree Go1 robot was able to perform smooth and natural skateboarding motions, with reliable mode identification and transitions under disturbances, demonstrating robust performance and mode identification consistent with human intuition.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the assumption that all states are continuous-valued, and the approach is not yet generalized to high-dimensional systems or complex real-world dynamics.

Título: Distributional Soft Actor-Critic With Three Refinements
Tarea: Continuous control tasks (e.g., humanoid, ant, half-cheetah, walker2d, inverteddoublependulum, hopper, pusher, reacher, swimmer, bipedalwalker, bipedalwalker-hardcore, and carracing).
Algoritmo (texto): Distributional Soft Actor-Critic with Three Refinements (DSAC-T or DSACv2), an off-policy RL algorithm based on Distributional Soft Policy Iteration (DSPI).
Observaciones: State and state-action distributions induced by the policy π, including physical positions and velocities of the robot’s joints, three-channel pixel values for the image-input-based task (CarRacing).
Acciones: Continuous actions (torque applied to joints for vector-input tasks, acceleration/braking and steering for the image-input-based task).
Recompensa: Positive rewards for maintaining good posture and moving toward the goal, negative rewards for failing to complete the task or applying excessive torque, and small negative rewards for the car to finish the race quickly, and positive rewards for reaching checkpoints.
Simulador: OpenAI Gym interface, including 11 vector-input-based control tasks and one image-input-based control task.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions that the algorithm is evaluated across a diverse set of benchmark tasks.
Métricas: Performance across a diverse set of benchmark tasks
Líneas base: SAC, TD3, DDPG, TRPO, and PPO
Resultado: DSAC-T outperforms or matches lots of mainstreaming model-free RL algorithms, including SAC, TD3, DDPG, TRPO, and PPO, across all benchmark tasks.
Limitaciones: The paper acknowledges that DSAC-T requires task-specific hyperparameter tuning, which is inconvenient in fast task setups.

Título: FACET: Force-Adaptive Control via Impedance Reference Tracking for Legged Robots
Tarea: control legged robots to achieve compliant and force-adaptive behaviors under external forces, specifically to improve robustness and reduce collision impulses.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a teacher-student framework, using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for training the student actor.
Robot: Go2 quadruped, G1 humanoid, B1+Z1 quadruped with mounted arm
Observaciones: position and velocity of the robot's center of mass (CoM), and external forces and torques applied to the system.
Acciones: joint position targets, continuous
Recompensa: defined as the difference between the robot's state and the reference state generated by the virtual mass-spring-damper system, aiming to minimize tracking error.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: vanilla policy (velocity tracking); robust policy (additional random impulse domain randomizations)
Sim2real: teacher-student training recipe for sim-to-real transfer
Resultado: The quadruped robot can survive impact forces exceeding twice its weight and significantly reduce the force required to either stop or move it, achieving an 80% reduction in collision impulse.
Limitaciones: The method assumes the system is near static, such that the force at the end-effector can be approximated by the external force applied, and it requires reliable sensing of external forces which is infeasible due to the absence of force sensors in most robots.

Título: FALCON: Learning Force-Adaptive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
Tarea: Performing force-adaptive loco-manipulation tasks such as transporting payloads, cart-pulling, and door-opening.
Algoritmo (texto): Dual-agent reinforcement learning (RL) framework with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for training the agents.
Observaciones: Whole-body proprioception and commands
Acciones: Discrete joint angle targets for the lower-body and continuous joint angle targets for the upper-body
Recompensa: Defined through a dual-goal-conditioned policy learning problem with separate rewards for locomotion and manipulation goals.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Upper-Body Joints Tracking Error; Root Velocity Tracking Error
Líneas base: Lower-RL-Upper-IK; Monolithic-Whole-body-RL; PD-w/o-Force-Curr.; PD-Force-Curr.; PID-Force-Curr.; PD-ID-Force-Curr.; M-WB-RL w/o-Force-Curr.; M-WB-RL with-Force-Curr.
Resultado: FALCON achieves 2× more accurate upper-body joint tracking compared to baselines while maintaining robust locomotion under force disturbances and achieving faster training convergence. Policies trained with FALCON are deployed across multiple humanoids, enabling forceful loco-manipulation tasks such as transporting payloads (0-20N force), cart-pulling (0-100N), and door-opening (0-40N) in the real world.
Limitaciones: The method requires careful tuning of the force curriculum and joint torque limits, and the performance may vary across different joint configurations.

Título: JaxRobotarium: Training and Deploying Multi-Robot Policies in 10 Minutes
Tarea: learning complex and scalable coordination behaviors in multi-robot systems
Algoritmo (texto): PQN, QMIX, MAPPO, IPPO
Observaciones: unicycle dynamics model, waypoint navigation, collision avoidance
Acciones: discrete actions (waypoints, commands to robots)
Recompensa: defined by task performance metrics (e.g., success rate, resource foraging, deliveries, etc.)
Simulador: Jax-RPS, a Jax-based simulator for the Robotarium
Entrenamiento: up to 20x more timesteps and higher returns compared to MARBLER, with support for GPU/TPU execution, parallelization, and just-in-time compilation
Líneas base: MARBLER; IsaacGym; IsaacLab; Cambridge RoboMaster; MuSHR; Duckietown; Robotarium; Google Research Football; BenchMARL
Resultado: JaxRobotarium can train for up to 20x more timesteps and achieve consistently higher returns compared to MARBLER given the same amount of time, with support for GPU execution, parallelization, and just-in-time compilation.
Limitaciones: only simulates the Robotarium GRITSBots, does not simulate observations from more complex perception modules, limited partial observability in most scenarios, differences in quadratic problem solvers between deployment and simulation.

Título: Learning Multi-Agent Loco-Manipulation for Long-Horizon Quadrupedal Pushing
Tarea: collaborative long-horizon pushing tasks by multiple quadrupedal robots in environments with obstacles.
Algoritmo (texto): hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework, with an RRT planner and a centralized adaptive policy at the high level, and decentralized goal-conditioned policies at the mid-level.
Algoritmo (diccionario): UVFA / políticas condicionadas por meta; MARL (genérico); PRM / RRT / RRT*
Observaciones: 2D position and yaw angle of the object, state of other robots, and obstacle state, all computed in the local torso frame of the robot.
Acciones: velocity commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: success rate; reduction in completion time
Líneas base: Sombolestan et al. [18]; Jeon et al. [21]; Sombolestan et al. [22]; Nachum et al. [23]; An et al. [24]; Xiong et al. [25]
Resultado: The proposed method achieves a 36.0% higher success rate and a 24.5% reduction in completion time compared to the best baseline approach in simulation, and can be deployed on real robots to successfully complete obstacle-aware, long-horizon Push-Cuboid and Push-T tasks.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge the large sim-to-real gap in learning-based low-level controllers, and the need for domain randomization to reduce this gap.

Título: Learning Smooth Humanoid Locomotion through Lipschitz-Constrained Policies
Tarea: training policies to produce smooth behaviors for humanoid robots
Algoritmo (texto): Lipschitz-Constrained Policies (LCP) with a gradient penalty
Robot: Fourier GR1T1; Fourier GR1T2; Unitree H1; Berkeley Humanoid
Observaciones: current observation and a history of past observations
Acciones: continuous, as indicated by the smoothness metrics and task returns
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: action jitter; DoF position jitter; DoF velocity; energy; base acceleration; task return
Líneas base: no smoothing; smoothness rewards; low-pass filters
Resultado: LCP produces smooth behaviors that are comparable to policies trained with explicit smoothness rewards, achieving similar task returns in real-world deployment and sim-to-sim transfer, with λgp = 0.002 providing a good balance between policy smoothness and task performance.
Limitaciones: The effectiveness of LCP is limited to basic walking behaviors, and further evaluation on more dynamic skills such as running and jumping is needed.

Título: Learning a Unified Policy for Position and Force Control in Legged Loco-Manipulation
Tarea: 学习统一的力和位置控制策略，以实现位置跟踪、力控制和顺应性响应等行为。
Algoritmo (texto): 强化学习（RL），使用Isaac Gym进行模拟。
Robot: Unitree B2-Z1 四足机器人平台; Unitree G1 人形机器人
Observaciones: 机器人基座方向、角速度、关节位置、关节速度、前一个动作、命令和脚的时钟计时。
Acciones: 输出残差添加到预定义默认姿态，并计算关节位置目标。
Recompensa: 奖励准确跟踪目标末端执行器位置和基座速度，同时使用MSE损失提高状态估计器的准确性。
Entrenamiento: 6000步滚动，使用随机生成的末端执行器轨迹进行位置跟踪评估。
Métricas: 位置跟踪误差; 力控制误差
Líneas base: 仅基于位置控制的策略
Sim2real: 通过在真实机器人上应用力命令并测量末端执行器力来验证。
Resultado: 在三种具有挑战性的接触丰富任务中，基于位置的模仿学习基线方法的成功率提高了约39.5%。
Limitaciones: 需要进一步研究将末端执行器和机器人基座集成的统一推导。

Título: Learning coordinated badminton skills for legged manipulators
Tarea: The task the agent learns is to play badminton, specifically to track and return shuttlecocks during gameplay with human opponents.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with an asymmetric actor-critic formulation, incorporating a shuttlecock perception model based on real-world camera data.
Observaciones: The agent observes the shuttle position computed in the camera frame, state estimation, and trajectory prediction.
Acciones: The agent outputs joint position commands for all 18 robot drives, with actions being continuous.
Recompensa: The reward is defined based on the final perception error and the ability to intercept the shuttlecock, with specific levels of difficulty for different parts of the court.
Simulador: The training was conducted in simulation, with the perception noise model using real-world camera data.
Entrenamiento: The training budget is not explicitly stated, but the experiments involved multiple rallies and a streak of 10 shots in a single rally.
Métricas: interception success rates; swing velocity tracking; active perception capabilities; adaptive locomotion strategies
Líneas base: FOV Reward policy; No Perception policy
Sim2real: The method is tested on a physical robot, and the results are validated in hardware experiments.
Resultado: The robot achieved a peak executed swing velocity of 12.06 m/s, with a success rate of 99.9% in hitting shuttlecocks across different parts of the court, and it was capable of consecutive hits with a streak of 10 shots in a single rally.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the rectangular FOV of the robot makes it challenging to maintain continuous visual contact with the shuttlecock, especially when it approaches from directly overhead or behind.

Título: Learning to control and coordinate mixed traffic through robot vehicles at complex and unsignalized intersections
Tarea: control and coordination of mixed traffic (human-driven vehicles and robot vehicles) at complex, unsignalized intersections
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with a decentralized training and centralized execution paradigm
Observaciones: local perception and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication
Acciones: high-level decision of whether to enter or not enter the intersection (discrete)
Recompensa: accounts for traffic efficiency and potential conflicts, with specific metrics like average waiting time
Simulador: high-fidelity traffic reconstruction and simulation using real-world traffic data
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: traditional traffic light control
Resultado: With 60% or more RVs, the method outperforms traditional traffic light control in terms of traffic efficiency, reducing the average waiting time of all vehicles by 25.9% and 40.7% at 70% and 90% RV penetration rates, respectively. With 100% RVs, the average waiting time is reduced by 42% compared to traffic light control and 89% compared to the traffic light absence baseline.
Limitaciones: The method is not yet tested on a physical robot, and the authors acknowledge the need to address challenges in modeling and controlling mixed traffic due to the diversity and suboptimality of human drivers.

Título: Long-horizon Locomotion and Manipulation on a Quadrupedal Robot with Large Language Models
Tarea: tasks that require strategic high-level reasoning, such as turning off a light, delivering a package, building a bridge, and riding an elevator.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) for motion planning and control, with a high-level reasoning layer based on large language models (LLMs) that generate hybrid discrete-continuous plans.
Observaciones: state variables and sensor data, including AprilTags and a RealSense D430 camera for pose estimation.
Acciones: discrete and continuous actions, generated as executable robot code.
Recompensa: evaluated using a success rate and a normalized distance metric specific to the task, with the distance metrics normalized by the initial distance.
Simulador: simulator with domain randomization and observation noise, using AprilTags and a RealSense D430 camera.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: RoboTool; hierarchical RL
Sim2real: techniques for transferring from simulation to the real robot, including domain randomization and replan-on-failure.
Resultado: the system achieves a success rate of 0.877 in the light switching task and 0.770 in the package delivery task, with a normalized distance of 0.100 and 0.136 respectively, outperforming RoboTool and hierarchical RL.
Limitaciones: the system is limited to a fixed set of low-level robot skills and has not been thoroughly evaluated in highly complex or unstructured failure cases.

Título: MARVEL: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Constrained Field-of-View Multi-Robot Exploration in Large-Scale Environments
Tarea: plan the shortest trajectory to fully map/cover an unknown environment through efficient robot coordination
Algoritmo (texto): multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with graph attention networks, using an attentive privileged critic network and an information-driven action pruning strategy
Observaciones: graph Gt = (Vt, Et) with nodes representing accessible locations and edges representing collision-free paths, and frontier distributions Ft
Acciones: viewpoint selection, with discrete actions corresponding to neighboring nodes
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: 2D indoor environments, Crazyflie 2.1 drones in a 4m by 4m arena
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: average trajectory length; success rate; overlap ratio; computation times
Líneas base: Nearest; MMPF; NBVP
Resultado: MARVEL outperforms all baselines in average trajectory length, achieving a 14.2% improvement over the best baseline with four agents, and has a perfect 100% success rate in all tests, demonstrating superior stability and generalization.
Limitaciones: MARVEL excels in 2D indoor settings but acknowledges the added complexity of 3D environments with intricate obstacles, planning to extend MARVEL to handle full 3D action spaces by integrating height information and associated FoV changes.

Título: MoE-Loco: Mixture of Experts for Multitask Locomotion
Tarea: traverse various terrains and perform different locomotion modes, including bipedal and quadrupedal gaits.
Algoritmo (texto): PPO with Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture
Observaciones: proprioception, explicit privileged state, implicit privileged state, and command
Acciones: 12 joint positions, discrete (quadrupedal or bipedal gait)
Recompensa: defined based on the gait command, with different components for quadrupedal and bipedal locomotion
Entrenamiento: 40,000 iterations for plane walking, 80,000 iterations on challenging terrain tasks, 10,000 iterations for adaptation to pure proprioception input
Métricas: success rate; average pass time; average travel distance
Líneas base: Ours w/o MoE; RMA
Resultado: The method achieved a success rate of 0.879 for mixed bar tasks with quadrupedal gait, and 0.956 for mixed bar tasks with quadrupedal gait in simulation, with an average travel distance of 89.41 meters and an average pass time of 230.98 seconds.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a complex architecture and requires substantial engineering efforts for reward design and pretraining.

Título: Multi-AUV Cooperative Underwater Multi-Target Tracking Based on Dynamic-Switching-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Underwater multi-target tracking using a multi-AUV system.
Algoritmo (texto): Hierarchical Software-defined Multi-AUV Reinforcement Learning (HSARL) with Dynamic-Switching mechanism, including Dynamic-Switching Attention and Dynamic-Switching Resampling mechanisms.
Observaciones: Sonar detection results, location information, and echo intensity from the target and other AUVs.
Acciones: Discrete actions (up, down, left, right, forward, backward, and stay in place).
Recompensa: Tracking accuracy, collision avoidance, ocean current stability, and energy efficiency.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Tracking accuracy; Collision avoidance; Ocean current stability; Energy efficiency
Líneas base: CTDE; PPM-BBD; DRSIR; MADDPG
Resultado: The proposed DSBM tracking algorithm can perform precise underwater multi-target tracking, comparing with many of recent research products in terms of various important metrics.
Limitaciones: The method faces challenges in managing and cooperating a complex multi-agent system, especially in dynamic and unpredictable marine environments, due to high variance and slow convergence problems in traditional MARL algorithms.

Título: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Persistent Monitoring with Sensing, Communication, and Localization Constraints
Tarea: Determine motion policies for each agent in a multi-agent system to persistently monitor a given environment considering limited sensing, communication, and localization constraints.
Algoritmo (texto): Graph Localized Proximal Policy Optimization (GALOPP), a multi-agent proximal policy optimization algorithm coupled with a graph convolutional neural network.
Observaciones: 2-channel image input: first channel is the locally observed visibility map (local map), second channel is an independently maintained version of the global map (mini-map) compressed to match the dimensions of the local map.
Acciones: Discrete actions, generated by the actor network in the GALOPP architecture.
Recompensa: The objective is to minimize the net penalty accumulated over time, which is the negative reward for not monitoring a cell. The reward is set to 0 when a cell is within the sensing range of an agent, otherwise, it decays linearly with a decay rate.
Simulador: Open maps with obstacles, two different environments: 2-room and 4-room.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Performance compared to baselines: random search, random search with ensured communication, and greedy search
Líneas base: random search; random search with ensured communication; greedy search
Resultado: GALOPP outperforms the baselines in terms of persistent monitoring performance.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the problem of determining motion policies for the agents considering the localization, sensing, and communication range constraints jointly has not been adequately addressed in the literature.

Título: Nav-R1: Reasoning and Navigation in Embodied Scenes
Tarea: Navigate to the bedroom and find a bed.
Algoritmo (texto): Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)-based reinforcement learning framework
Observaciones: Egocentric RGB-D views, scene point cloud, and language instructions
Acciones: Discrete actions (e.g., move forward, turn left, turn right, stop)
Recompensa: Three complementary rewards: format, understanding, and navigation. Format reward ensures structural adherence, understanding reward captures semantic correctness and visual grounding, and navigation reward optimizes path fidelity and endpoint accuracy.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: R2R [4]; R2R-CE [29]; RxR-CE [30]; SOON [57]; OVON [52]; Nav-CoT-110K (Ours)
Resultado: Nav-R1 achieves an average improvement of 8% compared to strong baselines across dialogue, reasoning, planning, and navigation tasks, and further demonstrates robust performance when deployed on a physical robot with limited on-board resources.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a large-scale dataset and requires cloud-based inference for real-world deployment, which may limit its scalability and real-time performance.

Título: Online Planning for Multi-UAV Pursuit-Evasion in Unknown Environments Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: multi-UA V pursuit-evasion in unknown environments
Algoritmo (texto): MARL-based algorithm (OPEN) with an evader-prediction-enhanced network and an adaptive environment generator
Observaciones: states, including the evader's position and the presence of obstacles
Acciones: collective thrust and body rates (CTBR) control commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated in detail, but the method aims to maximize the capture rate of the evader
Entrenamiento: not stated in detail, but the method aims to achieve near 100% capture rates across four test scenarios
Líneas base: traditional methods; MARL baselines
Sim2real: calibrated dynamics models of UA Vs, two-stage reward refinement
Resultado: The method outperforms all baselines with a clear margin and maintains a 100% capture rate in unseen scenarios, demonstrating strong generalization.
Limitaciones: The method is limited to the specific task of multi-UA V pursuit-evasion and may not generalize to other tasks.

Título: Rambo: RL-Augmented Model-Based Whole-Body Control for Loco-Manipulation
Tarea: loco-manipulation tasks, such as pushing a shopping cart, balancing a plate, and holding soft objects
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with a model-based whole-body controller (WBC) as a feedforward torque generator
Observaciones: end-effector position and contact forces
Acciones: torque commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: precision in tracking end-effector targets; robustness in typical locomotion tasks
Líneas base: model-based methods; learning-based methods
Resultado: RAMBO enables precise manipulation capabilities while achieving robust and dynamic locomotion
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Real-World Reinforcement Learning of Active Perception Behaviors
Tarea: learn active perception behaviors to compensate for the limitations of various sensory setups in robots, ranging from entirely blind robots operating purely from proprioception, to robots operating with sophisticated multi-camera setups.
Algoritmo (texto): asymmetric advantage weighted regression (AAWR), which extends advantage weighted regression (AWR) to incorporate privileged, training-time only observations.
Robot: Sim. Koch; Real Koch; Real Franka
Observaciones: privileged sensors (e.g., object detectors, segmentation masks) and partial observations (e.g., wrist camera, joint positions)
Acciones: discrete actions (e.g., grasping, moving to different viewpoints)
Recompensa: defined as the rate at which the policy successfully completes the task, the number of steps taken to complete the task, and the search behavior (whether the target appears in the camera frame, the policy approaches the target, and the policy remains fixated on the target after 5 timesteps)
Simulador: simulated environments for the simulated tasks, real robots for the real tasks
Entrenamiento: 20K to 100K offline steps, 80K to 900K online steps, depending on the task
Líneas base: AWR; BC; Distillation; VIB; Exhaustive; VLM+π0
Resultado: AAWR outperforms all prior approaches in synthesizing reliable active perception behaviors in 8 different settings, including simulated and real robots, and varied tasks. It efficiently generates information-gathering behaviors that allow the robot to operate under severe partial observability for manipulation tasks.
Limitaciones: AAWR requires access to privileged sensors during training, which may not always be available in real-world scenarios.

Título: Reinforcement learning for versatile, dynamic, and robust bipedal locomotion control
Tarea: learn dynamic locomotion controllers for bipedal robots, including walking, running, and jumping.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with a dual-history architecture, specifically a model-free approach
Observaciones: long and short input/output (I/O) history of the robot
Acciones: discrete or continuous joint-level inputs
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: tracking errors; robustness to unexpected disturbances
Líneas base: model-based optimal control (OC); RL with a short I/O history
Resultado: The proposed RL framework can reproduce a wide variety of locomotion skills, including robust walking, fast running, and versatile jumping, with significant robustness to unexpected disturbances in the real world.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the model-based OC community is making strides toward developing general tracking controllers, but these still rely on task-specific optimized trajectories.

Título: Residual Policy Learning for Perceptive Quadruped Control Using Differentiable Simulation
Tarea: learn locomotion and perceptive navigation for a quadruped
Algoritmo (texto): First-Order Policy Gradients (FoPG) with Backpropagation through Time (BPTT) and Analytical Policy Gradients (APG)
Observaciones: 16x12 depth camera input, proprioceptive inputs
Acciones: continuous, output of an MLP network
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Zeroth-Order Policy Gradients (ZoPGs); Backpropagation through Time (BPTT); Analytical Policy Gradients (APG); Short-Horizon Actor-Critic (SHAC); IsaacGym
Resultado: The method achieved blind locomotion and perceptive navigation for a quadruped in minutes, improving asymptotic rewards compared to sample efficiency for model-free RL.
Limitaciones: The method faces challenges in contact-rich tasks due to jagged loss landscapes and poor gradient conditioning, and requires closed-loop control for faster trotting and enhanced gait stability.

Título: Robust Ladder Climbing with a Quadrupedal Robot
Tarea: learn quadrupedal ladder climbing via reinforcement learning-based control policy
Algoritmo (texto): Interior-point Policy Optimization (IPO) with a multi-layer perceptron for encoding IMU observation history
Observaciones: proprioceptive observations, IMU history, ladder state, and ladder pose
Acciones: joint position targets, discrete
Recompensa: defined by equations in Table I, including position tracking, heading tracking, base motion, joint dynamics, action rate, action smoothness, foot slippage, flat orientation, stand still, and collision penalties
Entrenamiento: 15,000 epochs for teacher policy, 5,000 epochs for student policy, 4.5 days on NVIDIA RTX 3090
Líneas base: traditional ball-foot policy
Sim2real: technique used to transfer from simulation to the real robot, or 'not stated'
Resultado: 96% average success rate in simulation across all configurations tested, 90% success rate in real-world tests at ladder angles ranging from 70° to 90°, 232× faster climbing speed than the state of the art
Limitaciones: performance gap between simulation and real-world tests at 90° ladder angle due to unmodeled standoffs

Título: Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Behavior-Based Cooperative Navigation
Tarea: 移动机器人团队将形成中心的质心导航到目标位置，同时避免与静态障碍物和其他机器人碰撞，并保持预定义的机器人间距离。
Algoritmo (texto): 软演员-评论家算法（SAC）扩展到多智能体领域，采用集中训练分散执行（CTDE）方案。
Observaciones: 激光雷达读数，两个邻居的距离和角度，质心目标的距离，最近障碍物的距离和角度，机器人之间的参考距离，以及上一个时间步的机器人动作。
Acciones: 线性和角速度控制。
Recompensa: 奖励函数包括到达目标的稀疏奖励、碰撞或停滞的稀疏奖励、保持队形的奖励、保持安全距离的奖励以及引导质心接近目标的奖励。
Entrenamiento: 使用软演员-评论家算法（SAC），采用集中训练分散执行（CTDE）方案，训练预算未明确给出。
Métricas: 平均队形误差; 达到的目标数量
Líneas base: 多智能体深度确定性策略梯度（MADDPG）; 多智能体扩展的软演员-评论家（SAC）
Sim2real: 通过使用分布式模型预测控制（MPC）安全过滤器确保在真实机器人上训练时无碰撞。
Resultado: 使用MPC安全过滤器的多智能体强化学习方法在模拟和真实机器人上实现了无碰撞的行为基协同导航，减少了训练所需的回合数，并且在真实机器人上训练是安全的。
Limitaciones: 研究主要集中在行为基协同导航的安全学习上，但未详细讨论如何处理更复杂的任务或环境变化。

Título: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Mobile Robots with Reinforcement Learning: from NVIDIA Isaac Sim to Gazebo and Real ROS 2 Robots
Tarea: local planning and obstacle avoidance for mobile robots
Algoritmo (texto): Advantage Actor-Critic, Soft Actor-Critic, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: Lidar ranges, information on the target’s relative position, and the robot’s state
Acciones: discrete (actions for moving the robot based on policy decisions)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Nav2
Resultado: The RL policies trained in Isaac Sim achieved comparable performance to Nav2, demonstrating the potential for sim-to-real transfer in mobile robot navigation.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Target Search and Navigation in Heterogeneous Robot Systems with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Collaborative search and navigation in a mine tunnel environment.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization 2 (PPO2)
Robot: UGV (Unmanned Ground Vehicle) and UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle)
Observaciones: Laser observations (Li) and ego-state observations (Oi). Direction measurements (dir) with respect to the UAV.
Acciones: Discrete actions for both UGV and UAV, with UGV following the UAV's trajectory.
Recompensa: The reward is defined based on the success of the search and navigation task, with the UAV finding the victim and the UGV reaching the target point.
Simulador: Simulation environment with a top-down view of the mine tunnel, including walls and randomly appearing victims.
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Métricas: Success rate of the search and navigation task
Líneas base: Existing baseline methods
Resultado: The proposed method achieved a high success rate in simulated environments, outperforming existing baseline methods.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the UAV to provide the trajectory, which may not be feasible in all real-world scenarios.

Título: The Cambridge RoboMaster:An Agile Multi-robot Research Platform
Tarea: running classical model-based control, zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of multi-agent navigation tasks, running distributed visual SLAM, and utilizing large neural networks to estimate relative poses and track trajectories.
Algoritmo (texto): linear quadratic regulator (LQR) for Freyja, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) policies trained in VMAS
Observaciones: 3D attitude sensor, wheel encoders, body velocity sensors, battery level sensors, two camera CSI inputs (Raspberry Pi HQ camera with fisheye lens), physical bumper sensors
Acciones: discrete velocity commands in the robot’s body frame, low-level wheel speed commands, continuous velocities
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: position and velocity tracking error, reference and measured position and velocity, time
Líneas base: classical model-based control (Freyja), multi-agent navigation tasks
Sim2real: zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of multi-agent navigation tasks
Resultado: The platform combined with the Freyja controller suite demonstrated efficient single-agent trajectory tracking in straight and circular trajectories, with position and velocity tracking errors reported.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: VR-Robo: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Framework for Visual Robot Navigation and Locomotion
Tarea: reaching the target cone of a specified color within a limited time horizon, relying solely on ego-view RGB observation and proprioception.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for scene reconstruction
Observaciones: RGB only, ego-centric visual observation
Acciones: discrete actions for navigation and motion control
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: domain randomization, system identification, conditional generative models, LucidSim
Resultado: VR-Robo achieves effective navigation and locomotion policies in complex, real-world scenarios using RGB-only observations, demonstrating zero-shot Sim-to-Real policy transfer.
Limitaciones: The method relies on multi-view RGB images and does not explicitly mention the use of depth sensors, lidar sensors, or SLAM, which could be limitations in certain real-world scenarios.

Título: Whole-Body End-Effector Pose Tracking
Tarea: The task is to track the end-effector pose (position and orientation) across a large workspace and varying terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a game-based curriculum
Observaciones: Terrain mesh, coarse terrain height map, base poses, and joint angles
Acciones: Continuous joint actions
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the paper mentions tracking accuracy and pose reachability as goals.
Entrenamiento: 4000 robots in parallel, not stated how many episodes or steps
Líneas base: Model-based controllers; Existing RL approaches
Resultado: The learned controller achieves a pose-tracking error of 2.64 cm and 3.64°, outperforming existing competitive baselines.
Limitaciones: The paper acknowledges that the method is tested on a simulated environment and the real robot, but does not mention any specific limitations.

Título: Wildfire Front Monitoring With Multiple UAVs Using Deep Q-Learning
Tarea: monitoring a wildfire front with multiple autonomous UAVs
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Q-Learning (DQN) with multiple single-trained agents (MSTA) and value decomposition networks (VDN)
Observaciones: grid cells with fuel, burning status, and ignition probability
Acciones: displacement in grid cells (north, east, west, or south for multi-copter; changing bank angle for fixed-wing)
Recompensa: negative score for unmonitored burning cells; higher score for cells that are monitored
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: independent learners; joint agent
Resultado: our proposed methods outperform state-of-the-art approaches in a wildfire front monitoring task with up to 9 fixed-wing and multi-copter UAVs
Limitaciones: the stochastic model is simplified and may not capture all real-world complexities

Título: A Hybrid Technique for Active SLAM Based on RPPO Model With Transfer Learning
Tarea: explorar y mapear entornos desconocidos, evitando obstáculos y navegando de forma autónoma.
Algoritmo (texto): RPPO (Relational Proximal Policy Optimization) con convolución separable profunda y procesamiento en lote de datos.
Robot: no se menciona un robot específico
Observaciones: RGB images from a Kinect camera
Acciones: velocidades lineales y angulares continuas
Recompensa: recompensa basada en la rotación, colisiones y velocidad lineal y angular; se define una función de recompensa que penaliza la rotación y las colisiones, y recompensa la velocidad lineal y angular del robot.
Simulador: no se menciona un simulador específico
Entrenamiento: no se proporciona un presupuesto de entrenamiento
Líneas base: RPPO sin convolución separable profunda; RPPO sin procesamiento en lote de datos
Sim2real: no se menciona una transferencia de simulación a la realidad
Resultado: El algoritmo RPPO con convolución separable profunda y procesamiento en lote de datos logró una recompensa acumulada de 1200 en el experimento, mejorando la eficiencia de la exploración y la navegación autónoma del robot.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que la transferencia de aprendizaje a entornos desconocidos dinámicos y estáticos podría ser un desafío.

Título: Actor–Critic Model Predictive Control: Differentiable Optimization Meets Reinforcement Learning for Agile Flight
Tarea: flying a quadrotor through a race track
Algoritmo (texto): Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control (AC-MPC), which combines actor-critic reinforcement learning with a differentiable MPC module
Observaciones: observations to the cost function
Acciones: discrete (control commands)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: superhuman performance; speeds of up to 21 m/s
Líneas base: AC-MLP; L1-MPC
Resultado: The proposed AC-MPC architecture achieves superhuman performance in drone racing, attaining speeds of up to 21 m/s on a real quadrotor platform, on par with state-of-the-art model-free reinforcement learning.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Agile and Generalized Legged Locomotion via Attention-Based Neural Map Encoding
Tarea: Achieving agile and generalized legged locomotion across diverse terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with an Attention-based Map Encoder (AME-2) as the core feature extractor for the mapping input.
Observaciones: Elevation maps, local elevations with uncertainties, odometry, depth observations, proprioception.
Acciones: Joint PD targets, discrete actions at 50 Hz.
Recompensa: Goal-reaching rewards that maximize the probability of reaching position and heading goals.
Simulador: Parallel simulation with depth cloud and odometry.
Entrenamiento: Not stated in detail, but mentions training with ground-truth mapping in simulation and student policy training with proposed mapping under teacher supervision.
Métricas: Not explicitly stated, but the paper focuses on agility and generalization to unseen terrains.
Líneas base: DTC, RLOC, other RL-based methods, classical mapping methods, and recent off-road navigation approaches.
Sim2real: The same mapping pipeline runs both in parallel simulation and on the real robots, enabling online mapping during training.
Resultado: The resulting controllers exhibit strong agility and robust generalization to a wide range of terrains, with the proposed mapping pipeline producing high-quality elevation maps in real time.
Limitaciones: The method still shows some limitations in terms of zero-shot generalization to previously unseen environments, and the computational costs of the models in [52] are too high for deployment.

Título: DPL: Depth-Only Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion via Realistic Depth Synthesis and Cross-Attention Terrain Reconstruction
Tarea: Humanoid robot locomotion on diverse and challenging terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with multi-teacher distillation and adversarial reinforcement learning.
Observaciones: Egocentric depth inputs and proprioceptive history.
Acciones: Continuous actions for locomotion, discrete for stair traversal.
Recompensa: Defined by a discriminator that evaluates state transitions, with a focus on human-consistent motion.
Entrenamiento: 4096 parallel instances on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU for control policy, 2048 parallel environments on an A100 GPU for terrain reconstructor.
Métricas: Mean Absolute Error (MAE); Success rate; Traversing rate
Líneas base: CNN-based; ResNet-based; w/o GRU; w/o Condition; Ours
Sim2real: Physically grounded noise pipeline for depth images.
Resultado: The proposed method achieved a mean absolute error of 3.25±0.56 cm across terrains, with a success rate of 96% and a traversing rate of 92% on stairs, outperforming baselines.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a depth camera and may struggle with occluded or blind regions, though it addresses this with a self-occlusion-aware ray casting technique.

Título: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Real-World Humanoid Robot Locomotion Control with Automatic Reward Learning
Tarea: control de locomoción en robots humanoides
Algoritmo (texto): bilevel optimization framework (incluye Soft Actor-Critic y Proximal Policy Optimization)
Observaciones: posición y velocidad de las articulaciones
Acciones: acciones de control de locomoción, discretas o continuas
Recompensa: no se especifica en el resumen, pero se menciona que se aprende automáticamente
Entrenamiento: no se especifica en el resumen
Métricas: eficiencia de aprendizaje, rendimiento en simulaciones y en el mundo real
Líneas base: Soft Actor-Critic, Proximal Policy Optimization, métodos basados en recompensas manuales
Resultado: el método propuesto mejora significativamente la eficiencia de aprendizaje y logra un rendimiento superior a las recompensas manuales tanto en simulaciones como en el mundo real, y se transfiere con éxito al robot real Unitree G1
Limitaciones: el método aún requiere transferencia de simulación a real, lo que puede ser un desafío

Título: Deep reinforcement learning for multi-agent coordination
Tarea: collective pellet retrieval in crowded environments
Algoritmo (texto): Stigmergic Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (S-MADRL) based on Deep Q-Network (DQN)
Observaciones: local observations of the environment
Acciones: discrete actions to retrieve pellets
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG)
Resultado: The S-MADRL framework can effectively learn decentralized coordination behaviors for up to eight agents in stochastic environments, outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms like MADDPG which fail to scale beyond two agents.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge the limitations of the approach in achieving scalability and convergence, particularly in highly constrained environments.

Título: Deep reinforcement learning with enhanced PPO for safe mobile robot navigation
Tarea: autonomous navigation in a complex environment, avoiding obstacles
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with an enhanced neural network structure
Observaciones: laser readings across 30 dimensions, the robot’s past linear and angular velocities, target position relative to the robot, robot’s yaw angle, and orientation required to face the target
Acciones: continuous linear and angular velocities
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)
Resultado: The proposed approach significantly improves the navigation performance of the non-holonomic mobile robot in both obstacle and obstacle-free environments, demonstrating the effectiveness of the enhanced PPO algorithm for mapless motion planning.
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: DreamWaQ++: Obstacle-Aware Quadrupedal Locomotion With Resilient Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn obstacle-aware quadrupedal locomotion
Algoritmo (texto): proximal policy optimization (PPO) with a multi-modal perception module
Observaciones: proprioception, exteroception (3D voxel, IMU, joint position, joint velocity, body orientation, body angular velocity)
Acciones: continuous (torque commands)
Recompensa: maximize the expected discounted future rewards in a POMDP setting
Simulador: simulated quadrupedal locomotion with extensive domain randomization
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: performance in traversing various challenging environments
Líneas base: blind locomotion controllers, classical model-based control
Resultado: The controller demonstrated remarkable performance in traversing various challenging environments, including stairs, gaps, and deformable terrains, with a single neural network without specialized training for a particular scenario.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a single neural network and may struggle with diverse environmental changes if the learned latent representation does not account for explorative behavior that promotes skill discovery.

Título: From knowing to doing: Learning diverse motor skills through instruction learning
Tarea: learn different locomotion behaviors for biped and quadruped robots, including stepping, walking, and various gaits.
Algoritmo (texto): instruction learning, which combines a feedforward action with a feedback action learned by reinforcement learning
Robot: Ranger Max; Unitree A1; Unitree Go1
Observaciones: joint angles, body pitch and roll angles, and possibly velocity and orientation
Acciones: joint angle trajectories (feedforward) and neural network output (feedback), both discrete or continuous
Recompensa: a combination of a velocity reward and a mimic reward in imitation learning, but only a velocity reward in instruction learning
Entrenamiento: 10 seconds to complete 10k training steps, 1 million steps for biped and 3 million steps for quadruped robots
Líneas base: imitation learning; classical reinforcement learning
Sim2real: domain randomization, adding random disturbances, and using a smaller feedback ratio
Resultado: instruction learning can learn various gaits in about 2.78 hours in real time, with high efficiency and flexibility, and can be transferred to real robots with some modifications
Limitaciones: the sim-to-real transfer is not always successful and requires careful tuning, and the online learning requires a large field for experiments

Título: MAGICS: Adversarial RL with Minimax Actors Guided by Implicit Critic Stackelberg for Convergent Neural Synthesis of Robot Safety
Tarea: yield robust control policies for robot safety, specifically for legged locomotion tasks
Algoritmo (texto): Minimax Actors Guided by Implicit Critic Stackelberg (MAGICS), a novel adversarial reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm
Observaciones: state and control inputs, disturbance inputs
Acciones: continuous, from deep neural networks
Recompensa: defined as the discounted reach-avoid game, with a probabilistic interpretation of the discount factor γ
Simulador: OpenAI Gym environments, specifically Pendulum and Half Cheetah
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: ablation study; baseline methods
Resultado: MAGICS outperforms the state-of-the-art neural safety synthesis methods, achieving significantly higher reward and robust control policies
Limitaciones: The method is limited to local convergence and may not guarantee global optimality, and the discount factor γ can affect the probabilistic interpretation of the results

Título: MobileVLA-R1: Reinforcing Vision-Language-Action for Mobile Robots
Tarea: Go to specific locations and perform actions like avoiding obstacles, navigating through gaps, and manipulating objects.
Algoritmo (texto): Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) reinforcement learning, with a two-stage training paradigm that includes supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on CoT-annotated data.
Observaciones: RGB, depth, and point cloud observations
Acciones: Continuous locomotion commands (Vx, Vy, ωyaw, α) and discrete high-level actions
Recompensa: Movement reward for smooth and stable trajectories, action reward for discrete control behaviors, and format reward for structured reasoning consistency
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: CMA∗; Sim2Sim∗; GridMM∗; Ego2-Map∗; DreamWalker∗; Reborn∗; ETPNav∗; HNR∗; AG-CMTP; R2R-CMTP; InstructNav; LAW; CM2; WS-MGMap; AO-Planner; Seq2Seq; CMA; NaVid; Uni-NaVid; NaVILA; VLN-R1; OctoNav; StreamVLN; CorrectNav; MobileVLA-R1 (Ours)
Resultado: MobileVLA-R1 achieves approximately a 5% improvement in success rate over strong baselines and outperforms all methods that do not rely on simulator-pretrained waypoint predictors, even when those methods leverage additional inputs such as depth, panoramic views, and odometry.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a large-scale dataset and may not generalize well to unseen environments or tasks without further training.

Título: Parkour in the wild: Learning a general and extensible agile locomotion policy using multi-expert distillation and RL fine-tuning
Tarea: Crossing different terrains and obstacles using agile locomotion policies.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning, DAgger algorithm for distillation
Observaciones: Depth images, proprioceptive information, task commands
Acciones: Continuous, as inferred from the context
Recompensa: Defined through multiple reward terms including tracking position, joint velocity, torque, base acceleration, feet acceleration, action rate, feet force, collision avoidance, and standing at target
Simulador: Simulated environment combining all terrains used for expert training, 3D scans of real-world search and rescue facilities
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Líneas base: Model-Predictive Control (MPC); Teacher-student approach; Hybrid MPC-RL approaches; Foundation models
Resultado: The policy achieved significant performance improvements over existing methods in synthesizing multi-terrain skills into a single controller, and was successfully deployed on the ANYmal D robot in real-world environments, demonstrating agility and robustness in navigating complex terrains.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a diverse set of terrains and obstacles for training, and the performance drops in unstructured terrains where the policy cannot properly guess unseen parts of obstacles.

Título: Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy-Aware Coverage Path Planning for Precision Agriculture
Tarea: planear rutas de cobertura eficientes que maximicen la cobertura del área mientras se conserva la energía y se garantiza el retorno a las estaciones de recarga.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) con arquitectura de red que combina convolucional, atención múltiple y LSTM.
Robot: no se menciona un robot específico
Observaciones: mapa de obstáculos, estaciones de recarga, posición actual del robot, mapa de cobertura
Acciones: acciones discretas (arriba, abajo, izquierda, derecha)
Recompensa: recompensa que equilibra la cobertura, la eficiencia energética y la seguridad, con pesos para cada factor
Entrenamiento: 50,000 episodios, 128 unidades ocultas en LSTM, hardware NVIDIA RTX 3090
Métricas: recompensa total; tasa de cobertura; número de violaciones; eficiencia energética
Líneas base: RRT; PSO; ACO
Resultado: el algoritmo SAC logra una tasa de cobertura superior a 90% en todos los entornos simulados, reduciendo las violaciones de restricciones en un 83-85% en comparación con RRT, y superando a los métodos basados en heurísticas en un 7.3%, 8.0% y 9.1% en cobertura para los mapas 1, 2 y 3 respectivamente.
Limitaciones: la eficiencia de la convergencia disminuye con la complejidad del entorno, y la robustez a cambios en los parámetros es moderada.

Título: Self-Supervised Multisensory Pretraining for Contact-Rich Robot Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn expressive multisensory representations for contact-rich manipulation tasks
Algoritmo (texto): MultiSensory Dynamic Pretraining (MSDP), based on masked autoencoding
Observaciones: Proprioception, Force Torque (FT) sensor, Vision
Acciones: Continuous, through a special pooling of sensor embeddings for the actor, and via a cross-attention layer for the critic
Recompensa: Not explicitly stated, but related to the discounted sum of rewards in the POMDP framework
Entrenamiento: 6,000 online interactions, less than 55 minutes including data collection and pretraining
Líneas base: SAC; RLPD
Resultado: Achieved near-optimal performance in only 6,000 online interactions, leading to high success rates on the real robot
Limitaciones: Not explicitly stated, but the authors acknowledge the scalability and robustness of the approach

Título: Task Assignment and Exploration Optimization for Low Altitude UAV Rescue via Generative AI Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Minimizar el tiempo de finalización de las tareas y el consumo de energía de los UAVs, y maximizar la tasa de offloading de tareas a los GERs.
Algoritmo (texto): HG-MADDPG, que combina el algoritmo de Hungarian con un modelo de difusión generativo (GDM)-basado en MADDPG para optimizar la asignación de tareas y la exploración.
Observaciones: Trajectoria, observación de obstáculos, distribución de potencia de los GERs
Acciones: Selección de tareas y asignación de recursos, control de trayectoria
Recompensa: No se especifica directamente, pero se infiere que se relaciona con el tiempo de finalización de las tareas y el consumo de energía.
Simulador: Simulador de la tarea de rescate
Entrenamiento: No se especifica
Métricas: Tiempo de finalización de las tareas; Consumo de energía; Tasa de offloading de tareas
Líneas base: GER to UAV; UAV to UAV; UAV to GER; This work
Resultado: La propuesta del trabajo reduce significativamente el tiempo de finalización de las tareas, el consumo de energía y mejora la tasa de offloading de tareas en comparación con los métodos basados en la literatura.
Limitaciones: Se reconocen limitaciones en la capacidad de los UAVs para realizar tareas de baja latencia y la complejidad de la optimización en entornos dinámicos.

Título: Towards bridging the gap: Systematic sim-to-real transfer for diverse legged robots
Tarea: Robust and efficient locomotion for legged robots.
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement learning with a physics-grounded energy model for PMSMs, using a fixed-base excitation driven system identification pipeline.
Observaciones: Joint positions and velocities.
Acciones: Discrete actions for velocity tracking, energy consumption, collision avoidance, and foot-touchdown.
Recompensa: Four independently weighted terms: velocity tracking, energy consumption, collision avoidance, and foot-touchdown.
Entrenamiento: Not stated.
Líneas base: Cassie and BDX droids; Joint-centric methods; Body-centric methods; Hybrid strategies
Resultado: The method improves the energetic efficiency over state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 32% reduction in the full Cost of Transport of ANYMAL (1.27).
Limitaciones: The method relies on fixed-base joint excitation and does not use locomotion rollouts or motion priors, which may limit its applicability in some scenarios.

Título: Traversability-Aware Legged Navigation by Learning From Real-World Visual Data
Tarea: Learn to navigate through real-world environments while avoiding obstacles and hard-to-traverse terrains, minimizing traversal costs.
Algoritmo (texto): Hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) with an actor-critic method, using both online and offline data.
Observaciones: Color and depth vision sensors, proprioceptive feedback
Acciones: Continuous actions for locomotion control
Recompensa: Defined based on the traversability cost of the terrain, encouraging the robot to avoid high-cost regions and reach goals efficiently.
Entrenamiento: 15 minutes of real-world training, using both online and offline data
Métricas: Traversability cost estimation accuracy; Generalization to unseen scenarios
Líneas base: Baseline methods
Resultado: The proposed framework achieved the best performance in accurate traversability cost estimation and efficient learning from multi-modal data, enabling the quadrupedal robot to navigate through various real-world environments with challenging terrains in 15 minutes of training.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the robot’s proprioceptive feedback and may not generalize well to different types of terrains without further training.

Título: X-Nav: Learning End-to-End Cross-Embodiment Navigation for Mobile Robots
Tarea: Learning end-to-end cross-embodiment navigation for mobile robots, including wheeled and quadrupedal robots.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with privileged observations, followed by general policy distillation using imitation learning (IL) with a transformer model (Nav-ACT).
Algoritmo (diccionario): Imitation learning (genérico); Profesor-alumno / privilegiado; Transformers en RL (GTrXL…)
Observaciones: Depth images and proprioceptive observations (joint positions, joint velocities, base velocity, gravity projected in the base frame, IMU data).
Acciones: Low-level control commands for wheeled robots (linear and angular velocities) and quadrupedal robots (desired joint positions).
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the objective is to minimize travel distance.
Simulador: Simulated environments for training, photorealistic environments for validation.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions training with an increasing number of randomly generated embodiments.
Líneas base: Imitation learning (IL) methods; Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods
Resultado: X-Nav achieved zero-shot transfer to both unseen embodiments and photorealistic environments, with performance improving when trained with an increasing number of randomly generated embodiments.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge the need for more extensive validation in real-world environments and the potential for performance degradation in complex terrains.

Título: ZEST: Zero-shot embodied skill transfer for athletic robot control
Tarea: Learn and transfer a wide range of physical skills (e.g., army crawl, breakdancing, box-climbing) to different robots (Atlas, Unitree G11, Spot) from diverse data sources (motion capture, monocular video, animation).
Algoritmo (texto): Reinforcement Learning (RL) with an adaptive sampling strategy and a model-based assistive wrench for curriculum learning.
Observaciones: High-fidelity motion capture, noisy monocular video, and non-physics-constrained animation.
Acciones: Continuous actions for robot control.
Recompensa: Not stated explicitly, but the framework avoids extensive reward shaping and contact labels.
Simulador: High-fidelity simulation with moderate domain randomization.
Entrenamiento: Not stated explicitly, but the framework is trained entirely in simulation.
Métricas: Not stated explicitly, but the framework demonstrates remarkable generality across different robots and behaviors.
Líneas base: Not stated explicitly, but the framework circumvents the need for complex behavior discovery from scratch.
Resultado: ZEST learns dynamic, multi-contact skills from diverse data sources and transfers them to different robots, demonstrating remarkable generality.
Limitaciones: The framework avoids extensive reward shaping and contact labels, which might limit its performance in complex real-world scenarios.

Título: CAD2RL: Real single-image flight without a single real image
Tarea: choose actions for indoor navigation that avoid collisions with obstacles, such as walls and furniture
Algoritmo (texto): Monte Carlo policy evaluation, with a deep convolutional neural network for Q-function approximation
Observaciones: single RGB images from a monocular camera
Acciones: velocity commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: several baselines, a prior learning-based method that predicts turning directions [14]
Resultado: policies trained entirely in simulation outperform baseline methods and are able to navigate effectively around many kinds of obstacles, using only monocular images as input
Limitaciones: policies trained entirely in simulation do experience some collisions in the real world

Título: Curiosity-driven Exploration for Mapless Navigation with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn navigation policies for mapless navigation, where the agent needs to navigate to a target without the map of the environment, using low-cost localization solutions.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) with Intrinsic Curiosity Module (ICM) as a variant of DRL.
Observaciones: 72-dimensional laser range readings and 3-dimensional relative goal position.
Acciones: discrete actions: go straight for 0.06 m, turn left 8°, turn right 8°.
Recompensa: Extrinsic reward is a combination of reaching the goal, collision, and position/orientation penalties. Intrinsic reward is based on the prediction error of the ICM.
Simulador: simulated 2D environments with different floor plans.
Entrenamiento: 3 million iterations, approximately 15 hours using only CPU computation.
Líneas base: A3C-; Entropy; ICM; ICM+Entropy
Resultado: ICM+Entropy achieved the best performance with a success rate of 100% and an average of 75.160 ± 52.075 steps on Map1, and better generalization capabilities on Map2,3,4.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a simulated environment and the success rate on unseen maps is not as high as on the training map.

Título: Learning symmetric and low-energy locomotion
Tarea: Learning locomotion behaviors for various character morphologies (biped, humanoid, quadruped, hexapod) without using motion examples, finite state machines, or morphology-specific knowledge.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with modifications to the loss function and curriculum learning method.
Observaciones: Observations include joint angles and velocities, and possibly other kinematic variables.
Acciones: Continuous actions representing joint torques or muscle activations, output as a vector.
Recompensa: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions a reward function that does not include motion examples or morphology-specific terms.
Simulador: Simulated environments for different character morphologies.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the paper mentions a training process that involves learning without the mirror symmetry loss, learning without the curriculum, and learning without either component.
Métricas: Symmetry of actions; Energy consumption; Speed-appropriate gait patterns
Líneas base: Learning without the mirror symmetry loss; Learning without the curriculum; Learning without either component
Resultado: The agent learns locomotion behaviors that are symmetric, low-energy, and exhibit speed-appropriate gait patterns, without the need of motion examples, contact planning, and additional morphology-specific terms in the reward function.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a curriculum learning approach and may not generalize well to all types of tasks or morphologies without further tuning.

Título: The option keyboard combining skills in reinforcement learning
Tarea: El agente debe aprender a combinar conocimientos (skills) para realizar nuevas tareas en problemas de gestión de recursos y navegación.
Algoritmo (texto): Option Keyboard, que combina el uso de cumulantes y opciones (options) para combinar skills.
Observaciones: Estados y acciones del entorno, y posiblemente variables de estado adicionales.
Acciones: Acciones discretas, ya que se menciona la selección de acciones en un teclado.
Recompensa: No se especifica cómo se define la recompensa, pero se menciona que se combina en el espacio de cumulantes.
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se usan múltiples cumulantes y opciones.
Líneas base: No se mencionan líneas base o métodos comparados.
Resultado: El agente puede combinar skills aprendidas para realizar nuevas tareas, como caminar y coger un objeto al mismo tiempo, con un alto rendimiento.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que la combinación de cumulantes no siempre puede ser implementada como una alternancia de las acciones subyacentes.

Título: Autonomous exploration under uncertainty via deep reinforcement learning on graphs
Tarea: autonomous exploration in an a priori unknown environment, where the robot must choose sensing actions that curb localization uncertainty and achieve information gain.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
Observaciones: exploration graph containing previous poses, landmarks, and candidate frontier nodes
Acciones: choosing a frontier node to visit, discrete
Recompensa: defined based on the utility function of the EM exploration algorithm, with an additional term penalizing the travel distance associated with an exploratory action
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical exploration methods, learning-aided information-theoretic approaches, and graph-based exploration methods
Resultado: The proposed method achieves a nearly constant-time, real-time viable decision-making process, yielding accurate maps and high rates of information gain.
Limitaciones: The performance in test is unstable because the size of the graph is always changing throughout the exploration process, and the hyperparameters of the loss function are hard to tune.

Título: DenseCAvoid: Real-time Navigation in Dense Crowds using Anticipatory Behaviors
Tarea: safe robot navigation in dense crowds
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with a modified network and reward function
Observaciones: raw data from a 2-D lidar, raw image data from either a depth or an RGB camera, relative position of the goal with respect to the robot, robot’s current velocity, and predicted positions of pedestrians in the next frame
Acciones: continuous space consisting of the linear and angular velocities of the robot
Recompensa: minimization of the mean arrival time of the robot to its goal
Simulador: complex 3-D simulations of indoor environments with pedestrians and static obstacles
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: rates of reaching the goal; occurrence of the freezing robot problem
Líneas base: classical navigation methods; learning-based collision avoidance methods; other learning-based methods for navigation in dense scenes
Resultado: Our method increases rates of reaching the goal by up to 74% and reduces the occurrence of the freezing robot problem by up to 48% compared to times when prediction was not used.
Limitaciones: The method may not work well on dense crowds, and the training scenarios are quite different from the synthetic training data.

Título: Neural Simplex Architecture
Tarea: target-seeking ground rover navigating an obstacle field and a neural controller for an artificial pancreas system.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) with safe learning strategy, using reinforcement learning for online retraining.
Robot: target-seeking ground rover, artificial pancreas system
Observaciones: plant state or raw sensor readings
Acciones: continuous control inputs
Recompensa: defined as a function of the forward switching condition (FSC) and a performance-related reward function (rperf), with unrecoverable actions penalized by a negative number (runrecov).
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: not stated
Resultado: NSA improved the safety of the neural controller while maintaining or improving its performance, demonstrated through case studies of a target-seeking ground rover and a neural controller for an artificial pancreas system.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the choice of reverse switching logic does not affect safety but is application-dependent, and that the approach may degrade performance if noisy actions are directly used to control the plant.

Título: Safety Augmented Value Estimation from Demonstrations (SAVED): Safe Deep Model-Based RL for Sparse Cost Robotic Tasks
Tarea: navigation and manipulation, knot-tying on the da Vinci surgical robot
Algoritmo (texto): Safety Augmented Value Estimation from Demonstrations (SA VED), a variant of deep model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) inspired by deep model predictive control (MPC) and robust control
Observaciones: states and control inputs, task completion only
Acciones: continuous, based on control inputs
Recompensa: only indicates task completion, defined as convergence to a goal set without violating constraints
Simulador: 6 standard simulation benchmarks, physical knot-tying task on the da Vinci surgical robot
Entrenamiento: less than an hour, not stated specific steps or episodes
Métricas: success rate; constraint satisfaction rate; sample efficiency
Líneas base: 3 state-of-the-art model-free and model-based RL baselines
Resultado: SA VED outperforms baselines with a success rate of over 75% in the first 50 training iterations, compared to baselines succeeding less than 5% of the time
Limitaciones: challenges in designing dense cost functions, need for suboptimal but constraint-satisfying demonstrations

Título: A Novel Hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic Algorithm for Multi-Logistics Robots Task Allocation
Tarea: 分配多物流机器人任务，以提高无人仓库拣选效率。
Algoritmo (texto): Hierarchical Soft Actor-Critic (HSAC)，基于Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)。
Observaciones: 包含其他机器人信息的观察，具体传感器或状态变量未明确说明。
Acciones: 离散动作，通过Actor网络输出。
Recompensa: 通过完成子目标获得内在奖励，同时最大化熵。
Entrenamiento: 训练预算和硬件未给出。
Líneas base: SAC算法
Resultado: HSAC算法在仿真环境中不同场景下，使多物流AGV机器人协同工作，相比SAC算法提高了奖励约2.61倍。
Limitaciones: 未明确说明，但可能涉及实际机器人平台的具体实现细节。

Título: Adaptive and extendable control of unmanned surface vehicle formations using distributed deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: adaptar y extender el control de formaciones de vehículos superficiales no tripulados (USVs) mediante un algoritmo de aprendizaje por refuerzo distribuido.
Algoritmo (texto): DDPG (Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient), un algoritmo de aprendizaje por refuerzo basado en gradientes de política.
Robot: no se menciona un robot específico, se usan simulaciones.
Observaciones: posición, velocidad, ángulo de dirección, aceleración y velocidad angular.
Acciones: acciones continuas (aceleración y velocidad angular), discretas para los seguidores.
Recompensa: no se especifica explícitamente, pero se menciona que se utilizan recompensas para entrenar el algoritmo.
Entrenamiento: no se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona que se usaron 5 semillas.
Métricas: errores de distancia y ángulo de la formación; recompensas acumuladas
Líneas base: algoritmos de control clásicos
Sim2real: no se menciona una transferencia de simulación a realidad.
Resultado: el algoritmo DDPG logró que las formaciones de USVs se adaptaran a diferentes puntos de objetivo, aumentaran el número de USVs y mantuvieran diferentes formas de formación, con errores de distancia y ángulo de formación mínimos.
Limitaciones: se menciona que el algoritmo requiere un entrenamiento inicial para aprender estrategias generales, pero no se detalla más.

Título: Blind Bipedal Stair Traversal via Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: traverse stair-like terrain without any external perception or terrain models.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LSTM recurrent neural network, with dynamics randomization.
Algoritmo (diccionario): PPO; PPO recurrente (LSTM/GRU); Aleatorización del dominio; Políticas recurrentes (LSTM/GRU)
Observaciones: pelvis orientation, angular velocity of the pelvis, joint positions, joint velocities, command inputs, two cyclic clock inputs for each leg
Acciones: 11-dimensional vector of PD targets for the joints and a clock delta for regulating stepping frequency, discrete
Recompensa: penalizes large magnitudes of foot forces and foot velocities, encourages smooth actions, energy efficiency, and reducing pelvis shakiness
Simulador: simulated Cassie environment with dynamics randomization
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical and RL
Resultado: The learned controller achieved robust locomotion over a variety of real-world stairs and other stair-like disturbances using only proprioception, with minimal modifications to an existing flat-terrain training RL framework.
Limitaciones: The method relies on a known domain randomization and may not generalize well to completely unknown terrains.

Título: Dynamics Randomization Revisited: A Case Study for Quadrupedal Locomotion
