Tarea: Learning robust locomotion policies for the Laikago quadruped robot.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with actor-critic architecture
Observaciones: Robot state (position, orientation, joint angles, velocities) and user commands
Acciones: Residual PD joint target, discrete
Recompensa: Reward is a weighted sum of joint, position, and orientation errors, with additional time-varying components
Simulador: Isaac Gym with a GPU-accelerated simulator
Entrenamiento: 10^3 iterations, 2.4×10^8 samples, 6-8 hours per policy on a single GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPU
Líneas base: Dynamics randomization; No dynamics randomization
Sim2real: Transfer from simulation to the real robot without dynamics randomization
Resultado: Demonstrated that dynamics randomization is not necessary for successful sim-to-real transfer, across multiple gaits and speeds, while robust to common types of perturbations.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that domain randomization is neither necessary nor sufficient in some settings, and advocate for conservative application of dynamics randomization.

Título: Efficient Learning of Goal-Oriented Push-Grasping Synergy in Clutter
Tarea: grasping a pre-assigned goal object in clutter, which involves pushing to enable stable grasps.
Algoritmo (texto): goal-conditioned hierarchical reinforcement learning, with a discriminator (grasp net) and a generator (push net) for training.
Algoritmo (diccionario): HRL (genérico); UVFA / políticas condicionadas por meta
Robot: UR5 arm with an RD2 gripper (in simulation), not stated (in real world)
Observaciones: color heightmaps, depth heightmaps, and masks of the goal object
Acciones: discrete push actions and discrete grasp actions
Recompensa: grasping the goal object gives a reward, pushing actions are rewarded based on their contribution to future grasps, defined by a Q-value threshold
Entrenamiento: 350 episodes for the grasp net, 500 episodes for the push net, 1000 episodes for the grasp net in the final stage, not stated hardware
Métricas: completion; grasp success rate; motion number
Líneas base: grasping-only; goal-conditioned VPG; grasping the invisible
Resultado: The method outperforms existing methods in task completion rate and goal grasp success rate with less motion, achieving 99% completion and 90% grasp success rate in the real world.
Limitaciones: The method requires a 3D model of the goal object for the initial training stage, and the performance in goal-agnostic conditions is not as good as in goal-oriented conditions.

Título: LaND: Learning to Navigate from Disengagements
Tarea: autonomously navigate in diverse, real-world environments
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with a predictive model, specifically a convolutional recurrent neural network
Observaciones: 96×192 RGB image from a front-facing 170◦ field-of-view monocular camera
Acciones: steering angle, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: outperforms state-of-the-art imitation learning and reinforcement learning approaches
Líneas base: imitation learning; reinforcement learning
Resultado: LaND can successfully learn to navigate in diverse, real world sidewalk environments, outperforming both imitation learning and reinforcement learning approaches
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Smooth Exploration for Robotic Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: control a tendon-driven elastic robot, locomotion tasks (half cheetah, ant, hopper, walker 2D) and additional real robotics tasks (quadruped and RC car)
Algoritmo (texto): generalized State-Dependent Exploration (gSDE), adapted to recent Deep RL algorithms like SAC and PPO
Algoritmo (diccionario): PPO; SAC; Policy search (PGPE, PoWER, gSDE)
Robot: tendon-driven elastic robot, quadruped, RC car
Observaciones: state variables (tendon lengths, tendon forces, current pose, target pose)
Acciones: desired delta in tendon forces, discrete
Recompensa: weighted sum of negative geodesic distance to desired orientation and negative Euclidean distance to desired position, with a small continuity cost to reduce oscillations
Entrenamiento: 1 million steps, 10 runs, 20 evaluation episodes every 10000 steps, 2 hours for real robot training
Líneas base: no exploration noise; unstructured Gaussian noise; correlated noise (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process); adaptive parameter noise; low-pass filter
Resultado: gSDE achieved a good compromise between unstructured exploration and correlated noise, with better performance and lower continuity cost compared to other methods, especially for training on a real robot
Limitaciones: high computational cost for accurate modeling of the soft robot, limited to low-dimensional tasks

Título: Visual Navigation in Real-World Indoor Environments Using End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: find its goal given by an image in a real-world office environment
Algoritmo (texto): Parallel Advantage Actor-Critic (PAAC) algorithm with off-policy critic updates, using a single deep neural network
Observaciones: visual output of the camera mounted on the robot, and an image of the goal
Acciones: discrete set of allowed actions, with a new 'terminate' action
Recompensa: positive or negative reward based on the distance to the goal, or after a predefined maximum number of steps
Simulador: a novel, fast, and realistic 3D environment simulator based on Quake III Arena and DeepMind Lab
Entrenamiento: 30 hours on a single GPU
Líneas base: end-to-end DRL methods in simulated environments; methods relying on other types of input apart from the camera images
Resultado: In 30 navigation experiments, the robot reached a 0.3-meter neighborhood of the goal in more than 86.7% of cases
Limitaciones: The method requires a lot of training samples and the training process is computationally demanding

Título: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Precise Soccer Shooting Skills using a Quadrupedal Robot
Tarea: Enable a quadrupedal robot to perform precise soccer shooting skills by learning a control policy and a planning policy using hierarchical reinforcement learning.
Algoritmo (texto): Hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) with deep neural networks, using model-free RL to train a control policy and a planning policy.
Observaciones: The robot observes the current motion indicator, desired Bézier parameters, trajectory timespan, current motion phase, robot's current and past states, and a history of past actions.
Acciones: The agent outputs desired robot motor positions, which are continuous.
Recompensa: The reward is not explicitly stated in the provided text, but it is implied that the reward is related to the accuracy of the shooting and the stability of the robot during the maneuver.
Entrenamiento: The training environment is developed in MuJoCo, with a training budget not explicitly stated but implied to be extensive given the complexity of the task. The hardware is not specified.
Métricas: Accuracy of shooting the ball to the target; Stability of the robot during the maneuver
Líneas base: Classical model-based methods; End-to-end deep reinforcement learning methods
Resultado: The A1 quadrupedal robot was able to accurately shoot a soccer ball to a randomly given target in the real world, demonstrating the feasibility of attaining a robust control policy for dynamic soccer shooting motions and a precise planning policy to shoot a deformable soccer ball to a random specified target in a relatively large range.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that transferring policies learned in simulation to real legged robots is challenging due to differences between the dynamics of the simulator and the physical system.

Título: Learning Free Gait Transition for Quadruped Robots Via Phase-Guided Controller
Tarea: train a phase-guided controller for multiple gaits and free transitions for a quadruped robot.
Algoritmo (texto): phase-guided reinforcement learning (RL) with LSTM neural network, using PPO algorithm for training.
Observaciones: velocity commands, phases, and the state of the robot
Acciones: desired joint positions, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: about 3 hours on a workstation with intel i9-10900X CPU and RTX 2080Ti GPU
Líneas base: CPG; manually designed functions
Resultado: The controller can reproduce all learned gaits and free transitions robustly on the hardware, with gait similarity ranging from 0.78 to 0.95 and velocity error ranging from 0.04 to 0.16 m/s.
Limitaciones: The method requires a large amount of training time and computational resources, and the transition process may not be smooth for complex gaits.

Título: Learning Minimum-Time Flight in Cluttered Environments
Tarea: minimum-time flight through a sequence of waypoints in cluttered environments while avoiding obstacles
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (RL) combined with classical topological path planning
Observaciones: position, velocity, unit quaternion rotation, body rates, and rotor speeds
Acciones: optimal control commands, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: state-of-the-art methods
Resultado: The proposed method achieves 100% success rate of flying minimum-time policies without collision, while traditional planning and control approaches achieve only 40%. The learned policy outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of flight time in all tested scenarios that feature complex geometries.
Limitaciones: The method struggles with high sample complexity and nonconvexity of the task, and the learned policy may not generalize well to environments with a large number of obstacles.

Título: Multi-robot Cooperative Pursuit via Potential Field-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Cooperative pursuit of an evader by multiple robots in an environment with obstacles.
Algoritmo (texto): D3QN-based adaptive cooperative pursuit algorithm, combining deep reinforcement learning with artificial potential field method.
Observaciones: distance to the nearest obstacle, distance to the evader, distance to teammates, and corresponding bearing angles
Acciones: continuous actions, parameter pairs (η, λ)
Recompensa: The reward is defined based on the distance to the evader and the success of capturing the evader, with additional rewards for avoiding collisions and covering more area.
Entrenamiento: 1000 episodes, 7000 training steps, Adam optimizer, learning rate 3×10−4, discount factor 0.99, ε-greedy exploration
Líneas base: vanilla RL algorithm; modified APF method
Resultado: The proposed DACOOP algorithm achieved a success rate of 94% in simulations, significantly outperforming the modified APF method (14.6%). In experiments, the learned policy was deployed on differential wheeled robots and demonstrated adaptability to different scenarios.
Limitaciones: The algorithm is sensitive to the initial parameter values and may suffer from frequent collisions in crowded environments, but it can adapt to different tasks and positions within the team.

Título: Rule-Based Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Robot Navigation With Space Reduction
Tarea: autonomous robot navigation in complex environments.
Algoritmo (texto): Rule-based Reinforcement Learning (RuRL), combining Q-learning with wall-following and reduction rules.
Observaciones: the agent observes the environment to generate a closed-loop trajectory and navigate through it.
Acciones: discrete actions (wall-following, exploration strategies)
Recompensa: not stated explicitly, but related to the navigation performance and path length.
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: traditional rule-based methods; recent reinforcement learning methods
Resultado: RuRL can achieve improved navigation performance compared to traditional rule-based methods and recent reinforcement learning methods.
Limitaciones: The method relies on the environment model and expert knowledge, and the exploration process can be expensive due to inefﬁcient exploration.

Título: A deep multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for autonomous aerial navigation to grasping points on loads
Tarea: autonomous aerial navigation to grasping points on loads, both targeted and flexible navigation.
Algoritmo (texto): multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) with an attention mechanism, behavior cloning, and demonstration-based methods.
Observaciones: position, velocity, and life of neighboring UAVs and grasping points
Acciones: continuous actions for navigation and manipulation
Recompensa: defined as the distance travelled and the time spent, with a focus on maintaining a positive reward level
Entrenamiento: 1500, 2000, and 3500 episodes for loads with three, four, and six grasping points respectively, with a learning rate of 10^-4 for the actor and 10^-3 for the critic, and a discount factor of 0.95
Métricas: finished time; average speed; position deviation; success rate; total reward
Líneas base: MADDPG; MAPPO; behavioral swarm optimization (BSO); classical methods
Resultado: The average tracking deviations from the desirable grasping point to the final position of the UAV can be less than 10 cm in some real-world experiments, and the proposed methods outperform other baselines with a reasonable success rate especially in the scenarios with more grasping points.
Limitaciones: The performance of partial observation is inferior to that of full observation due to the policy’s inability to receive sufficient information for decision-making in the multi-agent system.

Título: Identifying important sensory feedback for learning locomotion skills
Tarea: learning locomotion skills such as balance recovery, trotting, bounding, pacing, and galloping
Algoritmo (texto): Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with integrated gradients for saliency analysis
Observaciones: joint positions, gravity vector, base linear and angular velocities
Acciones: discrete (joint positions, joint velocities, joint torques, foot positions, foot contacts)
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: sτ; sr; sf; shN; sϕN; sτ; sv; sψ; sh; sϕ
Líneas base: full-state policies
Resultado: learning locomotion skills with only key feedback states achieves comparable performance to using all available states, and the performance metrics for key states are evaluated to be more energy-efficient
Limitaciones: the study focuses on quadruped robots and the key states identified may not be generalizable to other types of robots

Título: Imitating and Finetuning Model Predictive Control for Robust and Symmetric Quadrupedal Locomotion
Tarea: Robust and symmetric quadrupedal locomotion
Algoritmo (texto): Imitating and Finetuning Model Predictive Control (IFM), combining Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP) and Raibert heuristics with imitation learning and deep reinforcement learning (DRL)
Observaciones: Observations include command vector, gait sequence, stance leg control, swing leg control, and torque
Acciones: Discrete actions (torque commands) for stance and swing legs
Recompensa: Defined through a combination of simple reward and contact reward, with a focus on tracking velocity commands and robustness
Entrenamiento: Training budget not explicitly stated, but involves multiple stages of imitation learning and reinforcement learning
Métricas: Survival time; Tracking error (linear and angular); Cost of Transportation (CoT); Phase-Portrait Index (PPI)
Líneas base: MPC; DAgger; Vanilla RL (Simple Reward, Contact Reward); Concurrent RL
Sim2real: Domain randomization and terrain curriculum used to transfer learning from simulation to real hardware
Resultado: IFM policies outperform other methods in terms of robustness, tracking error, and motion quality, with a minimal burden of reward shaping, achieving a 90% success rate on challenging terrains and significantly reducing computation time compared to MPC
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that Vanilla RL policies often require task-specific reward shaping, which can be challenging, and that IFM still benefits from domain randomization and terrain curriculum for better transferability

Título: Learning-Based Safe Control for Robot and Autonomous Vehicle Using Efficient Safety Certificate
Tarea: Learning a safe control policy and an efficient energy function for autonomous vehicles and robots.
Algoritmo (texto): SafeMR, which is a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm.
Observaciones: The agent observes the system state, specifically the distance to obstacles and the derivative of the distance with respect to time.
Acciones: Continuous, as the energy function is adjusted by parameters that can vary continuously (σ, k, n).
Recompensa: The reward is defined by the energy function, which should be low for safe states and high for hazardous states, ensuring the system remains in a low energy state and dissipates energy rapidly when the energy state is high.
Entrenamiento: Not explicitly stated, but the authors mention that they conducted experiments on Safety Gym and SUMO.
Líneas base: Constrained reinforcement learning (CRL) methods; Energy functions that only consider feasibility
Resultado: The proposed magnitude regularization method effectively improves the efficiency of the policy while ensuring safety, outperforming the baseline in terms of controller efficiency for the robot.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that few studies have discussed the efficiency of synthetic energy functions, and that the design of the energy function affects both efficiency and policy performance.

Título: Learning Complex Motor Skills for Legged Robot Fall Recovery
Tarea: learn generalized feedback-control policies for fall recovery of legged robots
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor Critic (SAC) with a neural network policy
Robot: Valkyrie; Spotmicro; Sigmaban; A1; B1; Jueying Pro
Observaciones: gravity vector, base angular velocity, base linear velocity, joint position, joint velocity, limb extremity position
Acciones: continuous, 25 Hz position references for all joints, 500 Hz joint torques
Recompensa: defined by multiple terms including base pose, base height, base velocity, joint torque regularization, joint velocity regularization, body-ground contact, upper torso pose, head height, left and right foot placement
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: classical and RL
Resultado: The proposed framework successfully learned fall recovery policies that are responsive and robust to changes in friction, external pushes, and irregular terrains, and was validated on a real quadruped robot.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method relies on explicit specification of contacts, either manually or automatically, and requires advanced optimization schemes, in which computational power and time grow exponentially when complexity scales up, being too slow for real-time solutions and making closed-loop control impractical for robot fall recovery.

Título: Overcoming Exploration: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Control in Cluttered Environments From Temporal Logic Specifications
Tarea: navigation tasks in cluttered environments, specified using Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) formulas.
Algoritmo (texto): Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) with a novel exploration guidance technique using geometric RRT* and distributed DPGs.
Observaciones: state vector in the compact set S, control input, and regions of interest labeled by a set of atomic propositions
Acciones: continuous actions, discrete or stochastic
Recompensa: defined using Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) formulas, converted into Non-deterministic Büchi Automata (NBA) and then into a product Büchi automaton (PBA) for path planning
Simulador: Pybullet for the car-like model and a 3D environment with Quadrotor dynamics
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: success rates of task satisfaction; training time
Líneas base: TL-based rewards in [26], [28]; NED (negative Euclidean distance) based reward; G-RRT* (global RRT*)
Resultado: The proposed method significantly improves the success rates of task satisfaction over both infinite and finite horizons in cluttered environments, and significantly reduces training time for the task over finite horizons.
Limitaciones: The method is sensitive to the environments and has poor performances, and when the optimal trajectories become complicated, 'G-RRT*' easily converges to sub-optimal solutions.

Título: Physics-informed reinforcement learning for motion control of a fish-like swimming robot
Tarea: velocity and path tracking for a planar swimming (fish-like) rigid Joukowski hydrofoil
Algoritmo (texto): Deterministic Policy Gradient (DPG) algorithm
Observaciones: velocity and angular position
Acciones: torque, discrete
Recompensa: not stated
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: Chaplygin sleigh
Resultado: A DPG agent was trained to generate the action (torque) to steer the Chaplygin sleigh and track a limit cycle in the velocity space at a specified translational velocity. This DPG agent of the Chaplygin sleigh was then transferred to a fluid simulation for training to steer the hydrofoil and track a speed. This step-by-step curriculum reinforcement learning circumvents the problem of high computational time to simulate the physics of the system and allows a way to imprint qualitative physics into a DPG agent. The results show the utility of physics-informed reinforcement learning for the control of fish-like swimming robots.
Limitaciones: The high computational time to simulate the physics of the system and the need for high-fidelity simulations for the final steps of training.

Título: Safe and Efficient Reinforcement Learning Using Disturbance-Observer-Based Control Barrier Functions
Tarea: The task is to navigate a unicycle and a 2D quadrotor to a target without colliding with obstacles or boundaries, while ensuring safety constraints are satisfied.
Algoritmo (texto): Disturbance-Observer-Based Control Barrier Function (DOB-CBF) with Quadratic Programming (QP) for safe reinforcement learning (RL).
Observaciones: State variables (position, velocity, angle, angular velocity) and uncertainty estimation.
Acciones: Continuous control inputs (linear velocity, angular velocity, thrust force) for the robots.
Recompensa: The reward is defined by the navigation performance and safety constraints, with a focus on minimizing safety violations and maximizing the episode return.
Simulador: Simulated environments for both unicycle and 2D quadrotor.
Entrenamiento: Training was performed on a desktop with an INTEL i9-9980XE and an NVIDIA 3090Ti GPU and 64GB RAM. The training budget is not explicitly stated in terms of steps or episodes, but it is mentioned that 200 episodes were used for the unicycle and 5000 episodes for the 2D quadrotor.
Métricas: Average Episode Return; Safety violation rate
Líneas base: GP-CBF-RL (Gaussian process-based CBF-RL)
Resultado: The DOB-CBF-RL method outperforms the GP-CBF-RL method in terms of safety violation rate and sample efficiency, achieving zero safety violations during training and significantly reducing the number of episodes required for convergence.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the intuitively selected function h may not be a DOB-CBF in the presence of uncertainties and control limits, which could lead to a loss of the rigorous safety guarantee provided by the framework.

Título: Collision Avoidance and Navigation for a Quadrotor Swarm Using End-to-end Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: collision avoidance and navigation for quadrotor swarms in obstacle-rich environments
Algoritmo (texto): asynchronous decentralized, independent proximal policy optimization (PPO)
Observaciones: local observations of its own state and goal, observation of the neighbor robots, and obstacle observations based on signed distance field (SDF)
Acciones: rotor thrusts, corresponding to the thrust levels at each of the four rotors, discrete
Recompensa: reward function consists of three main components: distance to goal, collision avoidance, and control effort
Entrenamiento: 400 million environment steps, 4 different seeds
Métricas: success rate; collision rate; distance to goal; flight distance; inference time
Líneas base: two state-of-the-art baselines
Sim2real: attention mechanism transferred from simulation to real quadrotors
Resultado: Our approach achieves a success rate of 0.95, a collision rate of 0.02, and a distance to goal of 0.15m, with 8 robots in a 10m × 10m × 10m room with 20% obstacle density and 0.6m obstacle size.
Limitaciones: The approach requires a large number of environment steps for training and may not perform well in more complex environments.

Título: D-VAT: End-to-End Visual Active Tracking for Micro Aerial Vehicles
Tarea: control the motion of a tracker agent to maintain the target within the FoV of the camera and at a predefined distance.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with an asymmetric actor-critic formulation
Observaciones: RGB images from a monocular camera
Acciones: thrust and angular velocity commands, continuous
Recompensa: defined as a combination of terms that encourage keeping the target in the center of the camera FoV, penalizing velocity and control effort, and avoiding collisions
Entrenamiento: 18,000 episodes in 6 parallel environments, on a workstation with 2 × NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti GPUs, Intel Core i7-9800X CPU, and 64 GB of RAM
Líneas base: model-based and data-driven SotA approaches
Resultado: D-V AT outperforms different SotA baselines in simulated environments that differ substantially from those encountered during training, achieving a much better tracking performance.
Limitaciones: The authors acknowledge that the method is trained in a model-free manner and has no explicit information about the dynamics of the system, which may limit its performance.

Título: Diffusion Policies for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Offline Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: learn robust policies from offline RL datasets, particularly focusing on out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization.
Algoritmo (texto): State Reconstruction for Diffusion Policies (SRDP), which incorporates state reconstruction feature learning in diffusion policies.
Observaciones: state and action coordinates in a 2D space
Acciones: continuous actions in a 2D space, discrete in the robot experiment
Recompensa: not stated
Simulador: 2D Multimodal Contextual Bandit environment, real UR10 robot
Entrenamiento: not stated
Líneas base: BC-Diffusion; Diffusion-QL
Resultado: SRDP achieved 167% improvement over the competing baseline on a sparse continuous control navigation task where various regions of the state space are removed from the offline RL dataset, including the region encapsulating the goal.
Limitaciones: The method is computationally expensive to train as it needs careful tuning of hyperparameters, and validation and hyperparameter optimization in offline RL remains an open area of research.

Título: Enhanced method for reinforcement learning based dynamic obstacle avoidance by assessment of collision risk
Tarea: dynamic obstacle avoidance for mobile robots, autonomous ships, and drones.
Algoritmo (texto): reinforcement learning (RL) with two metrics: collision risk metric and number of obstacles.
Observaciones: position, velocity, and heading angle of the agent and obstacles.
Acciones: discrete actions (torque and acceleration) for the agent.
Recompensa: negative reward for overlapping with obstacles, positive reward for avoiding obstacles.
Simulador: custom training environment with adjustable collision risk and number of obstacles.
Entrenamiento: 21 different agents trained with various collision risk distributions and obstacle ratios, 2x10^7 steps of training.
Líneas base: traditional training environment based on random initialization of agent and obstacles and longer training episodes
Resultado: The final performance increases with a higher percentage of high collision risk scenarios and more obstacles. Training with only high collision risks leads to unsatisfactory performance.
Limitaciones: The RL agent lacks generalization abilities when just being trained with a small interval of different collision risks.

Título: Enhancing efficiency and propulsion in bio-mimetic robotic fish through end-to-end deep reinforcement learning
Tarea: Optimizar el movimiento de un pez robótico bio-mimético para maximizar la eficiencia de la propulsión y minimizar el consumo de energía.
Algoritmo (texto): Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) con un proceso de decisión de Markov (MDP)
Observaciones: Ángulos de las articulaciones, velocidades angulares, posición y presión del flujo en 13 puntos
Acciones: Rotaciones de los enlaces y movimiento en la dirección y, acciones discretas
Recompensa: Función de recompensa compuesta que considera el coeficiente de empuje, el coeficiente de fuerza lateral, el coeficiente de consumo de potencia y la eficiencia de la propulsión
Simulador: Solver CFD con el método de inmersión de datos de borde (BDIM)
Entrenamiento: No se especifica un presupuesto de entrenamiento específico, pero se menciona la implementación de un pipeline de entrenamiento
Métricas: Coeficiente de empuje; Coeficiente de fuerza lateral; Coeficiente de consumo de potencia; Eficiencia de la propulsión
Líneas base: Control trigonométrico predefinido
Resultado: El algoritmo PPO optimizado logró una eficiencia de propulsión del 95.5% y un consumo de energía del 85.5% en comparación con el control trigonométrico predefinido, demostrando un aumento significativo en la eficiencia y la eficacia de la propulsión.
Limitaciones: Se menciona que el algoritmo podría no ser tan eficiente en entornos con estados incompletos o ruidosos, pero no se especifican más limitaciones.

Título: Graph Neural Network-based Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Distributed Coordination of Multi-Robot Systems
Tarea: multi-robot patrolling
Algoritmo (texto): multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) with a custom k-convolution GNN as the actor
Observaciones: graph-based observation, state of all vertices and agents within some radius r
Acciones: discrete, representing an edge connected to the agent’s current node
Recompensa: described as the reward to each agent for a particular system state, with metrics such as average idleness time and worst node idleness time
Entrenamiento: not stated
Métricas: average idleness time; worst node idleness time
Líneas base: GBS; SEBS; CBLS; DTA-Greedy; DTAP; LR; AHPA
Resultado: MAGEC outperforms existing methods in several experiments involving agent attrition and communication disturbance, and provides competitive results in scenarios without such anomalies
Limitaciones: not stated

Título: Learning agility and adaptive legged locomotion via curricular hindsight reinforcement learning
Tarea: Learn an end-to-end tracking controller for agile and adaptive legged locomotion, including fall recovery, high-speed turning, and sprinting.
Algoritmo (texto): Curricular Hindsight Reinforcement Learning (CHRL), which combines an MLP teacher policy and a student policy trained via imitation learning.
Observaciones: Joint angles, joint velocities, IMU orientation and angular velocities, and robot state including body velocity, foot contact, relative position, friction coefficient, and payload mass.
Acciones: 12-dimensional desired joint position vector, discrete
Recompensa: Encourages forward movement and penalizes jerky and inefficient motions, with specific penalties for velocity, orientation, joint torques, base acceleration, energy, and foot slip.
Entrenamiento: 6 million simulated time steps, 6 hours on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU
Métricas: Linear Velocity; Orientation Tracking; Height Constraint; Angle Velocity Penalties; Self-collision Penalties; Joint Torque Penalties; Base Acceleration Penalties; Energy; Foot Slip
Líneas base: previous work on fast running, uneven terrain locomotion, and mountain climbing
Sim2real: Domain randomization and automatic curriculum strategy
Resultado: The robot achieved a maximum outdoor running speed of 3.45 m/s and tuning speeds up to 3.2 rad/s, successfully performing fall recovery, coherent trotting, and adapting to changing terrains.
Limitaciones: The method relies on domain randomization and a fixed set of curriculum parameters, which may limit its generalizability to highly variable environments.

Título: PathRL: An End-to-End Path Generation Method for Collision Avoidance via Deep Reinforcement Learning
Tarea: Robot navigation using deep reinforcement learning to generate paths for collision avoidance.
Algoritmo (texto): Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm
Observaciones: Egocentric costmap and relative target pose
Acciones: Discrete control points for Bézier curve path generation
Recompensa: Smooth transition between adjacent paths, not stated explicitly
Entrenamiento: Not stated
Resultado: PathRL achieves better success rates and reduces angular rotation variability compared to other DRL navigation methods, facilitating stable and smooth robot movement.
Limitaciones: Training a navigation policy that outputs paths is challenging due to the higher-dimensional policy space and the need to predict interactions in multiple time steps.

Título: RL2AC: Reinforcement Learning-based Rapid Online Adaptive Control for Legged Robot Robust Locomotion
Tarea: Robust locomotion control for quadruped robots in various terrains and tasks.
Algoritmo (texto): RL2AC, which combines RL policy and adaptive control.
Observaciones: Proprioceptive observation, body velocity, joint positions, joint velocities, previous actions, privileged observations including disturbance force and height map.
Acciones: 12 joint position commands, discrete.
Recompensa: Reward function encourages linear velocity tracking, angular velocity tracking, z velocity, roll-pitch velocity, orientation, joint accelerations, joint power, body height, foot clearance, action rate, action smoothing, and power distribution.
Entrenamiento: Training on a laptop with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 GPU and Intel Core i7-12700H CPU, 50Hz for value network, 1000Hz for policy network.
Métricas: Linear velocity tracking; Angular velocity tracking; Z velocity; Roll-pitch velocity; Orientation; Joint accelerations; Joint power; Body height; Foot clearance; Action rate; Action smoothing; Power distribution
Líneas base: MPC-WBC; PD controller
Resultado: The proposed RL2AC achieved robust locomotion control in various terrains and tasks, with the quadruped robot performing similarly to the case without model uncertainties.
Limitaciones: The method relies on domain randomization during training, which may limit its generalization to unseen environments.

Título: Reinforcement Learning for Reduced-order Models of Legged Robots
Tarea: learn a reduced-order model (ROM) for legged locomotion within a model predictive control (MPC) framework to improve performance and task flexibility.
Algoritmo (texto): Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolutionary Strategy (CMA-ES) for reinforcement learning, with a model-based approach using a ROM planner as the policy.
Algoritmo (diccionario): Estrategias evolutivas (ES); CEM / CMA-ES; Híbridos evolutivos + RL
Observaciones: robot's state and input (x, u), task γ, and finite state machine information
Acciones: CoM states and foot step locations, discrete
Recompensa: reward function that encourages minimizing the cost and achieving a desired task, with a focus on motor torque cost and task completion
Entrenamiento: 1000 iterations, not stated hardware
Líneas base: initial model (LIP); optimal model from prior work
Resultado: 49% improvement in viable task region size and 21% reduction in motor torque cost compared to the initial model (LIP), and up to 28% increase in task space compared to the prior work.
Limitaciones: learning a policy for a large task space is difficult, so a curriculum learning approach is implemented to facilitate the learning process.

Título: Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion via Risk-Averse Policy Learning
Tarea: Robust locomotion control for quadrupedal robots in challenging terrains.
Algoritmo (texto): Risk-Averse Legged Locomotion (RALL) using a distributional value function and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization.
Observaciones: Base linear velocity, base angular velocity, gravity vector, velocity command, joint angle, joint velocity, and last action.
Acciones: Target joint position, with discrete actions via a PD controller.
Recompensa: Reward function penalizes certain state components exceeding predefined thresholds, with a very small probability of applying a large penalty.
Entrenamiento: 6000 iterations, approximately 7 hours, on a PC with 32-core Intel i9-13900K CPU, 128GB RAM, and NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU.
Métricas: Time to Fall (TTF); Success rates of robot walking down a platform
Líneas base: Baseline (PPO with curriculum terrain setting); Expanded Domain Randomization (DR); RMA (Risk Modeling and Adaptation)
Resultado: Our method outperforms others by making the robot survive for the longest duration under each setting, with significantly higher success rates in handling hazardous terrains.
Limitaciones: The method only utilizes proprioception to identify risks, and future work plans to incorporate external sensors.

Título: SLR: Learning Quadruped Locomotion without Privileged Information
Tarea: training a robust quadruped locomotion policy without relying on privileged information
Algoritmo (texto): Self-learning Latent Representation (SLR) algorithm, based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
Robot: Unitree Go1, Unitree Go2, Unitree A1, Unitree Aliengo robots
Observaciones: 45 dimensions including base angular velocity, commands from joystick, gravity vector, joint positions and velocities, and actions from the previous time step
Acciones: 12-dimensional vector corresponding to the four legs of the quadruped robot, with each leg having three motor drive units
Recompensa: defined in Table A1, coming from [10, 16, 23]; domain randomizations used for training
Entrenamiento: 6000 iterations, using three different random seeds
Métricas: Linear Velocity Tracking Error (LVTE); Angular Velocity Tracking Error (AVTE)
Líneas base: MoB; RLvRL; ROA; HIM; Baseline
Resultado: The SLR algorithm outperforms traditional privileged learning methods, achieving mean rewards comparable to the recently released top-performing HIM algorithm but with a higher terrain level, indicating superior performance. The SLR algorithm demonstrates enhanced tracking capabilities across various velocity ranges.
Limitaciones: The blind policy demonstrates robust motion, but achieving superior trajectory planning necessitates the use of vision sensors. The authors acknowledge that the current approach relies solely on proprioceptive data.
